reasoning: REQ-0000 is an architectural scaffolding requirement with no unique interface-observable obligation. A smoke scenario therefore verifies that the named module can operate in the bit-level-controller role through its public I2C control and bus interfaces.; Cover the supported command path with separate timed-sequence scenarios for START, STOP, WRITE, and READ, including both WRITE data values because the SDA sequence differs. Add a contrasting unsupported-command scenario in which the command-specific sequence is absent and no acknowledgement occurs.; The requirement is broad and is observed through command completion, status, read-data, and output-enable behavior. The plan uses separate supported and contrasting unsupported/no-event scenarios, plus corner scenarios for arbitration, stretching, synchronization, and filtering. All references are pinned to REQ-0002 revision 1.; REQ-0003 is the only requirement declaring needs=["testplan"]. The plan contrasts active-low drive and release phases for both SCL and SDA, while checking that scl_o and sda_o remain constant low in every phase. Each element identifies the holding side of the observed port behavior and treats the alternative side as a failure.; The requirement is observed through four output ports. The plan contrasts drive phases, where each active-low enable is low and the corresponding bus line is pulled low, with release phases, where each enable is high and the external pull-up allows the line high. A separate scenario checks that scl_o and sda_o remain constant low throughout operation.; REQ-0005 is observed through the output-enable behavior exercised by supported command sequences. Two contrasting scenarios are provided: one drives the I2C lines low with active-low enables, and one releases them high so the external pull-up determines the line level.; REQ-0006 is a scaffolding requirement with no behavioral interface observable that can distinguish architectural correspondence. elements.stimulus: Instantiate i2c_master_bit_ctrl with its specified ports, apply reset, then drive ena=1, a valid START command followed by a WRITE command, clk_cnt=1, din=1, and an externally released-high I2C bus.
elements.expected_response: The module operates as a bit-level I2C controller: it remains idle after reset with both output-enable signals released, accepts the commands on timing ticks, generates the START and WRITE bit phases through scl_oen and sda_oen, and produces command-complete pulses without unsupported interface behavior.
elements.check_method: Run an integration smoke test against the exact module port list; compare registered outputs and command sequencing with a cycle-accurate bit-level I2C reference model, sampling after each posedge clk and checking reset values, phase ordering, and cmd_ack pulse behavior.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive cmd=START (0001) while the bus is released high, and keep cmd stable until cmd_ack is observed. Allow each enabled timing tick to occur without clock stretching.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: from command acceptance through cmd_ack, scl_oen and sda_oen implement the START sequence: both lines initially release, SDA is driven low while SCL remains released/high, then SCL is driven low, and exactly one cmd_ack pulse is generated at completion.
elements.check_method: Use a transaction monitor sampled after each posedge to compare scl_oen and sda_oen against the reference START phase sequence and verify cmd_ack is a single-cycle pulse after the terminal phase.

elements.stimulus: After establishing a busy transaction, set ena=1 and drive cmd=STOP (0010) while the bus is otherwise released. Keep cmd stable until cmd_ack is observed.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: scl_oen and sda_oen implement the timed STOP sequence: SDA is driven low, SCL is released and allowed to be high, SDA is then released while SCL is high, and exactly one cmd_ack pulse is generated at completion.
elements.check_method: Capture the registered output-enable values on every posedge and match their ordered phases to the STOP reference model; assert that the final phase is followed by one and only one cmd_ack cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=0 on a released-high bus, and retain the command until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: sda_oen drives SDA low for the zero data bit, scl_oen releases SCL for the timed high phase and then drives SCL low, followed by one cmd_ack pulse; the output-enable sequence completes without arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Compare the sampled scl_oen and sda_oen sequence and phase ordering with the WRITE reference model for din=0, and check cmd_ack occurs once at the terminal phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1 on a released-high bus, keep SDA externally high during the released high phase, and retain the command until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: sda_oen releases SDA for the one data bit, scl_oen releases SCL for the timed high phase and then drives SCL low, followed by one cmd_ack pulse with no arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Match scl_oen and sda_oen against the WRITE din=1 reference sequence, verify SDA remains released during the high phase, and check the single completion acknowledgement.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive cmd=READ (1000); provide a released-high bus and return a stable external SDA value of 0 during the read window. Keep the command active until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: sda_oen remains released for the READ data window, scl_oen releases SCL for the timed read-high phase, then drives SCL low, and one cmd_ack pulse follows the low phase.
elements.check_method: Use a timing-aware reference model keyed to clk_en and filtered SCL edges to compare the ordered scl_oen/sda_oen phases and verify cmd_ack follows completion rather than occurring at command acceptance.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive cmd=NOP (0000), then each unsupported 4-bit command value other than 0001, 0010, 0100, and 1000, while the bus is released high. Hold each value for at least the maximum normal command duration.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise case of shows: scl_oen and sda_oen do not exhibit any command-specific timed SCL or SDA sequence; both remain in the idle released state, and cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: For each command value, monitor the output enables over the observation window and assert they remain at idle release without phase transitions or command acknowledgement.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive a released-high bus, issue cmd=START on an enabled timing tick, then hold cmd=NOP until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the DUT generates the START sequence by releasing SCL, driving SDA low while SCL is high, then driving SCL low; cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock at terminal completion, and busy becomes asserted when the filtered START is detected.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to compare scl_oen and sda_oen phase ordering, require exactly one cmd_ack pulse, and sample busy after filtered START detection.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and the bus released high, issue cmd=NOP and each unsupported 4-bit command encoding while idle, one command at a time.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: no supported command cycle is generated; scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the idle released state, cmd_ack remains low, and busy and al do not change solely because of these commands.
elements.check_method: Decode every command response against the reference model and assert no output-enable phase transition, no cmd_ack pulse, and no status change during each unsupported-command interval.

elements.stimulus: With busy asserted from a prior transaction, set ena=1, issue cmd=STOP on an enabled timing tick, and keep the external bus released unless the DUT drives it.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the DUT drives SDA low, releases SCL and waits for filtered SCL high, then releases SDA while SCL is high; cmd_ack pulses once at completion and busy clears when the filtered STOP is detected.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed scl_oen/sda_oen sequence and variable completion timing with a protocol reference model; check one-cycle cmd_ack and busy deassertion at the filtered STOP event.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a released-high bus, issue a WRITE command with din=0; allow the external bus to remain high whenever the DUT releases it.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: sda_oen drives SDA low for the data bit, releases SCL for the high phase, then drives SCL low; the command completes with one cmd_ack pulse, and al remains deasserted.
elements.check_method: Check active-low output-enable polarity and phase ordering against the reference model, require completion after the configured timing/filter delays, and assert no al or extra cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, issue a WRITE command with din=1; during the released-high WRITE phase, externally drive SDA low while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for arbitration-loss behavior: al asserts, the active command aborts without cmd_ack, and both scl_oen and sda_oen are released. al remains asserted until reset.
elements.check_method: Use the write high-phase probe and filtered SDA value to identify the arbitration check; assert sticky al, absence of cmd_ack, immediate return to idle, and released output enables.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, issue a READ command, first drive filtered SDA high at the READ filtered SCL rising edge, then repeat the transaction with filtered SDA low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: SDA remains released during READ, SCL is released for the read window and then driven low, dout captures 1 in the first transaction and 0 in the second at the filtered SCL rising edge, and each transaction produces one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Run two independent transactions against a filtered-bus reference model; compare dout at the rising-edge event, output-enable phases, and one-cycle completion pulses.

elements.stimulus: Leave the DUT idle with ena=1, keep SCL and SDA filtered high without issuing READ or any supported command, and toggle raw SDA without creating a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: dout is not updated by a READ capture; cmd_ack remains low and output enables remain in the idle released state.
elements.check_method: Record dout before and after the interval and assert it changes only at a filtered SCL rising edge during an active READ sequence; also check no command-completion pulse or command output sequence.

elements.stimulus: Issue a WRITE or READ with ena=1 while the DUT releases SCL, then hold scl_i low externally for multiple timing ticks before releasing it high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: slave clock stretching pauses the timing counter and active FSM phase; scl_oen remains released but the high-phase command does not advance, and completion is delayed until filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.check_method: Monitor slave_wait_active, cnt_nonzero, clk_en_tick, FSM phase probes, scl_oen, and cmd_ack; compare the stall and subsequent completion against a stretching-aware reference model.

elements.stimulus: During a released-SCL high phase, force an external filtered SCL falling edge while the local master has not requested SCL low, then allow SCL to return high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the DUT recognizes multi-master clock synchronization, reloads or resynchronizes its timing interval, and does not advance the high-phase FSM state until filtered SCL is high; the command later completes with its normal cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Correlate scl_sync_event with counter reload, clk_en_tick suppression, output-enable stability, and eventual phase progression using a cycle-accurate reference model.

elements.stimulus: With the bus initially filtered high, inject SDA and SCL raw pulses shorter than the filter sampling interval while ena=1; do not issue an active command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: synchronization and glitch filtering reject the short disturbances; no filtered START or STOP is detected, busy does not change, al remains deasserted, and no command output sequence or cmd_ack occurs.
elements.check_method: Compare raw input pulses with filter_sample_due and filtered transition probes; assert that no start_condition, stop_condition, busy transition, al assertion, or command-completion pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: Drive a stable filtered START-shaped transition by changing SDA from high to low while SCL remains high, then drive a stable STOP-shaped transition by changing SDA from low to high while SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy asserts after the filtered START and clears after the filtered STOP; each status change follows the synchronized, majority-filtered transition rather than the raw input edge.
elements.check_method: Use the synchronizer/filter reference model to predict filtered transitions and compare start_condition, stop_condition, and registered busy timing with the predicted one-clock output latency.

elements.stimulus: Run supported START, STOP, WRITE, and READ commands with clk_cnt values 0, 1, and a larger nonzero value while ena=1 and the external bus responds normally.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: all supported single-bit cycles remain functional at each prescaler boundary; clk_en occurs every enabled clock for clk_cnt=0 without a stuck divider, timing scales for larger values, output-enable phase ordering remains valid, and each completed command produces one cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Parameterize the reference model for each clk_cnt value, check divider/filter progress and variable latency, and assert no missing, repeated, or stuck command completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and provide an externally pulled-up bus. Issue a START command and wait through the command sequence until the controller enters the phase that pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the SCL observation: scl_o remains constant 0 throughout reset and the START sequence; when scl_oen is 0, the external SCL line is driven low. If scl_o is ever 1, the otherwise side applies—the controller could drive SCL high—and the requirement fails.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_o, scl_oen, and the externally resolved SCL line after each posedge through the START sequence. Assert scl_o==0 on every sample, and correlate scl_oen==0 with resolved SCL low using an open-drain bus model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and provide an externally pulled-up bus. Issue a STOP command from an active transaction and wait until the STOP sequence releases SCL.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting SCL control case: scl_o remains constant 0 while scl_oen changes to 1 and the externally pulled-up SCL line becomes high, demonstrating release rather than high-side drive. The holding-side requirement is still checked continuously; any scl_o value other than 0 is the otherwise condition and is a failure.
elements.check_method: Observe scl_o, scl_oen, and resolved SCL after each posedge. Assert scl_o==0; during the release phase assert scl_oen==1 and resolved SCL==1 with no external SCL-low drive.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and provide an externally pulled-up bus. Issue a START command and observe the initial released SDA phase followed by the phase that pulls SDA low while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the SDA observation: sda_o remains constant 0 throughout reset and the START sequence; when sda_oen is 0, the external SDA line is driven low. If sda_o is ever 1, the otherwise side applies—the controller could drive SDA high—and the requirement fails.
elements.check_method: Sample sda_o, sda_oen, and the externally resolved SDA line after each posedge through the START sequence. Assert sda_o==0 on every sample, and correlate sda_oen==0 with resolved SDA low using an open-drain bus model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and provide an externally pulled-up bus. Issue a STOP command from an active transaction and wait through the phase that releases SDA while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting SDA control case: sda_o remains constant 0 while sda_oen changes to 1 and the externally pulled-up SDA line becomes high, demonstrating release rather than high-side drive. The holding-side requirement is still checked continuously; any sda_o value other than 0 is the otherwise condition and is a failure.
elements.check_method: Observe sda_o, sda_oen, and resolved SDA after each posedge. Assert sda_o==0; during the release phase assert sda_oen==1 and resolved SDA==1 with no external SDA-low drive.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, deassert it, then operate the controller with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, a released-high external bus, and issue START, STOP, WRITE with din=0 and READ commands while allowing each command to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_o and sda_o remain continuously 0 throughout reset release and every command phase, regardless of scl_oen, sda_oen, or the externally observed bus levels.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_o and sda_o after every reset and posedge clk for the complete command sequences; compare against constant 0 and flag any transition to 1.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and both external lines initially released high, issue START and then STOP. Model the open-drain bus so a low output enable pulls the corresponding line low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting drive side of shows: during START and STOP phases that drive SCL or SDA low, the corresponding scl_oen or sda_oen is 0 and the corresponding bus line is low; scl_o and sda_o remain 0. During phases not driving that line, its enable is not required to be low.
elements.check_method: Use the FSM phase probes and sampled output enables to identify each SCL/SDA drive phase; assert enable=0 and modeled bus=0 for the driven line, while independently asserting scl_o=0 and sda_o=0.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and both external lines initially released high, issue START, WRITE with din=1, and READ commands; allow the controller to reach each command's released-line phase while the external participant leaves the corresponding line undriven.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting release side of shows: during every SCL release phase scl_oen is 1 and the externally modeled SCL line is high when no participant drives it; during every SDA release phase sda_oen is 1 and the externally modeled SDA line is high when no participant drives it. scl_o and sda_o remain 0 throughout.
elements.check_method: Identify release phases using the command and phase probes, compare scl_oen/sda_oen against 1, and compare the open-drain bus model against high with external drive disabled; also assert constant-low scl_o and sda_o.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. Issue a WRITE command with din=0, allowing the command to progress through its normal bit phases.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-low phase, sda_oen is 0 and the resolved SDA line is low, which is the low/driven side of the observed behavior. During the released SCL high phase, scl_oen is 1 and the resolved SCL line is high from the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: At each registered output update, correlate the WRITE phase probe with sda_oen and scl_oen and compare the resolved bus lines against an open-drain model: enable 0 forces low and enable 1 permits the externally pulled-up high level.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. Issue a READ command and allow it to enter its read window with the external participant not pulling SDA or SCL low.
elements.expected_response: During the READ released-line window, sda_oen is 1 and scl_oen is 1, so both corresponding I2C lines resolve high through the external pull-up; this is the release/high side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: While the READ sequence and released-line phase probes are active, sample the registered output enables and resolved bus levels, checking that enable 1 releases each line and that the open-drain bus model produces high when no external device drives low.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate an integration wrapper that instantiates the exact module `i2c_master_bit_ctrl` as the overall architecture's Bit Command Controller, with the specified clock, reset, command, bus, status, and probe connections.
elements.expected_response: Compilation and elaboration succeed with `i2c_master_bit_ctrl` bound at the Bit Command Controller instance; no alternate module, missing port, unexpected parameter, or unresolved connection is reported.
elements.check_method: Run the HDL compiler and elaborator, then inspect the elaborated hierarchy and instance binding to confirm the Bit Command Controller slot resolves to `i2c_master_bit_ctrl` with the contract-defined interface.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then issue cmd=START while idle. Continue clocking until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: scl_o remains 0 and sda_o remains 0 throughout. During the START sequence, scl_oen remains 1 while SCL is released, sda_oen changes to 0 to drive SDA low while SCL is released, then scl_oen changes to 0 to drive SCL low; output-enable changes are visible after their registered clock update.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model at posedge clk to compare scl_o, sda_o, scl_oen, and sda_oen through each START phase, allowing the specified one-cycle registered output latency and checking the observed phase ordering.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish a busy transaction state, then issue cmd=STOP with scl_i=1 and sda_i=0. Continue clocking until command completion.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: scl_o and sda_o remain 0. The STOP sequence drives SDA low with sda_oen=0, releases SCL with scl_oen=1 and waits for SCL high, then releases SDA with sda_oen=1 while SCL is high; each output-enable transition appears after the corresponding registered update.
elements.check_method: Compare the sampled output-enable waveforms against a STOP-command reference model at every posedge clk, verifying drive/release polarity, phase ordering, and registered visibility; independently assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 in every cycle.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold the bus released-high, issue cmd=WRITE with din=0, and provide no external SDA or SCL contention until completion.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: scl_o and sda_o remain 0. During WRITE, sda_oen is 0 when the data bit is driven low, scl_oen transitions to 1 for the released SCL high phase, and scl_oen returns to 0 for the SCL low phase; the output-enable sequence directly follows the commanded write phases.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model synchronized to clk_en and registered output updates to compare scl_oen and sda_oen over the complete WRITE operation, and check that the external open-drain line model observes the expected SCL/SDA levels.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then drive cmd=NOP for multiple enabled clock ticks followed by an unsupported cmd=0011 while the FSM is idle.
elements.expected_response: CONTRASTING CASE: no supported command is accepted, so scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the released idle state at 1 and no commanded SCL or SDA phase sequence occurs; scl_o and sda_o remain 0. This is the 'otherwise' side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk after reset settles, compare all four ports with the idle/no-op reference model, checking that output enables never enter a drive phase and that no transient command sequence occurs for either cmd value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena high and issue the supported START command while external SCL and SDA are released high; continue clocking until command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the requirement: during START execution, scl_oen remains released for the high window, sda_oen drives SDA low while SCL is released, and scl_oen subsequently drives SCL low for the required low phase.
elements.check_method: At each posedge, compare scl_oen and sda_oen against a reference START phase model and verify the observed sequence is entered only after the START command is accepted.

elements.stimulus: After establishing an active bus transaction, set ena high and issue the supported STOP command; provide released-high SCL when the STOP sequence reaches its high phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the requirement: during STOP execution, sda_oen first drives SDA low, scl_oen is released so SCL can become high, and sda_oen is released only after SCL is high for STOP completion.
elements.check_method: Trace scl_oen and sda_oen on every posedge and compare their ordering with the reference STOP sequence, checking that SDA release occurs after SCL release and observed SCL high.

elements.stimulus: Set ena high, issue the supported READ command on a released-high bus, return a defined external SDA bit during the released SCL high window, and continue until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the requirement: during READ execution, sda_oen remains released for the external bit, scl_oen is released for the read high window, and scl_oen subsequently drives SCL low for the required low phase.
elements.check_method: Compare the sampled scl_oen and sda_oen waveform with the reference READ phase model, including the release-to-low SCL ordering around the filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: Set ena high and issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 on a released-high bus; continue clocking through the complete bit transfer.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the requirement: during WRITE execution, sda_oen drives SDA low for din=0, scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase, and scl_oen drives SCL low for the following low phase.
elements.check_method: Compare registered scl_oen and sda_oen values at each timing tick with the reference WRITE(din=0) model and verify the expected low/high/low phase ordering.

elements.stimulus: Set ena high and issue a supported WRITE command with din=1 on a released-high bus; continue clocking through the complete bit transfer.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the requirement: during WRITE execution, sda_oen releases SDA for din=1, scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase, and scl_oen drives SCL low for the following low phase.
elements.check_method: Compare registered scl_oen and sda_oen values at each timing tick with the reference WRITE(din=1) model and verify SDA enable polarity and phase ordering.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena high and both external lines released high, issue NOP and then an unsupported cmd encoding such as 0011 while remaining idle.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of the requirement: because no supported bit command is active, no START, STOP, READ, or WRITE SDA/SCL sequence is generated; sda_oen and scl_oen remain released high throughout.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen and sda_oen over the command attempts and compare against the idle reference model, requiring no command-specific enable transition and no active command probe interval.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate i2c_master_bit_ctrl using a testbench that connects clk, rst, nReset, ena, and clk_cnt, then inspect the elaborated port declarations.
elements.expected_response: The module elaborates successfully with clk, rst, nReset, and ena declared as 1-bit inputs, and clk_cnt declared as a 16-bit input.
elements.check_method: Use compiler/elaborator diagnostics and VPI or simulator reflection to compare each port's direction and packed width against the required declarations.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate the DUT using the declared interface, then inspect the port declarations for cmd_ack, busy, and al.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack, busy, and al are each present as 1-bit output status signals; cmd remains a 4-bit input command port.
elements.check_method: Use compiler/elaborator metadata or an RTL interface parser to compare each port's name, direction, and width against the required declaration; record a passing structural bin only when all four ports match.

elements.stimulus: Run a negative interface-conformance check against DUT variants in which cmd_ack, busy, or al is declared as an input, omitted, or declared with a width other than 1.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: the interface must be identified as not declaring cmd_ack, busy, or al as the required 1-bit output status signal, and the structural check must fail rather than accepting the variant.
elements.check_method: Compile or inspect each deliberately malformed variant and assert that the interface checker reports the incorrect direction, width, or missing port for every injected defect.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate i2c_master_bit_ctrl with a wrapper that drives din, scl_i, and sda_i from testbench signals and connects dout, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, and sda_oen to testbench observation nets; query the elaborated port metadata.
elements.expected_response: At the module interface, din, scl_i, and sda_i are input ports, and dout, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, and sda_oen are output ports. This is the 'port is declared as an output' side of the requirement for each observed output.
elements.check_method: Use a compile-time interface-direction assertion or VPI/Verilog reflection check on the elaborated DUT port declarations; require exact direction matches and fail on any mismatch or connection-direction diagnostic.

elements.stimulus: Run an interface-contract negative test that inverts the required direction for each observed port, treating dout, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, and sda_oen as inputs and din, scl_i, and sda_i as outputs, and compare this inverted contract against the elaborated i2c_master_bit_ctrl interface.
elements.expected_response: The inverted contract is rejected because dout, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, and sda_oen are declared outputs rather than non-outputs, and din, scl_i, and sda_i are declared inputs rather than outputs. Thus the contrasting 'port is not declared as an output' side of each observed_via condition is not accepted.
elements.check_method: Use a negative compile/elaboration test or direction-reflection assertion that must report a mismatch for every inverted port direction; pass only when all deliberately incorrect direction expectations are rejected.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high and ena high, issue a START command and wait until the registered scl_oen is observed low. Assert rst high while keeping nReset high, then hold rst high without allowing a rising edge of clk.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting case where the clock requirement does not yet hold: scl_oen retains its prior registered low value before a rising edge of clk; it does not reset asynchronously.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen after rst assertion and throughout the interval before the next posedge clk; compare against the value captured immediately before rst assertion and require it to remain unchanged.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high and ena high, issue a START command and wait until the registered scl_oen is observed low. Assert rst high while keeping nReset high, then apply one rising edge of clk.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case where the clock requirement holds: at the rising edge of clk, scl_oen becomes 1, demonstrating that synchronous reset is clocked by clk.
elements.check_method: Capture scl_oen before the rising edge and sample it after nonblocking assignments settle on that edge; require the value to transition from the prior low value to 1 exactly at the posedge.

elements.stimulus: Set nReset high, rst low, ena high, clk_cnt to 0, and both bus lines released high. Issue an enabled START command and run the reference sequence until the command reaches its completion phase. Sample cmd_ack immediately after every rising edge of clk and at points between successive rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0013: cmd_ack asserts as the one-clock completion pulse immediately after the rising edge that completes the START command, remains at that registered value between that edge and the next rising edge, and deasserts only on a later rising edge.
elements.check_method: Use a clocking-block or post-NBA monitor to compare cmd_ack after each posedge and during the intervening interval; require all observed changes in cmd_ack to occur only at posedges, with exactly one clock interval of assertion.

elements.stimulus: While an enabled START command is active and before its completion edge, toggle cmd between valid and unsupported encodings and toggle din and the external bus inputs at times strictly between rising edges of clk. Continue sampling cmd_ack both immediately after each rising edge and throughout each inter-edge interval.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of REQ-0013: between successive rising edges, cmd_ack does not assert, deassert, or otherwise change in response to the between-edge stimulus. Any cmd_ack transition, including the completion assertion or subsequent deassertion, occurs only at a rising edge of clk.
elements.check_method: Timestamp every cmd_ack transition with an event monitor and assert that its timestamp coincides with a clk rising edge; additionally compare cmd_ack before and after each non-edge stimulus event and require equality until the next posedge.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high, initialize the bus released-high, issue a valid WRITE command with ena high, and wait until in_write_sequence is active. Assert rst high between clock edges, then sample outputs before the next posedge and at the next posedge.
elements.expected_response: Before the posedge, synchronous reset has not changed state. On the posedge with rst high, the command FSM returns to idle, scl_oen and sda_oen become high, cmd_ack is low, counters are cleared, and filtered input state is initialized to the released-high condition. This is the reset side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a clocking block to compare pre-edge and post-edge values of scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack; check in_idle, cnt_nonzero, cnt_expired, filtered_scl_high, and filtered_sda_high probes against the reset reference model.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high and rst low. Issue a valid WRITE command with ena high and wait until in_write_sequence is active; keep rst low through a rising edge while the command remains active.
elements.expected_response: The no-reset side of the observation occurs: scl_oen and sda_oen follow the active WRITE phase rather than being forced high, the FSM does not return to idle, and command processing continues. cmd_ack is not cleared by reset and may assert only when the normal command terminal phase is reached.
elements.check_method: At each posedge compare output enables and in_write_sequence/in_idle with the reference model, and verify that no reset transition occurs while rst remains low.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high, establish a filtered START condition by driving SDA from high to low while filtered SCL is high, and wait for busy to become high. Assert rst high before a rising edge of clk and keep it high at that edge.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge with rst high, busy is synchronously cleared low, the command FSM is idle, and both output enables are released high. This is the reset side of the busy observation.
elements.check_method: Detect the filtered START with start_condition, then compare busy, in_idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen immediately after the reset posedge against the reset reference model.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high and rst low after establishing a filtered START condition and observing busy high. Keep the bus busy and sample across subsequent rising edges without asserting rst.
elements.expected_response: The no-reset side of the busy observation occurs: busy remains high while no filtered STOP condition is detected; it is not synchronously cleared merely by a clock edge with rst low.
elements.check_method: Compare busy and stop_condition over multiple posedges with the reference model, requiring busy to remain high until a valid filtered STOP or reset occurs.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high, issue a WRITE with din=1, allow the controller to reach write_stable_high_phase with SDA released, and externally hold SDA low to cause arbitration loss. After al asserts, drive rst high before a rising edge and keep it high at that edge.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge with rst high, the sticky arbitration-loss flag al is synchronously cleared low, the FSM is idle, and scl_oen and sda_oen are high. This is the reset side of the arbitration-loss observation.
elements.check_method: Use write_stable_high_phase and sda_check_active to confirm the loss stimulus, then compare al, in_idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen after the reset posedge with the reference model.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high and rst low. Cause arbitration loss during a WRITE with din=1 by holding SDA low during write_stable_high_phase, then continue clocking without asserting either reset input.
elements.expected_response: The no-reset side of the arbitration-loss observation occurs: al remains asserted on subsequent rising edges, and the controller remains in its post-loss released-line behavior rather than clearing al due to ordinary clocking.
elements.check_method: After detecting arbitration loss, compare al, scl_oen, sda_oen, and in_idle on multiple posedges with rst low; require al to remain high until a reset is applied.

elements.stimulus: Deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 with both bus lines released high, issue a START command, and wait until the registered scl_oen is low during the START sequence. Assert nReset low between two rising edges of clk and keep clk stopped during the observation.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_oen rises to 1 immediately after nReset is asserted low, before the next clk edge, indicating asynchronous initialization of the sequential output state.
elements.check_method: At the instant nReset transitions high-to-low between clock edges, sample scl_oen without advancing clk; require scl_oen==1 before the next posedge. Record a bin for asynchronous reset response.

elements.stimulus: Using the same setup, reach the START sequence with scl_oen low, keep nReset high, hold clk between rising edges, and do not assert any reset input or change command/control inputs during the observation interval.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of shows: scl_oen remains low while nReset stays high between clk edges; it does not asynchronously rise to 1 without a reset assertion or clocked state update.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen for the entire inter-edge interval with nReset==1; require no transition from 0 to 1 before the next posedge. Record a bin for the contrasting non-reset behavior.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to 1, keep the bus released and externally high, assert ena, and issue a supported START command on an enabled timing tick. After the command is accepted and before its terminal phase, drive ena low and hold it low for multiple clocks; then drive ena high again.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-low side of the requirement's shows statement: cmd_ack must not pulse while ena is low, and the active command must not complete because normal timing and command progression are held. After ena returns high, the command resumes and eventually produces one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack on every settled posedge while ena is low and assert it remains 0; use in_start_sequence or command_active to confirm the command remains active. After re-enabling ena, compare the observed command completion and exactly one-cycle cmd_ack pulse against a reference model that resumes timing only when ena is high.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to 1, keep the bus released and externally high, hold ena high throughout, and issue the same supported START command on an enabled timing tick.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-high side of the requirement's shows statement: with ena remaining high, the active command reaches its terminal phase and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack after command acceptance and compare its occurrence with the reference model's completion point; assert that it becomes high once for exactly one settled posedge and then returns low, with no indefinite hold in the active command.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0, then drive ena=0 before the command reaches its terminal completion phase and hold ena=0 for multiple enabled-clock intervals.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for cmd_ack: cmd_ack does not pulse while ena is low; timing progression and the active command phase are paused. After ena returns high, the command resumes and eventually produces exactly one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: At every posedge while ena=0, assert cmd_ack=0 and verify the active-command phase and timing/filter probes do not progress. After ena=1, compare the observed phase sequence and single cmd_ack pulse against a reference model that resumes from the paused state.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to the same nonzero value, issue the same supported WRITE command with din=0, and leave ena high until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting enabled case for cmd_ack: normal timing progression occurs and cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock at command completion.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to predict the variable completion time from clk_cnt and bus conditions; assert that exactly one cmd_ack pulse occurs with ena high and that no extra pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: Reset with busy=0, set ena=0, keep filtered SCL high, and apply a stable SDA high-to-low transition long enough to require filter samples while ena remains low; then hold the raw bus transition stable for several clocks.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for busy: input-filter operation is gated, no filtered START is processed, and busy remains low while ena=0.
elements.check_method: Observe busy after every posedge and assert it remains 0 while ena=0. Monitor filter_sample_due and filtered START probes to ensure no new filtered transition is processed during the disabled interval.

elements.stimulus: Reset with busy=0, set ena=1, keep filtered SCL high, and apply the same stable SDA high-to-low transition until the three-sample majority filter produces a filtered START.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting enabled case for busy: filtering progresses and busy becomes high when the filtered START is detected.
elements.check_method: Compare filter samples, filtered SDA transition, start_condition, and registered busy against a reference model; assert busy rises on the clock that processes the filtered START and remains high thereafter absent a STOP or reset.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set clk_cnt to 1, drive a released-high bus, and issue an accepted START command with ena high. After the START sequence is active but before its terminal phase, drive ena low and hold it low for multiple clock cycles, including cycles on which the divider would otherwise expire; then restore ena high.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-low side of the observed behavior: while ena is low, cmd_ack remains low, no command-completion pulse occurs, the active START phase does not advance, clk_en_tick and filter_sample_due do not assert, and the divider reload/filter-counter reset behavior postpones completion. After ena returns high, normal progression resumes and exactly one cmd_ack pulse eventually occurs.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for divider reload, filter-counter reset, and FSM timing. At every posedge during the ena-low interval compare cmd_ack, phase probes, clk_en_tick, filter_sample_due, and counter probes; then verify one eventual cmd_ack pulse after re-enabling ena.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the reset, released-high bus, clk_cnt=1, and accepted START-command sequence, but keep ena high continuously from command acceptance through the terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting ena-high side of the observed behavior: the divider and input-filter timing progress normally, the START sequence reaches its terminal phase, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock without being postponed by an ena-low interval.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed phase transitions, clk_en_tick/filter_sample_due activity, and one-clock cmd_ack pulse against the enabled reference-model schedule, allowing the specified registered output latency.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, present cmd=START with a released-high bus, and hold the command until it is accepted. After acceptance, keep ena=1 and the bus free so the START FSM phase can advance.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: the divider is loaded from clk_cnt and, after the clk_cnt-derived enabled interval expires, generates a timing tick that advances the bit-level FSM; scl_oen changes to the next prescribed START-command SCL phase. Before that expiration, scl_oen remains in its current phase.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the divider reload, decrement, expiration, and clk_en generation. Correlate the modeled expiration/tick with the observed registered scl_oen transition and assert that no transition occurs earlier than the modeled boundary.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, issue and accept a START command on a released-high bus, then deassert ena before the next clk_cnt-derived timing interval expires and hold ena=0 for several clocks.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise side of shows: while ena is low, timing progression is disabled, no clk_en advancement occurs, and scl_oen holds its current phase rather than advancing at the nominal clk_cnt boundary.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen each clock against the reference model with ena gating applied. Assert that the divider is held/reinitialized according to the enabled-timing model and that no scl_oen phase transition occurs during the ena-low interval, even when the ungated clk_cnt interval would have expired.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the filter initialized and ena=1, set clk_cnt=8, keep scl_i high and the bus otherwise released, establish filtered SDA high, then drive sda_i stably low and hold it low. Record the synchronized transition, filter_sample_due events, and the posedge at which busy rises.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy rises only after the stable SDA high-to-low transition is processed on the filter cadence derived from clk_cnt; with clk_cnt=8, the sampling interval is floor(8/4)=2 enabled clocks, subject to the modeled synchronizer and registered busy latency. The measured latency must match the reference model using that interval.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage synchronizer, filter counter, three-sample majority filter, START detection, and registered busy update. Compare the observed busy-rise cycle and filter_sample_due cadence against the model, allowing no unexplained dependence on raw input timing.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the identical initialized-bus START stimulus with ena=1, but set clk_cnt=0. Keep scl_i high, establish filtered SDA high, then drive sda_i stably low and hold it low; compare the busy-rise cycle and filter_sample_due cadence with TP-0000 using clk_cnt=8.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: with clk_cnt=0, the filter sampling interval is treated as zero and sampling occurs on every enabled clock. busy must therefore rise at the zero-interval reference-model latency and at a measurably different, no-slower filter cadence than the clk_cnt=8 run; it must not retain the clk_cnt=8 latency. This is the holding side of the requirement, while unchanged or differently scaled latency is the otherwise side.
elements.check_method: Run both prescaler configurations from identical reset and input-transition conditions, count enabled clocks from the synchronized SDA transition to busy rising, and compare each result with the reference model. Assert that the clk_cnt=0 filter_sample_due cadence is every enabled clock and that the two busy latencies differ as predicted.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000, keep the bus externally released high, then while the command FSM is idle drive cmd=4'b0001 (I2C_CMD_START) through an enabled timing tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0021: the idle FSM decodes cmd=I2C_CMD_START and enters the START sequence; after the registered state update, sda_oen becomes 0 to drive SDA low while scl_oen remains 1 so SCL is released high.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset, sample sda_oen and scl_oen after nonblocking assignments settle; correlate the transition with the enabled timing tick and verify the START-sequence probe is active and the observed sda_oen value is 0.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000, keep the bus externally released high, then while the command FSM is idle drive cmd=4'b0000 (NOP, a non-START command) through an enabled timing tick and continue observing for several enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of REQ-0021: cmd is not decoded as I2C_CMD_START, the FSM remains idle without entering the START sequence, and sda_oen remains 1 (released high) rather than becoming 0 or producing the START signature.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare sda_oen against the idle reset value and verify it remains 1 throughout the observation window; also verify in_idle remains asserted and in_start_sequence never asserts.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus externally released high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the FSM idle, drive cmd=I2C_CMD_STOP (4'b0010), and wait for the enabled timing tick that accepts the command.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: sda_oen becomes 0 on the registered output update for the initial STOP phase, driving SDA low before SCL is released; the FSM enters the STOP sequence.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after NBA settling, assert that in_idle is followed by in_stop_sequence and that sda_oen changes from 1 to 0 during the initial STOP phase; record a bin for STOP acceptance and compare the observed phase against the reference FSM model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus externally released high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the FSM idle, drive cmd=I2C_CMD_NOP (4'b0000), and wait through the enabled timing tick that would accept an idle command.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of shows: sda_oen remains 1 and no STOP-sequence SDA drive-low phase occurs; the FSM remains idle.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after NBA settling, assert in_idle remains true and sda_oen remains 1 throughout the observation window; compare against the reference decoder model and record a bin for absence of STOP-sequence entry.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena high and drive cmd=4 (I2C_CMD_WRITE) while the controller is idle. Provide a normal released-high I2C bus, drive din to 0, and hold the command and bus inputs stable until the WRITE operation completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the requirement's observed-via shows: the controller accepts cmd=4 as WRITE, executes the WRITE sequence, and asserts cmd_ack high for exactly one clock cycle at WRITE completion without asserting arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_idle, in_write_sequence, command_active, cmd_ack, al, scl_oen, and sda_oen on each posedge after registered updates. Confirm entry into the WRITE sequence, exactly one cmd_ack pulse, completion after the expected variable timing, and no arbitration-loss abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena high and drive an unsupported cmd value such as 3 while the controller is idle. Keep the bus released high and hold din and all other inputs as in the equivalent normal WRITE trial until any command processing would have completed.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of the requirement's observed-via shows: the unsupported cmd value is not accepted as I2C_CMD_WRITE; the controller remains idle, produces no WRITE output sequence, and does not assert a WRITE completion cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_idle, in_write_sequence, command_active, cmd_ack, scl_oen, and sda_oen on each posedge after registered updates. Confirm no transition into the WRITE sequence and no cmd_ack high pulse during the complete observation window.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release nReset and rst, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, and drive cmd=4'b1000 (I2C_CMD_READ) while in_idle. Hold the command through an enabled clk_en_tick, then provide a valid filtered SCL read clock pulse with the external SDA response held high or low and allow the command to complete.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled idle-state evaluation, the controller enters the READ sequence rather than remaining idle, performs the READ operation, and produces exactly one cmd_ack pulse at the terminal phase. The acknowledgement occurs after the variable timing, filtering, and any bus-wait delays, not prematurely at command presentation.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle and in_read_sequence probes to confirm the state transition and READ execution; use a reference model for clk_en, filtering, and variable latency; compare cmd_ack against the model and assert that exactly one clock-wide pulse occurs for the accepted READ command.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1, clk_cnt=1, and both bus lines released high, keep the FSM idle and drive cmd=4'b0000 (I2C_CMD_NOP) through an enabled clk_en_tick. Return cmd to NOP and continue clocking for the full command-processing observation window.
elements.expected_response: The idle command evaluation takes the no-op side of the requirement: the FSM remains in_idle and cmd_ack never pulses.
elements.check_method: Sample in_idle and cmd_ack after each settled posedge; assert in_idle remains asserted and compare the complete cmd_ack history over the observation window against an all-zero expectation.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the idle-state command evaluation with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1 for every unsupported 4-bit command value 4'b0011, 0101, 0110, 0111, 1001, 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101, 1110, and 1111, holding each value through an enabled clk_en_tick while scl_i and sda_i remain released high.
elements.expected_response: For each unsupported command value, the controller takes the no-op side of the requirement: it remains in_idle and produces no cmd_ack pulse or command-processing sequence.
elements.check_method: Run each encoding as an independent trial, sample in_idle and cmd_ack after every settled posedge, and assert that the FSM stays idle with an all-zero cmd_ack trace for every unsupported value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, select a nonzero clk_cnt, drive din=0, keep the external SDA and SCL lines released high, and issue cmd=WRITE. Hold din=0 through acceptance and the WRITE data-bit phase until command completion.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase while the controller transmits din=0, sda_oen is 0. This is the din=0 side of the required behavior: sda_oen is 0 when din is 0.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while in_write_sequence is asserted and the data-bit phase is active, compare the registered sda_oen output against the reference value 0; require no arbitration loss or command abort before cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, select a nonzero clk_cnt, drive din=1, keep the external SDA and SCL lines released high, and issue cmd=WRITE. Hold din=1 through acceptance and the WRITE data-bit phase until command completion.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase while the controller transmits din=1, sda_oen is 1. This is the din=1 side of the required behavior: sda_oen is 1 when din is 1.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while in_write_sequence is asserted and the data-bit phase is active, compare the registered sda_oen output against the reference value 1; require no arbitration loss or command abort before cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, cmd=WRITE (0100), and din=0. Present a released-high bus and hold din=0 from command acceptance through completion while allowing the WRITE sequence to run until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE bit's SDA output phase after command acceptance and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 0, meaning the DUT drives SDA low. This is the din=0 holding side of the observed shows condition.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while in_write_sequence and before cmd_ack, compare the registered sda_oen output against the reference active-low mapping sda_oen == 0 for din=0; require no mismatch.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, cmd=WRITE (0100), and din=1. Present a released-high bus and hold din=1 from command acceptance through completion while allowing the WRITE sequence to run until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE bit's SDA output phase after command acceptance and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 1, meaning the DUT releases SDA high. This is the din=1 contrasting side of the observed shows condition.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while in_write_sequence and before cmd_ack, compare the registered sda_oen output against the reference active-low mapping sda_oen == 1 for din=1; require no mismatch.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and a finite clk_cnt, issue a READ command, and after the DUT releases SCL by driving scl_oen high, hold scl_i low so the released bus SCL remains low throughout the READ sample window.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: scl_oen remains high and the READ window does not end while the externally held-low scl_i produces filtered SCL low; the DUT must not transition to the phase that pulls SCL low or generate the READ completion acknowledgment until filtered SCL rises.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk, sample scl_i, filtered-SCL probes, in_read_sequence, slave_wait_active, scl_oen, and cmd_ack after nonblocking updates settle. Compare against a reference model of synchronization, filtering, slave-wait behavior, and variable timing; assert that scl_oen stays high and no READ completion occurs during the filtered-low interval.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and a finite clk_cnt, issue a READ command, and after the DUT releases SCL by driving scl_oen high, allow scl_i to rise and remain high so the released bus SCL becomes filtered high.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of shows: once the external scl_i rise propagates through synchronization and filtering, scl_oen transitions low to end the READ window, after which the READ sequence proceeds to completion and produces its command-complete pulse.
elements.check_method: Drive the open-drain bus model with the DUT output enable and external scl_i, then sample filtered_scl_rising, in_read_sequence, scl_oen, and cmd_ack after each posedge clk. Compare transition ordering and variable latency with a reference model, requiring scl_oen to fall only after the filtered SCL rising event and the subsequent READ low phase.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous reset, release it, and wait for the bus and filtered histories to be high. With ena high and clk_cnt set to 1, issue a START command and hold scl_i high while drive sda_i from high to low long enough to pass synchronization and majority filtering.
elements.expected_response: The synchronized and filtered SCL is observed high when the filtered SDA falling transition forms a START; busy asserts on the registered detection cycle. This is the holding side of the busy 'sets high for a filtered START' behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample busy after each posedge and compare against a reference model of the two-stage SCL/SDA synchronizers, three-sample majority filter, and filtered START detector; require busy to transition from 0 to 1 only after the filtered transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy low, drive scl_i low long enough for filtered SCL to become low, then drive sda_i high to low while filtered SCL remains low; subsequently return scl_i high. Also inject a one-sample SCL high glitch that does not change the majority-filtered SCL.
elements.expected_response: No filtered START or STOP is detected during the invalid-SCL transition or the short glitch, and busy remains unchanged at 0. This is the contrasting side of the busy behavior: busy does not change for a raw transition or glitch that does not produce the corresponding filtered transition.
elements.check_method: Compare busy on every settled posedge with the filter reference model and assert that no busy transition occurs unless the modeled filtered SDA edge occurs while modeled filtered SCL is high.

elements.stimulus: Establish busy high using a filtered START, keep filtered SCL high, then drive filtered SDA from low to high by holding sda_i and scl_i at their required levels long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to complete.
elements.expected_response: busy clears on the registered cycle that processes the synchronized and filtered STOP condition. This is the holding side of the busy 'clears low for a filtered STOP' behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the filtered SDA rising edge while filtered SCL is high, then compare the predicted busy-clear cycle with the DUT busy output.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and clk_cnt set to 1, issue a WRITE command with din=0 on a bus whose scl_i remains high throughout the released-SCL high phase; do not inject any external SCL transition or stretch.
elements.expected_response: After the synchronized and filtered SCL condition permits the normal phase boundary, scl_oen changes from released high to driven low at the normal timed boundary. This is the ordinary side of the scl_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: Track clk_en and filtered SCL in a cycle-accurate reference model; assert that scl_oen changes only at the predicted enabled timing phase and that the registered output appears one posedge after the state update.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and clk_cnt set to 1, issue a WRITE command with din=0. During the released-SCL high phase, externally hold scl_i low long enough for synchronized filtering to make filtered SCL low; then release scl_i high and hold it high until filtering completes.
elements.expected_response: While filtered SCL remains low, the controller enters slave-wait behavior, pauses timing/FSM progression, and does not advance scl_oen to the normal SCL-low phase boundary. After filtered SCL returns high, timing resumes and scl_oen advances only after the permitted timed boundary. This is the holding side of the scl_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen, clk_en, and the slave-wait probe against a reference model including synchronizer latency, majority filtering, counter hold, and reload; assert no phase advance while modeled filtered SCL is low.

elements.stimulus: During the released-SCL high phase of a WRITE, apply an scl_i low pulse shorter than the synchronization/filter qualification interval, then restore scl_i high before the filtered SCL changes.
elements.expected_response: The raw SCL pulse does not produce a filtered SCL falling event or sustained filtered-low condition; scl_oen follows the normal timed phase progression rather than being postponed or reloaded. This is the contrasting side of the scl_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: Model the two-stage synchronizer and three-sample majority filter, verify that no filtered SCL event is produced, and compare the DUT scl_oen transition cycle with the no-stretch reference.

elements.stimulus: Issue a READ command with ena high and clk_cnt set to 1. Hold scl_i low, set sda_i to 1, then raise scl_i and hold both inputs stable long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to produce a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: dout updates to 1 on the registered cycle that processes the synchronized and filtered SCL rising edge. This is the holding side of the dout behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to predict the filtered SCL rising edge and filtered SDA value, then require dout to equal the modeled SDA value on the corresponding posedge and remain stable otherwise.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller so dout is 0, start a READ with scl_i low and sda_i high, then apply an scl_i high pulse shorter than the synchronization/filter qualification interval and return scl_i low without producing a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: dout remains 0 and does not update for the raw SCL edge or glitch that fails to produce a filtered SCL rising edge. This is the contrasting side of the dout behavior.
elements.check_method: Confirm with the synchronizer/filter reference model that no filtered SCL rising event occurs, then assert that dout has no transition during and after the raw pulse.

elements.stimulus: Instantiate the module with the external open-drain SDA buffer connected to sda_i. After reset, keep the controller idle and enabled, drive filtered SCL high through scl_i, hold the external SDA line high long enough to establish the filtered high value, then drive sda_i low and hold it long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to produce a qualifying high-to-low transition.
elements.expected_response: busy rises high after the synchronized and filtered SDA transition while filtered SCL is high. This is the asserting side of the observed_via shows: busy rises, demonstrating that the external SDA line reaches START-condition detection.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage synchronizer, filter sampling, majority filter, and START edge detection; after each posedge and settled nonblocking update, check that busy has a new rising event at the modeled filtered START detection and that the observed sda_i waveform is the source of the transition.

elements.stimulus: Instantiate the module with the external open-drain SDA buffer connected to sda_i. After reset, keep the controller idle and enabled, drive filtered SCL high through scl_i, and hold the external SDA line high continuously for the observation interval without applying any qualifying high-to-low transition.
elements.expected_response: busy does not newly rise during the observation interval. This is the non-asserting side of the observed_via shows: busy remains without a new rise when the external SDA line remains high and no qualifying filtered START transition occurs.
elements.check_method: Monitor busy for a rising edge after reset while comparing synchronized and filtered sda_i/scl_i values against the reference model; fail if busy rises without a modeled high-to-low SDA transition while filtered SCL is high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue cmd=START while idle. Allow the synchronized SDA transition caused by the START sequence to pass through the three-sample majority filter while filtered SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for busy: busy rises to 1 only after the synchronized and filtered SDA high-to-low transition is detected as START; a raw or intermediate synchronized value before filtered acceptance does not set busy.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage SDA synchronizer, filter sampling, three-sample majority value, and START edge detection; compare the predicted filtered transition and registered busy output after each posedge.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the controller idle and both filtered lines high, apply an sda_i low pulse shorter than the synchronization and majority-filter acceptance interval, then return sda_i high without issuing a command or changing scl_i.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for busy: busy remains unchanged at 0; the raw SDA pulse that does not survive synchronization and filtering does not create a START indication or set busy.
elements.check_method: Predict the synchronizer and filter histories cycle by cycle and assert that filtered SDA never produces a qualifying high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high; compare busy against the model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1, keep the bus released high initially, and drive sda_i low during the WRITE released stable-high phase while scl_i is high. Hold the low level long enough to become the filtered SDA value.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for al: al rises to 1 during the released stable-high arbitration phase because the synchronized and filtered SDA value is low when a high SDA was expected; the active command aborts without cmd_ack and both output enables are released.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the WRITE released-high arbitration window and filtered SDA value, then compare the predicted arbitration-loss event, sticky al assertion, absence of cmd_ack, and released output enables.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1 and keep sda_i high throughout the released stable-high phase, while injecting a low SDA pulse too short to be accepted by the synchronizer and majority filter.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for al: al remains low because the released SDA is observed high through the filtered path; the rejected raw disturbance does not cause arbitration loss, and the WRITE completes with its normal cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Model the SDA synchronization and filtering and verify that filtered SDA never becomes low during the arbitration-check window; compare al, cmd_ack, and command completion against the model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ, keep scl_i released high, and drive sda_i to a stable low or stable high value early enough for synchronization and filtering to settle before the active READ filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for dout: on the filtered SCL rising edge during READ, dout updates to the synchronized and majority-filtered SDA value, reproducing the externally supplied read bit.
elements.check_method: Run the reference model for synchronization, filter history, filtered SCL edge timing, and READ sampling; at each filtered SCL rising edge compare the predicted filtered SDA bit with registered dout on the following settled clock state.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=READ with clk_cnt=0, keep filtered SCL low or otherwise prevent a filtered SCL rising edge, and toggle sda_i through a raw pulse that is rejected by synchronization/filtering. Restore sda_i without allowing a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for dout: dout does not update from the raw SDA transition; a filtered SCL rising edge is required, and the filtered-out SDA glitch is not captured as a read bit.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to verify that no filtered SCL rising edge occurs and that the SDA pulse does not alter the filtered SDA value; assert that dout retains its prior value throughout the stimulus.

elements.stimulus: Set ena high, hold the bus released and high, issue cmd=START while idle, and continue driving the external bus so the complete START sequence finishes without reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at command completion, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock cycle; it is low on the following clock and the command FSM is idle.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack on settled posedge samples; assert exactly one high sample at the terminal completion event, no adjacent high sample, and in_idle is true afterward.

elements.stimulus: Establish a busy transaction as needed, issue cmd=STOP with ena high, and allow the complete STOP sequence to finish with SCL released high and no reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock cycle when STOP completes, then deasserted on the next clock while the command FSM is idle.
elements.check_method: Compare registered cmd_ack against the modeled STOP terminal phase and count consecutive high samples; require a single-cycle pulse followed by low and in_idle.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and the external device providing a valid SCL response and SDA data, issue cmd=READ while idle and let all READ timing phases complete without reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack becomes high for exactly one clock at READ completion and returns low on the following clock, with the command FSM returned to idle.
elements.check_method: Use the reference timing model to identify READ completion, then sample cmd_ack after each posedge and require one and only one high cycle followed by low and in_idle.

elements.stimulus: With ena high, issue cmd=WRITE for din=0 and allow the external bus to acknowledge the complete WRITE timing sequence without arbitration loss or reset.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock when WRITE completes, is low on the next clock, and the command FSM is idle.
elements.check_method: Model the WRITE terminal phase, compare its completion cycle with cmd_ack, and assert one-cycle pulse width with no additional high cycles and in_idle afterward.

elements.stimulus: While idle with ena high, drive cmd=0000 (NOP), then drive each unsupported 4-bit command encoding other than 0001, 0010, 0100, and 1000 for at least one enabled clock.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: no supported command-completion event occurs, so cmd_ack remains low and no one-clock command-complete pulse is produced.
elements.check_method: At every enabled posedge during and after each NOP or unsupported command, assert cmd_ack is 0 and confirm the FSM remains idle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive a released-high bus, and issue cmd=START on an enabled timing tick. Allow the START sequence to progress through SDA-low while SCL is high and the subsequent SCL-low terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: When the START bit-level sequence reaches its terminal phase, cmd_ack becomes high for exactly one clk cycle. This is the holding case of the requirement; the command-complete indication is present.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare cmd_ack against a reference FSM that identifies START terminal-phase completion; assert one and only one consecutive high sample, with cmd_ack low on the preceding and following cycles.

elements.stimulus: Establish busy by applying a filtered START condition, then set ena=1 and issue cmd=STOP on an enabled timing tick. Drive the bus so STOP performs SDA low, releases SCL until filtered SCL is high, then releases SDA.
elements.expected_response: When the STOP bit-level sequence reaches its terminal phase, cmd_ack becomes high for exactly one clk cycle. This is the holding case of the requirement; the command-complete indication is present.
elements.check_method: Use the reference STOP sequence to mark terminal completion and compare the registered cmd_ack waveform, requiring exactly one high cycle and low before and after it.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, issue cmd=READ on an enabled timing tick, release SDA, and provide a filtered SCL rising edge followed by the required low phase. Repeat with external SDA returning 0 and returning 1.
elements.expected_response: For each READ transaction, cmd_ack is asserted high for exactly one clk cycle after the READ bit-level sequence completes, following the filtered SCL rising-edge capture and low phase. This is the holding case of the requirement; the command-complete indication is present.
elements.check_method: A timing-aware reference model locates each READ terminal completion despite prescaler and filter latency, then checks that cmd_ack is a single-cycle pulse aligned to that completion and is absent at all other cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive din=0 and issue cmd=WRITE on an enabled timing tick; allow the write sequence to set SDA, release SCL for the high phase, and pull SCL low. Repeat with din=1 while SDA remains high externally so arbitration is not lost.
elements.expected_response: When each WRITE bit-level sequence reaches its terminal phase, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle. This is the holding case of the requirement; the command-complete indication is present for both din values.
elements.check_method: Track WRITE terminal phases with a reference FSM and compare cmd_ack after settled posedges, requiring one pulse per completed command, exactly one cycle wide, with no extra high cycles.

elements.stimulus: Issue a supported WRITE command with ena=1, then hold released SCL externally low during its high phase so the command remains active and cannot reach its terminal phase. Observe cmd_ack before, during, and after this hold; then release SCL and allow the command to finish.
elements.expected_response: Before and throughout the non-terminal clock-stretching interval, cmd_ack remains low; this is the contrasting case of the requirement, where the command has not finished. After SCL is released and the terminal phase is reached, cmd_ack becomes high for exactly one clk cycle and returns low thereafter.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to distinguish active non-terminal cycles from terminal completion, assert cmd_ack=0 for every non-terminal cycle, and then require exactly one high cycle at completion followed by low.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the filtered bus idle and released high, set ena=1 and issue the START command on an enabled timing tick. Drive the external bus released high and allow the filtered START transition to complete; then hold the bus in the busy interval without issuing STOP.
elements.expected_response: In the steady interval after the filtered START transition and before the next filtered STOP transition, busy is high, which is the 'busy is high when the bus is busy' side of the requirement.
