elements.check_method: At each settled posedge after the registered START detection, compare busy against a reference bus-state model and require busy==1 throughout the interval until STOP detection.

elements.stimulus: Create a busy interval by issuing START on an enabled timing tick with the bus released high, then issue STOP after START completion. Allow the STOP sequence to release SDA while filtered SCL is high and allow the resulting filtered STOP transition to complete; keep the bus released and idle afterward.
elements.expected_response: In the steady interval after the filtered STOP transition, busy is low, which is the 'busy is low when the bus is idle' side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge after the registered STOP detection, compare busy against the reference bus-state model and require busy==0 throughout the idle interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the bus released and both scl_i and sda_i high, hold SCL high and drive SDA from high to low; maintain the resulting levels long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to produce a filtered START condition. Keep ena high and sample after each posedge.
elements.expected_response: The filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high is detected as START, and busy changes from low to high on the registered update following detection and remains high while no STOP is detected. This is the high-after-START side of the required port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the synchronizers, filter histories, filtered START edge, and registered busy update. Assert that busy is low before the modeled START detection update and high on that update and throughout the subsequent interval until STOP or reset.

elements.stimulus: First generate and filter a START condition with SCL high and SDA transitioning high to low, then keep the bus busy and SCL high while drive SDA from low to high; maintain the levels long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to produce a filtered STOP condition. Keep ena high and sample after each posedge.
elements.expected_response: After the filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL is high is detected as STOP, busy changes from high to low on the registered update following detection and remains low. This is the low-after-STOP side of the required port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the filtered START and STOP detection cycles and compare the registered busy output. Assert that busy is high before the modeled STOP detection update and low on that update and thereafter until another START or reset.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1 while the bus is released high. Wait for the enabled clk_en tick that accepts the command and for the WRITE sequence to reach its released-SDA stable high arbitration-checking phase. Then externally hold sda_i low long enough for the synchronized, majority-filtered SDA value to become low while sda_oen remains 1.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of shows: al asserts when filtered SDA is observed low during released-SDA arbitration checking. The active command is aborted, no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted command, and both output enables are released.
elements.check_method: At the clock edge processing the filtered SDA-low observation, compare al against 1 and monitor it for sticky retention until reset; verify sda_oen and scl_oen release and verify cmd_ack never pulses after the injected loss.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1 while the external bus remains high whenever the controller releases SDA. Allow the command to reach and complete its released-SDA stable high arbitration-checking phase without injecting a filtered SDA-low condition.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise side of shows: al remains deasserted because released-SDA arbitration checking observes filtered SDA high and no unrequested STOP occurs.
elements.check_method: During the entire active WRITE sequence, sample filtered SDA and the write arbitration-checking probe, and assert that al remains 0 through command completion; verify a normal one-clock cmd_ack occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=0 or din=1, wait until the command is active, and drive the external bus so filtered SCL is high. While the non-STOP command is active, create a filtered STOP condition by driving filtered SDA from low to high while filtered SCL remains high; do not issue cmd=STOP.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of shows for the second condition: al asserts when an unrequested STOP is detected during the active non-STOP command. The command aborts without cmd_ack and the controller releases both output enables.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered STOP-condition probe to identify the detection cycle, then compare al=1 on the corresponding settled clocked output and verify it remains asserted until reset; check that no completion pulse is produced for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ, and allow the READ sequence to reach its data-bit sample window. Hold the external bus SDA low for the received bit, release SCL, and drive the bus so the filtered SCL makes a rising edge while the filtered SDA is low.
elements.expected_response: At the registered observation following the filtered SCL rising edge, dout captures 0, which is the received data bit; this is the 'dout captures the current received data bit' side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use the READ-sequence and filtered_scl_rising probes to identify the sample event, then compare dout after the posedge and settled nonblocking assignments against the filtered SDA value of 0. Require the value to remain 0 until a subsequent qualified sample or reset.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ, and allow the READ sequence to reach its data-bit sample window. Hold the external bus SDA high for the received bit, release SCL, and drive the bus so the filtered SCL makes a rising edge while the filtered SDA is high.
elements.expected_response: At the registered observation following the filtered SCL rising edge, dout captures 1, which is the received data bit; this is the 'dout captures the current received data bit' side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use the READ-sequence and filtered_scl_rising probes to identify the sample event, then compare dout after the posedge and settled nonblocking assignments against the filtered SDA value of 1.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset so dout is initialized, release it, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ. Allow the READ sequence to enter its data-bit sample window, keep the external SCL line low so filtered SCL does not rise, and toggle SDA between low and high without producing a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: dout does not capture the current SDA value at any observation point without a filtered SCL rising edge and remains at its prior value; this is the contrasting 'dout does not capture the current received data bit and remains its prior value' side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: While in the READ sample window, assert that filtered_scl_rising is absent and compare dout on each posedge against its value before the SDA toggles. Require no dout change until a qualified filtered SCL rising edge occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, enable the controller, issue a READ command, and provide a released-high SCL bus. Drive SDA so that the filtered SDA value is 0 before a filtered SCL rising edge, then make the filtered SCL rise while the filtered SDA remains 0; repeat with filtered SDA equal to 1 for a later filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: On each rising-edge cycle of filtered SCL, dout captures the current filtered SDA value: dout becomes 0 for the first edge and 1 for the later edge. This is the holding case of shows: dout captures the current filtered SDA value on the filtered-SCL rising-edge cycle.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronizers, majority filtering, and filtered SCL edge detection. At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare dout with the modeled filtered SDA value whenever filtered_scl_rising is asserted, and require the captured value to match on every such edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a READ command and establish a previously captured dout value of 0 using one filtered SCL rising edge with filtered SDA low. While filtered SCL remains low and no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, change the bus so the filtered SDA value becomes 1, then hold SCL low for multiple enabled clocks before producing the next filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: During every cycle without a filtered SCL rising edge, dout does not capture the new filtered SDA value and remains 0 despite filtered SDA becoming 1. This is the contrasting side of shows: dout does not capture a new filtered SDA value on a cycle without a rising edge of filtered SCL.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify cycles where filtered_scl_rising is deasserted and filtered SDA changes to 1. Sample dout after each posedge settles and require it to retain its prior value until the next modeled filtered SCL rising edge; then check that it updates to 1 only on that edge.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, then keep rst low and ena low while observing the DUT through reset recovery and idle operation.
elements.expected_response: Shows side of the requirement: scl_o is continuously 1'b0 at every observation during reset recovery and idle; it never becomes 1 or otherwise nonzero.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_o asynchronously during nReset assertion and after each posedge following release; assert scl_o==0 independent of reset and idle state.

elements.stimulus: With nReset released and ena high, issue START, WRITE with din=1, and STOP using clk_cnt=1; provide a released-high bus so the command FSM progresses through phases that alternately drive and release scl_oen.
elements.expected_response: Shows side of the requirement in the contrasting command-processing context: scl_o remains continuously 1'b0 while scl_oen transitions between drive-low and release states throughout START, WRITE, and STOP; scl_o must not become 1 or otherwise nonzero.
elements.check_method: At every posedge and after each settled registered output update, compare scl_o against constant zero while independently recording scl_oen transitions; flag any scl_o value other than 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the bus externally released high. Issue the START command (cmd=0001) on an enabled timing tick and allow the START sequence to progress through its SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase into the phase that drives SCL low.
elements.expected_response: During the START phase that applies an SCL-low output, scl_oen is 0; because scl_o is constantly 0, the resulting SCL bus level is low. This is the positive side of the observed_via shows statement: scl_oen=0 indicates that SCL is driven low.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, monitor in_start_sequence and the SCL-low phase, then compare scl_oen to 0 and independently resolve the open-drain bus level as scl_oen==0 or external_scl_drive_low. Require scl_oen==0 and observed SCL low for the active phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the bus externally released high. Issue the START command (cmd=0001) on an enabled timing tick and observe the initial START phase before the controller pulls SCL low, when SDA is driven low while SCL remains released.
elements.expected_response: During the START phase in which SCL is released rather than driven low, scl_oen is 1 and the SCL bus remains high when no external participant drives it low. This is the contrasting side of the observed_via shows statement: scl_oen=1 indicates that SCL is released rather than driven low.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, identify the START phase with SDA driven low and SCL released, then compare scl_oen to 1 and resolve the open-drain bus level. Require scl_oen==1 and observed SCL high with the external SCL driver released.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, deassert it, keep ena high and clk_cnt at 0, hold scl_i and sda_i high, then issue the START command and observe the phase in which the controller has released SCL.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen is 1, allowing the external pull-up to drive SCL high, and sda_o remains 0 at every observed clock.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen and sda_o against the expected release-phase values; bin the release observation and assert sda_o never differs from 0.

elements.stimulus: Continue the same START command sequence until the controller enters its subsequent phase that drives SCL low, with ena high and the external bus otherwise released.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_oen is 0 rather than 1 because SCL is actively driven low in this phase, while sda_o remains constant 0.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, detect the SCL-low phase and assert scl_oen=0 there; independently sample sda_o throughout the sequence and assert it remains 0, distinguishing the non-release observation from the release case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, enable the module, issue a WRITE command with din=0 on an enabled timing tick, and provide a released-high SCL/SDA bus so the WRITE reaches its SDA-low drive phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the SDA drive phase, sda_o remains exactly 1'b0 and sda_oen asserts its active-low drive state (0), causing the SDA line to be driven low through sda_oen rather than through sda_o.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while the WRITE drive phase is active, compare sda_o against constant 1'b0 and check that the observed low SDA line coincides with sda_oen=0; fail if sda_o changes or if line control is represented by sda_o.

elements.stimulus: After reset, enable the module, issue a WRITE command with din=1 on an enabled timing tick, and provide a released-high SCL/SDA bus so the WRITE reaches its SDA released phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: during the SDA release phase, sda_o remains exactly 1'b0 while sda_oen deasserts to 1, releasing SDA high; no SDA control is attempted by changing sda_o.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while the WRITE released-high phase is active, compare sda_o against constant 1'b0 and check that the high SDA line coincides with sda_oen=1; fail if sda_o takes any nonzero value or if release is not controlled by sda_oen.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it; set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, keep the bus externally released high, then issue a START command and wait until the START sequence reaches its SDA-low phase while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: The holding case applies: sda_oen is 0, indicating that SDA is actively driven low.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the START SDA-low phase, compare the registered sda_oen output with 0 and verify the resolved SDA line is low under an externally released bus.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it; set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, keep SDA and SCL externally released high, and leave the controller idle without issuing a command, then observe the SDA output-enable.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting case applies: sda_oen is 1, indicating that SDA is released rather than actively driven low.
elements.check_method: After reset initialization and on subsequent settled posedges while idle, compare sda_oen with 1 and verify that the externally released SDA line remains high.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, deassert reset, set ena=1, provide clk_cnt=0 and an externally released-high SDA/SCL bus, then issue the START command and sample sda_oen during the initial START phase before the controller pulls SDA low.
elements.expected_response: sda_oen is high; this is the holding side of the requirement, indicating that SDA is released for the external pull-up and the observed SDA line is high.
elements.check_method: At settled posedge observations, assert sda_oen==1 and, with the external bus not driving low, assert the resolved SDA line is high during the START release phase.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, deassert reset, set ena=1, provide clk_cnt=0 and an externally released-high SDA/SCL bus, then issue the START command and advance through the START sequence until its SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase.
elements.expected_response: sda_oen is low; this is the contrasting side of the observed port behavior, indicating that SDA is driven low rather than released for the external pull-up, and the resolved SDA line is low.
elements.check_method: At settled posedge observations in the SDA-low START phase, assert sda_oen==0 and assert the resolved SDA line is low while the external participant is released.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, then apply synchronous rst on a rising edge. After reset, hold ena high with cmd=N​​OP in idle while externally releasing both bus lines high.
elements.expected_response: During reset and idle, scl_o and sda_o remain 0 at every observation. This is the holding side of the observed behavior: low outputs show that the module never directly drives either line high. Any scl_o=1 or sda_o=1 is the otherwise side and is a failure.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_o and sda_o asynchronously during nReset assertion and after each settled posedge while rst and idle conditions are applied; assert both outputs are continuously 0.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and an externally released-high bus, execute START, WRITE with din=0, READ, and STOP commands, allowing each command to complete and observing every command phase, including phases where the controller releases SCL or SDA.
elements.expected_response: Even when the external bus is high because the lines are released, and throughout every START, WRITE, READ, STOP, and idle phase, scl_o and sda_o remain 0. This is the holding side: low port outputs mean the bus-high level is never driven directly by the module. A high scl_o or sda_o would be the otherwise side of the observation and is a failure.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from command acceptance through cmd_ack and return to idle, compare scl_o and sda_o against constant 0 while independently checking the external bus level; flag any cycle on which either output is 1.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low, release it, then keep rst low and ena high with cmd=NОP while sampling scl_o and sda_o on every subsequent posedge clk.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: while the module operates in idle, scl_o=1'b0 and sda_o=1'b0 at every sampled clock edge. Any nonzero value is the otherwise/non-holding side.
elements.check_method: At each post-reset sampled posedge, compare scl_o and sda_o exactly against 1'b0; record a failure on any nonzero sample.

elements.stimulus: With nReset released, ena high, and a released-high external bus, issue START, then WRITE commands with din=0 and din=1, then READ and STOP, waiting for each command's cmd_ack before issuing the next command; sample scl_o and sda_o throughout all command phases and during returned idle.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting active-operation side of shows: during START, WRITE, READ, STOP, and idle phases, scl_o and sda_o remain 1'b0 despite the output-enable sequencing. A nonzero scl_o or sda_o would be the otherwise/non-holding side and fails the requirement.
elements.check_method: Continuously compare both output ports to constant zero after each settled posedge clk for the complete command sequence, independently of scl_oen and sda_oen values.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the external SCL and SDA drivers released high, issue a START command with ena=1, then allow the command to advance through its phases. Observe the phase where SDA is asserted low while SCL remains released, and the following phase where SCL is asserted low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0046: whenever scl_oen=0, the observed SCL bus line is pulled low, and whenever sda_oen=0, the observed SDA bus line is pulled low. The constant scl_o and sda_o values remain 0.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge observation, compute each open-drain bus line as low if either the corresponding DUT output-enable is 0 or the external driver is low, otherwise high. Assert that sda_oen=0 implies SDA is low and scl_oen=0 implies SCL is low during the START sequence.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep external SCL and SDA drivers released, issue a START command and then a STOP command with ena=1. Observe the initial START phase and the STOP phases in which the controller releases SCL and SDA, including the final idle state.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of REQ-0046: whenever scl_oen=1, SCL is released and the external pull-up makes the observed SCL line high when no external device pulls it low; whenever sda_oen=1, SDA is released and the external pull-up makes the observed SDA line high when no external device pulls it low.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge observation, drive no external low and compare the bus line levels against the output-enable values. Assert that scl_oen=1 produces a released/high SCL line and sda_oen=1 produces a released/high SDA line, and verify both remain released in idle after STOP.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, then deassert it while ena is high and leave the bus externally undriven with pull-ups enabled; observe the idle state.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for SDA: sda_oen is high, so SDA is released and the resolved SDA line is high from the external pull-up rather than being driven by the DUT.
elements.check_method: After reset settles, sample sda_oen and the resolved SDA bus. Compare against sda_oen==1 and resolved SDA==1; also verify sda_o==0.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, deassert it, and leave the bus externally undriven with pull-ups enabled; observe the released idle SCL line.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for SCL: scl_oen is high, so SCL is released and the resolved SCL line is high from the external pull-up rather than being driven by the DUT.
elements.check_method: After reset settles, sample scl_oen and the resolved SCL bus. Compare against scl_oen==1 and resolved SCL==1; also verify scl_o==0.

elements.stimulus: With the controller idle, ena high, clk_cnt set to a value allowing progress, and the bus externally released high, issue a START command and wait for the START sequence's SDA-low phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for SDA: sda_oen is low, so the DUT actively pulls SDA low; the resolved SDA line is low despite the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: During the START SDA-low phase, sample sda_oen and the resolved SDA bus. Compare against sda_oen==0 and resolved SDA==0; verify the low level is caused by DUT ownership rather than an external low drive.

elements.stimulus: With the controller idle, ena high, clk_cnt set to a value allowing progress, and the bus externally released high, issue a START command and wait for the subsequent phase in which the controller pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for SCL: scl_oen is low, so the DUT actively pulls SCL low; the resolved SCL line is low despite the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: During the START SCL-low phase, sample scl_oen and the resolved SCL bus. Compare against scl_oen==0 and resolved SCL==0; verify scl_o==0 and that the low level is caused by DUT ownership.

elements.stimulus: Do not drive any DUT operation or command on behalf of REQ-0048; classify the requirement as having no specified behavioral activation.
elements.expected_response: No requirement-specific DUT response, output, timing, or state transition is expected.
elements.check_method: Traceability review compares the requirement text and normalized expectation against the testplan element and confirms that no behavioral claim or executable DUT check is attributed to REQ-0048.

elements.stimulus: Deassert both resets, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value greater than 1, issue START and wait for its completion, then issue WRITE with din=0. During the WRITE stable-high phase, keep the external SCL and SDA lines high and observe several clk rising edges while cnt is nonzero and before the next timing expiration.
elements.expected_response: This is the ordinary non-reload case from REQ-0049: cnt decrements on each enabled clock and clk_en remains low. Consequently, scl_oen remains at its current released/high-phase value and the WRITE phase does not advance on those intermediate clocks.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare the reference divider model's cnt and clk_en against cnt_nonzero and clk_en_tick, and assert that scl_oen and in_write_sequence remain unchanged until the modeled expiration.

elements.stimulus: Run the same enabled WRITE sequence with clk_cnt=1 and din=0. Enter the stable-high WRITE phase with SCL released, then continue clocking with the external bus high through the counter expiration.
elements.expected_response: At the modeled counter boundary, cnt loads clk_cnt, clk_en is asserted for that cycle, and the FSM advances. This is the holding case in the observed-via description: scl_oen changes from 1 to 0 at the next bit-timing boundary rather than remaining in the released phase indefinitely.
elements.check_method: Use the divider reference model and the cnt_expired/clk_en_tick probes to identify the expiration edge; after NBA settling, assert the expected one-cycle tick and compare scl_oen against the WRITE phase transition in the model.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous nReset low between clock edges with clk_cnt=16'hA5A5, then release nReset while rst remains low. After reset, repeat with clk_cnt=0 and ena=1, clocking the DUT for multiple enabled cycles without issuing a command.
elements.expected_response: When reset is active, cnt loads clk_cnt and clk_en is asserted; after reset release, clk_cnt=0 does not create a stuck divider, and the timing tick occurs on every enabled clock. Since the FSM is idle, scl_oen remains released high, while the timing probes show repeated expiration/reload behavior.
elements.check_method: Check asynchronous reset state immediately and sample after each posedge. Compare cnt, cnt_expired, and clk_en_tick with a reference model for both clk_cnt values, and assert that no unintended scl_oen transition occurs while idle.

elements.stimulus: Start a WRITE with din=0 and clk_cnt=4, reach the stable-high phase, then drive ena low for several clock cycles before reasserting ena. Keep the external SCL high and do not change command inputs during the disabled interval.
elements.expected_response: This is the reload condition in REQ-0049: while ena is low, cnt is loaded from clk_cnt and clk_en is asserted, but command timing progression is disabled. The observed contrasting behavior is that scl_oen remains at its current phase during the disabled interval instead of advancing the WRITE phase on every clock; after ena returns high, timing resumes from the reloaded count.
elements.check_method: Assert that the divider model reloads on every disabled cycle and that clk_en does not cause an FSM phase change while ena=0. Compare scl_oen and in_write_sequence before, during, and after the pause, allowing the modeled post-enable boundary transition.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, issue WRITE with din=0, and reach a phase where SCL is released. While the DUT is released, externally force SCL low to create a filtered falling edge and then keep it low for several clocks before releasing it high.
elements.expected_response: The externally caused multi-master synchronization reloads cnt from clk_cnt and asserts clk_en at the synchronization event. The WRITE timing model reflects the corresponding timing boundary; scl_oen changes only according to that clk_en-driven phase transition and does not advance on subsequent clocks while the synchronized/stretched filtered SCL remains low.
elements.check_method: Drive the bus using open-drain resolution, detect the filtered SCL falling edge with scl_sync_event and filtered_scl_falling, and compare cnt reload, clk_en_tick, slave_wait_active, and scl_oen against the reference model cycle by cycle.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0, release it, and initialize with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1. Issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 while the bus is released high. When the WRITE phase releases SCL (scl_oen=1), externally drive SCL low and hold it low long enough for filtered_scl_low and slave_wait_active to assert. Keep ena=1 and the command inputs stable until filtered SCL returns high, then release the external SCL drive.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed behavior: while released SCL remains filtered low, the timing counter holds its value, clk_en_tick remains low, the WRITE phase does not advance, scl_oen remains 1, and cmd_ack does not pulse. After filtered SCL returns high, timing progression resumes and cmd_ack eventually produces the normal one-clock completion pulse, delayed by the stretch duration.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare clk_en_tick, cnt_nonzero, slave_wait_active, in_write_sequence, scl_oen, and cmd_ack against a reference timing model. Assert that no clk_en_tick or cmd_ack occurs during the interval slave_wait_active is asserted, and that exactly one cmd_ack pulse occurs after the filtered SCL-high release with latency extended relative to the unstretched model.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0, release it, and initialize with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1. Issue the same supported WRITE command with din=0 while the bus is released high. When the WRITE phase releases SCL (scl_oen=1), leave the external SCL drive released so filtered SCL remains high throughout the released high phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting ordinary case of the observed behavior: because released SCL is filtered high, no slave_wait state is inserted, the command advances through its phases on clk_en ticks, and cmd_ack produces one normal one-clock completion pulse without the stretch-induced delay.
elements.check_method: Use the reference divider/FSM model and sample after each posedge. Confirm slave_wait_active and filtered_scl_low remain deasserted during the released high phase, clk_en_tick occurs according to the configured counter, and exactly one cmd_ack pulse occurs at the predicted unstretched terminal completion; compare its latency with TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: Apply any legal clock, reset, command, enable, prescaler, and bus-input sequence; no stimulus is required by the numbered list marker "3.".
elements.expected_response: No specific DUT output, state transition, timing, or protocol behavior is required by REQ-0051.
elements.check_method: Mark the scenario as covered by review inspection; perform no functional comparison because the requirement declares no behavioral obligation.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=0, and issue cmd=0100 (WRITE). Model the open-drain bus so external SCL is held low after the DUT releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), long enough for the synchronized three-sample filter to keep filtered SCL low across the normal high-phase timing boundary.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of REQ-0052: when scl_oen has just released SCL and filtered SCL remains low, slave_wait_active asserts, timing/FSM progress pauses, and scl_oen remains 1 instead of transitioning back to 0 at the normal eligible boundary. Release external SCL high and allow filtering to complete; the controller then resumes progression and eventually completes the WRITE.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen and the slave_wait_active probe against a reference model of the released-SCL and filtered-SCL conditions. Record that slave_wait_active is asserted while scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL is low, that no normal high-phase scl_oen release-to-drive-low transition occurs during the wait, and that progress resumes only after filtered SCL becomes high.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=0, and issue cmd=0100 (WRITE). Model the open-drain bus with external SCL released high whenever the DUT sets scl_oen=1, allowing the filter to become high before the normal high-phase timing boundary.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case of REQ-0052: because released SCL becomes filtered high, slave_wait_active does not assert and scl_oen transitions from 1 to 0 at the next eligible bit-timing boundary, allowing the WRITE sequence to continue and eventually acknowledge.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen and the slave_wait_active probe with the reference timing model. Verify that filtered SCL reaches high while scl_oen=1, slave_wait_active remains deasserted, and scl_oen transitions to 0 at the modeled eligible boundary rather than remaining high beyond it.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1. Issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 while the bus is idle. When the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1) during the active command, externally hold scl_i=0 long enough for the synchronizer and filter to establish filtered SCL low, and maintain that condition for multiple timing intervals.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in REQ-0053: while SCL is released but remains filtered low, cmd_ack is not pulsed and command completion is postponed. The active command remains paused until filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while scl_oen=1 and filtered_scl_low/slave_wait_active is asserted, compare cmd_ack against a reference model and require cmd_ack=0; verify the command does not reach its terminal acknowledgement phase during the hold.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, ena=1, clk_cnt=1, and din=0 WRITE sequence, but when the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1), allow the external bus to remain high by driving scl_i=1. Keep SDA consistent with din=0 and do not inject arbitration loss or another bus event.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting case in REQ-0053: once released SCL is filtered high, the command is allowed to finish and cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock cycle.
elements.check_method: Use the divider, synchronizer, filter, and FSM reference model to predict completion after filtered SCL rises; verify cmd_ack asserts once for one settled posedge and is low on the surrounding cycles.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt=16'h0001, then issue a supported WRITE command (cmd=4'b0100, din=1'b0) while idle. After the WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen=1), drive scl_i=0 and hold it low long enough for the filtered SCL to become low; keep ena high and do not reset.
elements.expected_response: While scl_oen remains 1 and the filtered SCL line remains low, the timing counter and command phase remain paused: no following SCL phase transition occurs and no command completion is generated. After scl_i is released high and the filtered SCL becomes high, timing resumes and scl_oen transitions to the following WRITE phase at a subsequent enabled timing opportunity. This is the clock-stretching side of the specified behavior.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare scl_oen and command-phase progress against a reference model including the filtered SCL wait condition. Assert that clk_en_tick and the following phase transition do not occur while slave_wait_active is asserted, and that progress resumes only after filtered_scl_high. Check that no cmd_ack occurs during the pause.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt=16'h0001, then issue the same supported WRITE command (cmd=4'b0100, din=1'b0) while idle. After the WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen=1), keep scl_i=1 so that the filtered SCL remains or becomes high; keep ena high and do not reset.
elements.expected_response: Because released SCL is not being stretched, scl_oen does not remain waiting for a low filtered SCL condition; the timing counter continues to generate normal timing opportunities and scl_oen transitions to the following WRITE SCL phase, driving SCL low, at the normal phase timing. This is the no-stretching side of the specified behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model with the same clk_cnt and filter settings, and compare the observed scl_oen transition and command-phase timing. Assert that slave_wait_active is not entered, normal clk_en_tick progression continues, and the following phase occurs without the indefinite postponement required for the stretching case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt. Issue a WRITE command while scl_i and sda_i are released high. During the WRITE stable-high phase, when scl_oen=1, drive scl_i low and hold it low long enough for the synchronizer and majority filter to produce a filtered SCL falling edge; then release scl_i high after the synchronization interval.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observation: the controller detects the externally caused filtered SCL falling edge as a synchronization event. scl_oen remains released at 1 while the synchronization-induced low-period timing is restarted, then transitions to 0 only after the reloaded timing interval. cmd_ack is postponed until after that interval and the subsequent WRITE completion; no arbitration loss is caused by the SCL event.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered-SCL reference model and event probe to identify the filtered falling edge while scl_oen=1. Measure scl_oen and cmd_ack at settled posedges, and compare their transition and completion times with a model that reloads the timing counter at the synchronization event; assert that both occur later than the no-event reference.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and the same nonzero clk_cnt. Issue an otherwise identical WRITE command with scl_i and sda_i held high throughout the released SCL high phase; do not inject an external SCL falling edge before the nominal phase completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting no-event case of the observation: without an externally caused filtered SCL falling edge, scl_oen transitions from released 1 to driven-low 0 at the nominal WRITE phase timing, and cmd_ack occurs at the nominal completion of the WRITE timing sequence rather than being postponed by synchronization.
elements.check_method: Run the same filtered-input and divider reference model without an external SCL falling edge. At settled posedges compare scl_oen's release-to-low transition and the one-clock cmd_ack pulse against the nominal model, and verify they occur earlier than in TP-0000 by the synchronization reload interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value. Issue a valid WRITE command with din=1 while the bus is released high. During the active WRITE high phase, after the DUT releases SCL (scl_oen=1) and before the command's normal completion boundary, have an external participant drive scl_i low long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to produce a filtered SCL falling edge; hold SCL low through the synchronized low-period timing, then release it.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for REQ-0056@1: the filtered SCL falling edge is treated as another master forcing SCL low. cmd_ack must not pulse at the pre-event normal completion boundary; completion is postponed until the synchronized low-period timing has completed and the WRITE command can finish normally.
elements.check_method: Use the divider, synchronizer, filter, and command-phase reference model to predict the normal completion boundary and the delayed boundary. Assert that scl_sync_event occurs only while SCL is released, that cmd_ack is low at the normal boundary, and that exactly one cmd_ack pulse occurs only after the synchronized low-period delay.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and the same nonzero clk_cnt used for the event case. Issue the same valid WRITE command with din=1 while the bus is released high. During the active WRITE high phase, keep scl_i high and do not cause any externally driven filtered SCL falling edge while scl_oen=1; allow the command to proceed to its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting no-event case for REQ-0056@1: with no externally caused filtered SCL falling edge while SCL is released, cmd_ack must pulse at the command's normal completion timing and must not be postponed by clock synchronization.
elements.check_method: Run the same reference model and compare the observed cmd_ack pulse against the normal completion boundary. Assert that no scl_sync_event or filtered external SCL falling edge occurs during the released-SCL window and that exactly one cmd_ack pulse occurs at the predicted normal time.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0, and keep the bus externally high. During the active WRITE phase after the DUT releases SCL (scl_oen=1), externally pull scl_i low long enough for the synchronized, filtered SCL to produce a falling edge, then release it after the low-period synchronization has been established.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the requirement: the externally caused filtered SCL falling edge reloads the internal timing counter and restarts the low-period timing. The next scl_oen phase transition that would otherwise occur on the normal clk_en schedule is postponed until the restarted low-period timing completes; no earlier transition occurs.
elements.check_method: Use the timing reference model for synchronizers, filtering, counter reload, and clk_en. Detect the filtered SCL falling-edge event while scl_oen=1, record the nominal next scl_oen transition without synchronization, and assert that the observed registered scl_oen transition occurs only after the restarted low-period counter expires and is later than the nominal transition.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the identical reset, ena=1, clk_cnt=4, WRITE with din=0, and released-high bus sequence, but do not externally pull SCL low while the DUT has scl_oen=1; keep the filtered SCL high through the corresponding low-period boundary.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise-side of the requirement: without an externally caused filtered SCL falling edge, scl_oen makes the next command phase transition on the normal clk_en timing schedule, with no synchronization reload or inserted low-period delay.
elements.check_method: Run the same reference model and compare the observed registered scl_oen transition against the nominal no-synchronization schedule. Assert that the transition occurs at the normal modeled clk_en boundary and that no additional synchronization delay is present, contrasting it with TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: No DUT stimulus is required; record the presence of list-item marker 5 as a scaffolding item.
elements.expected_response: No behavior is required or expected from the DUT for this item.
elements.check_method: Review the generated testplan traceability report and confirm the item is marked covered without a DUT assertion or behavioral pass/fail check.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and establish a filtered idle-high bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Drive sda_i stably from 1 to 0 while keeping scl_i=1, then continue clocking for the complete two-stage synchronization and filter propagation interval.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy rises only after the SDA transition has propagated through the two-stage cSDA synchronization and filtered START processing; it does not rise at the raw input transition.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the two-stage synchronizers and filter sampling/majority logic. Compare the observed busy rising cycle with the modeled filtered START-detection cycle, allowing the specified registered busy update latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy=0, set ena=1 and establish scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Drive sda_i from 1 to 0 while keeping scl_i=1, and sample busy on every posedge from the raw transition until the two-stage synchronization and filter propagation window has completed.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case: busy remains at its prior value of 0 immediately after the raw SDA transition and throughout all cycles before synchronized, filtered START detection completes; no premature busy assertion occurs.
elements.check_method: Timestamp the raw SDA transition and use the reference model to identify the earliest cycle on which synchronized and filtered processing can detect START. Assert busy remains 0 at all earlier sampled cycles, including the first cycle after the raw transition.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset with ena=1, drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, and select a nonzero clk_cnt. Keep both bus inputs stable through multiple filter-counter expiries so each expiry shifts synchronized high samples into fSCL and fSDA without creating a filtered START condition.
elements.expected_response: At every enabled filter-counter expiry, new synchronized samples are shifted into the fSCL and fSDA histories. Because the shifted histories do not produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high, busy remains 0; this is the 'otherwise' side of REQ-0060's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the synchronizers, filter-counter expiration, and three-sample histories to predict each sample-shift event. At each predicted expiry, compare the observed history-update timing indirectly through busy and assert that busy remains unchanged when no filtered START is produced.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset with ena=1, drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 until the filter is settled, then change sda_i to 0 while keeping scl_i=1 and hold both inputs stable across the required synchronizer and filter-counter expiries.
elements.expected_response: When the enabled filter counter expires, new synchronized samples are shifted into fSCL and fSDA. Once the shifted histories produce filtered SDA changing from high to low while filtered SCL is high, busy rises to 1; this is the 'shows' side of REQ-0060's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Predict filter-counter expiries, synchronized samples, majority-filtered values, and the resulting filtered START with a reference model. On the expiry that produces the filtered START, compare busy after the clock edge and require it to transition from 0 to 1.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high, clk_cnt at a value allowing regular filter samples, and hold the external bus high with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. After filter histories are high, drive sda_i=0 while keeping scl_i=1 for at least two consecutive filter_sample_due events, then continue clocking until the filtered transition is processed.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the majority-filtered SDA changes from high to low while majority-filtered SCL remains high, and busy becomes high on the registered cycle that processes the resulting START condition.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to update the three-sample fSCL and fSDA histories at each filter_sample_due event and compute each filtered value as the 3-input majority. At the corresponding settled posedge, compare the predicted START-detection busy update with the DUT busy output.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high, clk_cnt and scl_i=1, and initialize the external bus with sda_i=1 until the filter histories are high. Drive sda_i=0 for only one filter-sample interval so that exactly one new low sample is shifted into fSDA, then return sda_i=1 before the next filter sample; continue clocking with no other bus activity.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: the single low sample does not create a majority-filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high, so busy remains unchanged and is not set.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to verify the fSDA history contains at most one low sample during the glitch and that its majority remains high. Compare the predicted absence of START detection against the DUT busy output after each settled posedge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, establish an idle bus with synchronized and filtered SCL high, filtered SDA high, and busy low. Apply an SDA low glitch on sda_i whose duration is shorter than the synchronized/filter sampling interval needed for two of the three SDA history samples to become low, then return sda_i high and allow synchronization and filtering to settle.
elements.expected_response: This is the requirement-holds case: the three-sample majority remains high, no filtered START condition is detected, and busy remains low. The short raw SDA glitch does not affect busy.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the two-stage SDA synchronizer, filter sampling schedule, three-sample majority, and filtered edge detector. At every settled clock edge compare the predicted filtered SDA, START detection, and registered busy output; require no busy assertion during or after the glitch.

elements.stimulus: After reset, establish an idle bus with synchronized and filtered SCL high, filtered SDA high, and busy low. Drive sda_i low continuously for enough enabled filter samples that at least two of the three SDA history samples become low, maintaining SCL high throughout; then allow the filtered transition and registered status update to occur.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting requirement-does-not-hold case: the majority-filtered SDA transitions high to low while filtered SCL is high, a filtered START condition is detected, and busy rises on the corresponding registered update.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to predict the synchronized samples, three-sample majority transition, START edge, and one-cycle registered busy-update latency. Compare the predicted filtered START event and busy assertion with the DUT trace, and require busy to remain low before the filtered transition and rise after it.

elements.stimulus: Apply no activation condition or functional stimulus; perform a requirements-to-testplan traceability review for the scaffolding item.
elements.expected_response: No DUT behavior, output value, timing relationship, or state transition is required by REQ-0063.
elements.check_method: Review the requirement text and normalized expectation, and confirm that the testbench contains no DUT assertion or functional check attributed to REQ-0063.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy=0, release both bus lines high and hold filtered SCL high. Drive sda_i high long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to establish filtered SDA high, then drive sda_i low and hold it long enough for filtered SDA to transition high-to-low while filtered SCL remains high; keep ena high and do not issue a command.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the filtered START condition sta_condition = ~sSDA & dSDA & sSCL is asserted, and busy rises to 1 on the registered detection update and remains asserted.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the two-stage synchronizers, filter sampling, three-sample majority values, and delayed filtered SDA edge. At the posedge processing the modeled filtered high-to-low SDA transition with filtered SCL high, compare busy against 1 and verify the transition is not attributed to a raw unfiltered edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy=0, hold sda_i high while filtered SCL is high for multiple filter intervals, with ena high and no command. Then optionally drive sda_i low only while filtered SCL is low, and hold the bus in that state without producing any filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: sta_condition is never asserted, so busy does not rise due to START detection and remains 0.
elements.check_method: Use the same synchronizer/filter reference model to confirm that no cycle has filtered SDA transitioning high-to-low concurrently with filtered SCL high. Sample busy after every posedge and flag any rise while the qualifying filtered START condition is absent.

elements.stimulus: After reset, with the DUT released and filtered SCL high, drive SDA high long enough to establish the filtered idle history, then drive SDA low and hold it while SCL remains high until the filtered START transition is detected and busy is 1. Next release SDA high while keeping SCL high, and hold both lines stable long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to produce a filtered SDA low-to-high transition.
elements.expected_response: When filtered SDA rises from low to high while filtered SCL is high, the STOP-condition observation is the holding side of the requirement: busy clears to 0 on the registered update following detection, providing evidence that the filtered STOP condition was detected.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter sampling, majority value, and filtered SDA edge detection. At the modeled filtered low-to-high SDA transition with filtered SCL high, compare the next settled posedge value of busy against 0 and require the transition to occur only after the filtered condition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, with the DUT released and filtered SCL high, drive SDA high long enough to establish the filtered idle history, then drive SDA low and hold it while SCL remains high until the filtered START transition is detected and busy is 1. Keep SDA low and SCL high for the same filtered observation interval used in the STOP test, without allowing SDA to rise from low to high.
elements.expected_response: When filtered SDA does not rise from low to high while filtered SCL is high, the contrasting side of the requirement applies: busy remains high and does not clear during the observation interval.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter and edge model to confirm that filtered SCL is high and no filtered SDA rising edge occurs. Sample busy after every settled posedge throughout the interval and require it to remain 1, with no STOP-induced clear.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, set ena=1, and hold the bus released with filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high. Drive SDA low while SCL remains high long enough for the synchronizer/filter reference model to produce a filtered START condition. Then keep the bus in the active state without a STOP for multiple enabled clocks, and finally drive SDA high while SCL remains high long enough to produce a filtered STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: The busy output is low before the filtered START, rises when the filtered START is detected, remains high throughout the interval after START and before the filtered STOP, and clears when the filtered STOP is detected.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the filtered SDA falling and rising transitions while filtered SCL is high; sample busy after each settled posedge and assert the required low-to-high hold-to-low sequence, with no low value between the modeled START and STOP events.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, set ena=1, and keep both filtered SCL and filtered SDA stably high for an interval covering multiple filter samples and clock-enable ticks. Optionally apply SDA disturbances shorter than the filter interval while filtered SCL remains high, ensuring the reference model reports no filtered START or STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: The busy output remains low throughout the interval because no qualifying filtered START occurs; it also remains low afterward because no filtered STOP is needed to clear it.
elements.check_method: Compare the reference model's filtered START/STOP event stream with the DUT busy output at every settled posedge; with no modeled qualifying event, assert busy is continuously low.

elements.check_method: Review the requirement trace and confirm that the element asserts no DUT output, timing, state, or protocol expectation beyond acknowledging the absence of a requirement.

elements.stimulus: Initialize with nReset asserted then deasserted, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1 while the bus is otherwise released. After the command reaches the WRITE released-high arbitration-check phase with sda_oen=1, externally drive sda_i=0 and hold it long enough for the synchronizer and majority filter to produce filtered SDA low.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in observed_via.shows: at the clock edge where filtered SDA is observed low during the released-high WRITE arbitration-check phase, al asserts high and remains asserted. The command is aborted and no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted WRITE.
elements.check_method: Use the write_stable_high_phase and sda_check_active probes to qualify the observation, model the synchronizer and three-sample majority filter to identify the filtered-SDA-low edge, then compare al after settled posedge sampling against a reference model. Verify al remains high on subsequent clocks until reset and that cmd_ack does not pulse.

elements.stimulus: Initialize with nReset asserted then deasserted, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1 while the bus is otherwise released. During the WRITE released-high arbitration-check phase, keep sda_oen=1 and externally leave sda_i=1 so the filtered SDA remains high throughout the arbitration-check event.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting otherwise case in observed_via.shows: al does not assert for this arbitration-check event when filtered SDA is not low. The WRITE continues through its normal low phase and completes with one cmd_ack pulse, absent any other error.
elements.check_method: Use write_stable_high_phase and sda_check_active to qualify the arbitration-check phase, verify via the filter reference model that filtered SDA stays high, and compare al and cmd_ack after each settled posedge against the expected normal WRITE behavior. Confirm al remains low through completion.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high and clk_cnt at 4 with the bus released high, then accept a READ command. During the READ command's released-SCL/high phase and before command completion, externally drive SDA low while filtered SCL is high, hold it long enough to pass the input filter, then release SDA high and hold it long enough to produce a filtered STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of REQ-0070: al asserts on the registered update that processes the filtered STOP condition, the active READ command aborts without cmd_ack, and both scl_oen and sda_oen are released.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for command acceptance, synchronizer/filter latency, and filtered STOP detection. At the filtered STOP event while in the active READ sequence, compare the post-posedge al value against 1 and verify no cmd_ack pulse occurs for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high and clk_cnt at 4 with the bus released high, then accept a requested STOP command while idle. Allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL, and release SDA while filtered SCL is high so that the command produces its normal filtered STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case of REQ-0070: when the filtered STOP condition occurs for the requested STOP command, al does not newly assert; the STOP command completes with its one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to identify the requested STOP command and its filtered STOP event. Confirm al remains 0 across that event and compare cmd_ack against a single-cycle completion pulse after the STOP terminal phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a WRITE command with din=1. Allow the command to reach its released-high WRITE phase, then externally hold SDA low while SCL is released high. Continue clocking until the registered arbitration-loss response occurs.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: al asserts, the command FSM returns to idle, and at the registered response both scl_oen and sda_oen are high, releasing SCL and SDA. This is the 'scl_oen is high, releasing SCL' and 'sda_oen is high, releasing SDA' side of the observed-via shows.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after outputs settle, monitor al, in_idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen. When al first rises, require in_idle=1 and scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 before any subsequent command activity; also require that no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a WRITE command with din=0. Keep the external SDA and SCL lines released high whenever the DUT releases them, and do not inject an unexpected STOP or arbitration conflict. Observe an active WRITE low phase before command completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: no arbitration-loss response occurs; al remains low, the FSM remains active rather than being forced to idle, and during the driven WRITE low phase the output enables follow the ordinary WRITE behavior rather than both being released as the arbitration-loss response. In particular, scl_oen=0 and sda_oen=0 during that driven low phase, so the 'scl_oen does not become high' and 'sda_oen does not become high' sides of the observed-via shows apply.
elements.check_method: Use in_write_sequence and command_active to identify the ordinary driven low phase. Sample al, in_idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen after each settled posedge; require al=0 and in_idle=0 during the phase, require scl_oen=0 and sda_oen=0 there, and then verify the command proceeds to its normal completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue cmd=READ while idle and wait until the READ data-sampling window releases SCL. Hold the external SDA line high and drive SCL low, then high long enough for the reference filter model to produce one filtered SCL rising edge before cmd_ack or any abort.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: on the filtered SCL rising edge during the READ sampling window, dout updates to 1, the filtered SDA value, with the specified registered observation timing.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to predict synchronizer, majority-filter, and filtered SCL edge timing. At the modeled filtered rising edge, compare dout after the corresponding posedge to 1 and verify the update occurs before cmd_ack or an abort.

elements.stimulus: Complete a READ operation that captures filtered SDA=1 to establish dout=1. Issue a second enabled cmd=READ, wait for its READ data-sampling window, hold external SDA low, and drive SCL from low to high long enough for the reference filter model to produce one filtered SCL rising edge before cmd_ack or any abort.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: on the filtered SCL rising edge during the READ sampling window, dout updates from 1 to 0, the filtered SDA value, with the specified registered observation timing.
elements.check_method: Model the two-stage synchronization, three-sample majority filtering, and filtered SCL rising-edge detection. On the second READ edge, compare dout after the corresponding posedge against filtered SDA=0 and verify the change occurs before cmd_ack or an abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset, leave the controller idle with ena=1 and cmd=NOP. Set external SDA high and drive SCL from low to high long enough for the reference filter model to produce a filtered SCL rising edge, without issuing READ or another active command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: because no READ data-sampling window is active, dout does not capture the filtered SDA value for this filtered SCL rising edge and remains at its reset value of 0.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter model to identify the filtered SCL rising edge, then compare dout before and after the corresponding posedge; require no dout update, no cmd_ack, and the idle probe to remain asserted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=1000 (READ) while the bus is released. During the READ data-sampling window, drive filtered SDA to 0 and produce a filtered SCL rising edge, then drive filtered SDA to 1 and produce a second filtered SCL rising edge before allowing the READ command to complete.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: on each filtered SCL rising edge in the READ sampling window, dout updates on the corresponding clocked observation to the received filtered SDA bit: 0 for the first edge and 1 for the second edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronization, filtering, and filtered-SCL edge timing; at every qualifying filtered SCL rising edge, compare dout after the registered update with the modeled filtered SDA value and record a coverage bin for each sampled bit value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=1000 (READ) with ena=1, keep filtered SCL low throughout the READ data-sampling window, and toggle the external SDA input so that filtered SDA changes without producing a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: NON-HOLDING CASE: at each clock while no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout does not carry a newly sampled READ data bit and remains at its previously registered value, despite changes on filtered SDA.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the absence of filtered-SCL rising edges; compare dout on every subsequent clock against its prior value and flag any update not coincident with a qualifying READ sampling edge.

elements.stimulus: No DUT stimulus; review the requirement and testplan traceability entry for the list-item marker "10.".
