elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep the filtered bus released-high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, then issue a supported START command while the command FSM is idle. Continue clocking with ena=1 until multiple clk_en_tick opportunities occur, including the expected START phase boundaries.
elements.expected_response: This is the clk_en-present side of the observed_via shows: at each command-phase boundary where clk_en_tick is asserted, the active START sequence advances and the registered scl_oen or sda_oen changes to the next required START phase after the corresponding clocked update. No phase transition occurs without a corresponding clk_en_tick.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to predict clk_en_tick and START phase boundaries. At every posedge, compare the settled registered scl_oen/sda_oen values with the model and assert that every phase transition is associated with clk_en_tick=1.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep the filtered bus released-high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, then issue a supported START command while idle. After command acceptance and before the next reference-model clk_en_tick, hold all command and bus inputs stable and sample several posedges; repeat the observation between successive clk_en_tick opportunities.
elements.expected_response: This is the no-clk_en side of the observed_via shows: scl_oen holds its prior registered value on every clock between clk_en opportunities, with no premature SCL phase transition and no advancement to the next START phase. The phase may change only on a later posedge that processes clk_en_tick.
elements.check_method: Track clk_en_tick from the divider reference model and compare consecutive settled scl_oen values. Assert scl_oen is unchanged for every posedge with clk_en_tick=0, and permit a transition only on a posedge with clk_en_tick=1.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so the command FSM is idle, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, drive cmd=START (0001), and provide a released-high bus. Hold these inputs through an enabled acceptance tick.
elements.expected_response: On the acceptance tick the FSM enters the START sequence: sda_oen becomes 0 while scl_oen remains 1, followed by the normal START sequence and eventual cmd_ack pulse unless reset or arbitration loss is injected.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after NBA settling, assert the idle-to-START transition using the in_idle and in_start_sequence probes and compare sda_oen=0 with scl_oen=1 during START entry; verify exactly one terminal cmd_ack pulse with a reference FSM model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so the command FSM is idle, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, drive cmd=STOP (0010), and provide a released-high bus. Hold these inputs through an enabled acceptance tick.
elements.expected_response: On the acceptance tick the FSM enters the STOP sequence: SDA is driven low before SCL is released high, followed by the normal STOP sequence and eventual cmd_ack pulse unless reset or arbitration loss is injected.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle and in_stop_sequence probes to identify acceptance, then scoreboard the ordered output-enable phases, requiring sda_oen=0 before scl_oen=1, and verify the reference model predicts one terminal cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so the command FSM is idle, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, drive cmd=READ (1000), and allow the external bus to remain high with no clock stretching. Hold these inputs through an enabled acceptance tick.
elements.expected_response: On the acceptance tick the FSM enters the READ sequence: scl_oen is released to 1 for the READ window and later becomes 0 for the low phase, followed by the normal completion cmd_ack pulse unless reset or arbitration loss is injected.
elements.check_method: Correlate the in_idle-to-in_read_sequence probe transition with the ordered scl_oen=1 then scl_oen=0 phases and compare completion timing and one-cycle cmd_ack against a variable-latency reference model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so the command FSM is idle, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, drive cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=0, and provide a released-high bus with no arbitration loss. Hold these inputs through an enabled acceptance tick.
elements.expected_response: On the acceptance tick the FSM enters the WRITE sequence, performs its SDA/SCL bit phases, and terminates with exactly one cmd_ack pulse unless reset or arbitration loss is injected.
elements.check_method: Use in_idle and in_write_sequence to confirm the selected sequence, monitor sda_oen and scl_oen phase ordering, and compare the terminal one-cycle cmd_ack against the reference command-decode and FSM model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so the command FSM is idle, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, drive unsupported cmd=0011, and hold the command through multiple enabled acceptance ticks while the bus remains released high.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case: the FSM remains idle, no START, STOP, READ, or WRITE sequence begins, the output enables remain in the idle released state, and cmd_ack is never asserted.
elements.check_method: At every enabled tick, assert in_idle remains high and in_start_sequence, in_stop_sequence, in_read_sequence, and in_write_sequence remain low; scoreboard scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, and cmd_ack=0 against the reference decoder.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, clk_cnt=16'd1, and both external bus lines released high. While in idle, present cmd=4'b0001 (START) on an enabled timing tick, then keep cmd at NOP until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after command acceptance, scl_oen and sda_oen show the START phase sequence: both released initially, SDA driven low while SCL remains released, then SCL driven low. The sequence completes with exactly one cmd_ack pulse; sda_check_active remains inactive for the START sequence.
elements.check_method: At every clk_en_tick, compare the registered scl_oen and sda_oen waveform against the START reference-model phase sequence, accounting for one clock of output-register latency. Check that the phase order completes before cmd_ack and sample sda_check_active during each phase.

elements.stimulus: Establish a busy transaction context, keep ena=1, clk_cnt=16'd1, and the external bus released high except when driven by the DUT. From idle, present cmd=4'b0010 (STOP) on an enabled timing tick, then keep cmd at NOP until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen and sda_oen show the STOP phase sequence: SDA is driven low, SCL is released and allowed to go high, then SDA is released while SCL is high. The sequence completes with exactly one cmd_ack pulse; sda_check_active is inactive.
elements.check_method: Use a phase-aware reference model sampled after each posedge to compare scl_oen and sda_oen at every clk_en_tick, including the required high-SCL wait before SDA release. Verify the final phase precedes the single cmd_ack pulse and inspect sda_check_active.

elements.stimulus: Keep ena=1, clk_cnt=16'd1, and provide a released-high SCL bus. From idle, present cmd=4'b1000 (READ) on an enabled timing tick. Return SDA first low and then high on successive filtered SCL rising edges, and allow the command to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: throughout READ, sda_oen remains released for the read window, scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase, and scl_oen drives SCL low for the following low phase while SDA remains released. The command completes with one cmd_ack pulse; sda_check_active remains inactive.
elements.check_method: Drive the external bus through the synchronization and filter model, then compare registered scl_oen and sda_oen against the READ phase sequence at each clk_en_tick and filtered SCL edge. Verify output values before cmd_ack and check that sda_check_active is never asserted.

elements.stimulus: Keep ena=1, clk_cnt=16'd1, and the external SCL line released high. From idle, present cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) with din=1 on an enabled timing tick; keep SDA externally released high and keep cmd at NOP until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: WRITE drives SDA released for the data-high bit, releases SCL during the stable high phase, asserts sda_check_active during that released high phase, then drives SCL low while retaining the SDA phase value. The command completes with exactly one cmd_ack and no al.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen and sda_oen after each posedge against the WRITE(din=1) reference waveform, checking the stable-high phase and its ordering relative to the SCL-low phase. Check sda_check_active is asserted only in the released stable-high phase, and verify cmd_ack occurs once without al.

elements.stimulus: Keep ena=1, clk_cnt=16'd1, and the external SCL line released high. From idle, present cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) with din=0 on an enabled timing tick; keep SDA externally released or driven low by the bus and keep cmd at NOP until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: WRITE drives SDA low for the data-low bit, releases SCL during the high phase without enabling SDA arbitration checking, then drives SCL low while SDA remains driven low. The command completes with exactly one cmd_ack and no al.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen and sda_oen at each clk_en_tick against the WRITE(din=0) phase model. Verify sda_check_active remains inactive despite SDA being low, and check the phase ordering, single cmd_ack pulse, and absence of al.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'd1 while the controller is idle. Apply cmd=4'b0000 and then each unsupported encoding 4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111, 4'b1001, 4'b1010, 4'b1011, 4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, and 4'b1111 for an enabled timing tick, with cmd returned to NOP between trials.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-activation case: because no supported command sequence is entered, scl_oen and sda_oen remain at the released idle pair (1,1); they do not take any START, STOP, READ, or WRITE phase-specific values. No cmd_ack is generated and sda_check_active remains inactive.
elements.check_method: For each command trial, monitor in_idle and compare scl_oen/sda_oen on every clock against the released idle value. Confirm no command-sequence probe asserts, no phase-specific output transition occurs, no sda_check_active assertion occurs, and no cmd_ack pulse is emitted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, present cmd=START while the filtered bus is released high, and hold the command until it is accepted. Allow the START sequence to execute without reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: after the START terminal phase, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock cycle, then deasserts on the next clock.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare cmd_ack against a reference FSM completion event and count consecutive asserted cycles; require one and only one asserted cycle at terminal completion, followed by in_idle=1 and cmd_ack=0. Record a completion bin for START.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, present cmd=STOP while idle with the bus released high, and hold the command until it is accepted. Allow the STOP sequence to execute without reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: after the STOP terminal phase, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock cycle, then deasserts on the next clock.
elements.check_method: Use the reference command-sequence model to identify STOP completion; sample registered outputs after each posedge and require exactly one cmd_ack cycle coincident with completion, followed by in_idle=1 and no further cmd_ack. Record a completion bin for STOP.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, present cmd=WRITE with din=0 while the external bus permits every phase, and hold the command until accepted. Allow the complete WRITE sequence to run without reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: at the WRITE terminal completion phase, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock cycle; cmd_ack is low on both neighboring clocks.
elements.check_method: Predict variable phase progression with a reference model, then compare the registered cmd_ack waveform at each posedge; assert a one-cycle pulse at predicted completion and in_idle=1 after completion. Record a completion bin for WRITE.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, present cmd=READ while the external device returns a stable SDA value and permits SCL to rise, and hold the command until accepted. Allow the complete READ sequence to run without reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: after the READ low-phase terminal completion, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock cycle, then is low on the next clock.
elements.check_method: Model filtered SCL rising-edge capture and READ phase completion; compare cmd_ack after settled posedges and require exactly one completion pulse with no duplicate or stretched assertion, followed by in_idle=1. Record a completion bin for READ.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and start a supported WRITE with din=1 and clk_cnt=0. During its released high phase, externally hold SDA low to force arbitration loss before the terminal completion phase.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise side of shows: because the command does not reach its terminal completion phase, cmd_ack does not pulse; the command aborts and the FSM returns to idle with both output enables released.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the arbitration-loss abort edge; assert al becomes set, command_active ends, in_idle becomes true, and cmd_ack remains 0 throughout the abort and subsequent idle cycles. Flag any cmd_ack assertion as a failure.

elements.stimulus: Apply no DUT stimulus; inspect the requirement database and generated verification plan entry for Item 11.

elements.check_method: Review the traceability record and confirm the item is classified as scaffolding with no observable behavior and is not used to create a DUT assertion or waveform expectation.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release nReset and rst, hold scl_i and sda_i high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue cmd=4'b0001 (START) while the command FSM is idle. Keep ena high and the bus released until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed_via shows: during the START sequence, scl_oen is high during the initial release and SDA-low-while-SCL-high phases, then becomes low for the final SCL-low phase. sda_oen is high during the initial release phase, then becomes low while scl_oen remains high and the filtered SCL is high. After SCL is pulled low, cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock and then returns low.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, use a temporal scoreboard to verify the ordered phases: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 first; then scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=0 with filtered SCL high; then scl_oen=0; then cmd_ack=1 for one clock only. Assert that no cmd_ack occurs before the final SCL-low phase.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release nReset and rst, hold scl_i and sda_i high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, and keep the command FSM idle while issuing cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) for several enabled clocks; do not issue cmd=4'b0001.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding side of the observed_via shows: scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the idle released state rather than exhibiting the START released-then-pulled-low sequence, and cmd_ack remains low because no START sequence completes.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack after each settled posedge for the full observation window. Compare against the idle reference: scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, and cmd_ack=0 throughout; assert that no SDA-low phase followed by SCL-low phase occurs.

elements.stimulus: Review the specification item corresponding to list item 12; do not apply a DUT stimulus because the item defines no required behavior.
elements.expected_response: No DUT output, state transition, timing property, or interface behavior is required by REQ-0081.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high, rst low, ena high, and the bus in an active transaction state, issue cmd=0010 (STOP) on a clock edge and keep the external SCL and SDA lines released high. Allow the STOP command to progress without clock stretching.
elements.expected_response: The STOP sequence first drives SDA low (sda_oen=0), then releases SCL high (scl_oen=1) while SDA remains driven low, and finally releases SDA high (sda_oen=1) while scl_oen remains 1. This is the holding case of REQ-0082: scl_oen releases after the SDA-low phase, and sda_oen transitions from driven low to released high during the final phase.
elements.check_method: Use a temporal waveform assertion sampled after each posedge: after STOP acceptance, observe sda_oen=0; before sda_oen becomes 1, require scl_oen=1; when sda_oen becomes 1, require scl_oen=1 and require the ordering sda_oen:0->1 after scl_oen:0->1. Fail if SDA is released before SCL or if SCL is not released before the final SDA release.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high, rst low, ena high, and the bus in an active transaction state, issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=0 instead of cmd=0010, and allow the command to complete with no arbitration loss or clock stretching.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case: because a STOP command is not executed, the DUT shall not produce the STOP-specific sequence of driving SDA low, releasing SCL, and then releasing SDA while SCL is high. The observed scl_oen and sda_oen waveform shall follow WRITE behavior rather than the REQ-0082 STOP ordering; in particular, no final SDA release shall be attributed to a STOP phase.
elements.check_method: Classify the output-enable waveform from command acceptance through cmd_ack and compare it with the WRITE reference model. Assert that no STOP sequence signature occurs: there is no ordered pattern of sda_oen=0 followed by scl_oen=1 followed by sda_oen=1 while scl_oen remains 1, unless that pattern is independently required by the WRITE model. Check command identity and phase probes to ensure the comparison is made only for the non-STOP command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive a released-high bus. Issue cmd=0001 (START), wait for its completion, then from idle issue cmd=0010 (STOP). Allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL, observe filtered SCL high, and then release SDA while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: immediately after the terminal STOP phase releases SDA high while SCL is high, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock and then deasserts.
elements.check_method: Use a reference FSM to identify the STOP terminal phase and compare the registered cmd_ack waveform on each posedge; assert that cmd_ack is high on the completion clock only and is low on the following clock.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=0010 (STOP) from idle, then assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the STOP sequence reaches the phase that releases SDA high while SCL is high. Hold reset active for at least one clock, then release it without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: the STOP sequence is aborted before its terminal phase, so cmd_ack does not assert for that aborted STOP command.
elements.check_method: Monitor the STOP sequence probe and the asynchronous reset edge; verify that no cmd_ack pulse occurs from the aborted command between command acceptance and reset, or after reset release until a new command is issued.

elements.stimulus: Review Item 13 of the implementation-details list and inspect the generated verification obligations for REQ-0084.
elements.expected_response: No DUT stimulus, behavioral expectation, interface check, or functional coverage obligation is generated for Item 13 because the item states no requirement.
elements.check_method: Perform a requirements-traceability and testplan-lint comparison confirming REQ-0084 is represented only by this no-obligation audit element and that no DUT behavior is asserted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=4'b1000 for READ while the bus is released high. Allow the READ sequence to reach its SDA release/data-bit window, keep the external SDA participant free to drive either value, and continue until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the READ data-bit window after entry into the SDA release phase and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is high. This is the holding side of the observed behavior: SDA is released so the slave can drive the data bit.
elements.check_method: Use the in_read_sequence probe and the READ data-window phase to qualify a sampled assertion that sda_oen remains 1 on every clock before cmd_ack; bin the READ release phase and flag any low sample.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=4'b1000 with ena=1 and reach the READ SDA release/data-bit window. Apply a verification fault override or equivalent mutation that forces the observed sda_oen output low during this window, then allow the sequence to continue toward cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: sda_oen low during the READ data-bit window is the contrasting otherwise side of the observed behavior: it drives SDA rather than releasing it. The checker must report this as a failure of REQ-0085@1; an unmutated DUT must never produce this response.
elements.check_method: Monitor sda_oen while in_read_sequence is active in the data-bit window and assert that no low value is observed; confirm the injected low value is detected and attributed to REQ-0085@1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt to a nonzero value, hold scl_i and sda_i high unless the DUT drives them low, and issue cmd=READ (1000) while the command FSM is idle. Allow the READ command to progress into its SCL sample window without asserting reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: The holding side of shows is observed: during the READ SCL sample window, scl_oen becomes and remains 1, releasing SCL high, and after the sample window it transitions to 0 to drive SCL low again. sda_oen remains 1 during the sample window.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk after registered outputs settle, use the in_read_sequence and filtered-SCL phase probes to identify the READ sample window. Assert that scl_oen is 1 throughout that window, then compare the first subsequent low-phase transition and require scl_oen=0. Record coverage for both the release and subsequent drive-low transitions.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt to a nonzero value, issue cmd=READ (1000) while idle, and wait until the READ SCL sample window is active with scl_oen=1. Then assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the normal transition that drives SCL low; release nReset and do not issue a new command.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting side of shows is observed: because the active READ sequence is aborted by reset, scl_oen does not remain released high through a completed READ sample window followed by the normal drive-low transition. Instead, reset immediately initializes the output-enable state to released, with scl_oen=1, and no READ low-phase completion or cmd_ack is produced.
elements.check_method: Detect the sample window using in_read_sequence and scl_oen=1, inject nReset between clocks, and check asynchronously and on the next clock that the FSM is idle, cmd_ack is low, and the normal READ transition to scl_oen=0 does not occur. Classify the result as the non-holding/abort side of the observed-via difference.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (1000) while the bus is released. Drive the external bus so filtered SDA is stable at 0 during the READ data-bit phase, then produce a filtered SCL rising edge and hold the value through that edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: during the READ data-bit phase, dout updates on the clock processing the filtered SCL rising edge to the filtered SDA value 0, and remains 0 until another qualifying filtered SCL rising edge or reset.
elements.check_method: Use the filter and edge-detection reference model to identify the filtered SCL rising edge; sample dout after the corresponding posedge and compare it with the modeled filtered SDA value. Confirm the update occurs only once for that edge.

elements.stimulus: Complete a READ data-bit sample with filtered SDA=0 and a filtered SCL rising edge so dout becomes 0. Then, while the READ operation remains active and filtered SCL stays low with no further filtered SCL rising edge, change the external SDA so the filtered SDA becomes 1.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case of shows: dout does not update to the new filtered SDA value 1 without a filtered SCL rising edge; it holds its previously captured value 0.
elements.check_method: Track filtered SCL edges and filtered SDA with the reference model, then compare dout after each posedge during the SDA change. Require no dout transition on the SDA change alone and no update until a subsequent modeled filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and issue cmd=1000 (READ) while the bus is released high. Allow the READ sequence to release SDA and SCL, drive a valid sampled read bit on SDA, allow filtered SCL to rise and capture the bit, then allow the final filtered SCL low phase to complete without stretching or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at the terminal READ phase, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock, indicating that the READ command ends; cmd_ack is low on the preceding and following clocks.
elements.check_method: Use the READ reference model and filtered-SCL edge probes to identify read-bit capture and completion of the final low phase; compare the registered cmd_ack waveform against a single-cycle pulse beginning after terminal-phase recognition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and issue cmd=1000 (READ) while the bus is released high. During the active READ sequence, before the final low phase completes, drive filtered SDA from low to high while filtered SCL is high to inject an unexpected STOP and cause arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: cmd_ack does not pulse at the terminal READ phase because the READ command is aborted before completion; al asserts and the controller returns idle with both output enables released.
elements.check_method: Use filtered SDA/SCL transition probes to confirm the injected STOP occurs during the active READ sequence, then assert that al becomes set, no cmd_ack high cycle occurs from command issue through abort, and no later terminal READ acknowledgment is emitted without a new command.

elements.stimulus: Apply no command or state-specific stimulus beyond normal reset initialization and leave the DUT otherwise unconstrained.
elements.expected_response: No requirement-specific DUT response is expected because list item 14 defines no substantive behavior.
elements.check_method: Record the scenario as a coverage bin and confirm that no additional observable assertion is associated with REQ-0089.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, then apply rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=0, and a released-high external bus. Issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) on a rising clock while the controller is idle; keep scl_i and sda_i high and do not assert reset or arbitration loss until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: This is the din=0 side of the required sda_oen behavior: during WRITE data setup and throughout the corresponding stable SCL-high phase, sda_oen is 0, driving SDA low. The controller then releases SCL with scl_oen=1 for the high phase, enables SDA arbitration checking during that high phase, and subsequently pulls SCL low with scl_oen=0 before producing the WRITE completion acknowledgment.
elements.check_method: Use the in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and sda_check_active probes to delimit the WRITE phases. At settled post-posedge samples, assert sda_oen=0 before and throughout the stable high phase, record an ordered scl_oen transition 0-to-1-to-0, and verify the final transition occurs after the released high phase and before cmd_ack. Add a bin for the din=0 case and compare the observed sequence against a cycle-accurate reference model.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, then apply rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=1, and a released-high external bus. Issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) on a rising clock while the controller is idle; keep scl_i and sda_i high so arbitration is not lost, and do not assert reset until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting din=1 side of the required sda_oen behavior: during WRITE data setup and throughout the corresponding stable SCL-high phase, sda_oen is 1, releasing SDA. The controller releases SCL with scl_oen=1 for the high phase, enables SDA arbitration checking during that high phase, and subsequently pulls SCL low with scl_oen=0 before producing the WRITE completion acknowledgment.
elements.check_method: Use the in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and sda_check_active probes to delimit the WRITE phases. At settled post-posedge samples, assert sda_oen=1 before and throughout the stable high phase, record an ordered scl_oen transition 0-to-1-to-0, verify arbitration checking is active while SDA is released, and verify the final transition occurs before cmd_ack with al remaining 0. Add a bin for the din=1 contrast case and compare the sequence against a cycle-accurate reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) while idle. Drive the external bus released-high except for the DUT's intentional open-drain actions, hold din at either 0 or 1, and allow the WRITE sequence to complete without arbitration loss or reset.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of REQ-0091: after the WRITE sequence performs its data and SCL phases, cmd_ack asserts high for exactly one clock to indicate that the WRITE command has ended, then returns low.
elements.check_method: Use the in_write_sequence and command_active probes to identify the terminal WRITE phase; compare cmd_ack against a reference FSM and assert that exactly one sampled posedge has cmd_ack=1 after command acceptance, with no additional pulse while idle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) while idle with din=1. During the released, stable-high WRITE phase, externally drive SDA low so filtered SDA is low while the DUT expects SDA high; do not assert either reset input.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of REQ-0091: arbitration loss aborts the WRITE before normal completion, so cmd_ack does not assert for that command; al asserts and the controller releases both output lines.
elements.check_method: With write_stable_high_phase or sda_check_active asserted, verify the reference arbitration condition and then check that al rises, cmd_ack remains low for the aborted command, and sda_oen and scl_oen indicate released lines; flag any completion pulse as a failure.

elements.stimulus: Instantiate the DUT and execute the standard testbench initialization without applying any requirement-specific stimulus.
elements.expected_response: No output behavior is required or asserted for this requirement.
elements.check_method: Record the test as a coverage-only item and perform no functional comparison; confirm the requirement remains classified as having no observable expectation.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high, ena high, clk_cnt nonzero, and the bus released high, start a command sequence that makes the FSM active and drives or releases the output enables; then assert nReset low asynchronously between clk rising edges and hold it low without waiting for a clock.
elements.expected_response: This is the reset side of the observed port differences: immediately during asynchronous nReset assertion, the FSM returns to idle, scl_oen and sda_oen become high to release both lines, and cmd_ack, al, and busy are low. The reset values remain in effect while nReset is low. Counters and filter state are reset, with filtered SCL and SDA initialized high.
elements.check_method: Monitor outputs immediately after the asynchronous nReset transition, independent of clk, and continuously while reset is held. Check scl_oen==1, sda_oen==1, cmd_ack==0, al==0, busy==0, and the idle/reset state in the reference model; verify no command acknowledgement or output-enable activity occurs during reset.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset high and ena high, provide a released-high bus, issue a START command and then a normal WRITE command with din=0; allow the command phases and completion to occur, and do not assert either reset input.
elements.expected_response: This is the outside-reset side of the observed port differences: scl_oen and sda_oen follow the active command phases and are not forced high (the START/WRITE sequence drives the required low phases and releases the lines in high phases); cmd_ack is low except for the normal one-clock completion pulse; al remains low because no arbitration loss is injected; and busy becomes high after the filtered START and remains asserted until a STOP is detected. These ordinary non-reset values contrast with the unconditional reset values.
elements.check_method: Use a clocking-block or post-NBA monitor to compare the registered outputs against a transaction reference model on every posedge. Check the output-enable polarity and phase sequence, detect exactly one cmd_ack pulse at command completion, verify busy asserts on the filtered START, and verify al remains low throughout the successful transaction.

elements.stimulus: Asynchronously initialize the DUT, deassert nReset, set ena=1 and a valid clk_cnt, issue a START or WRITE command, and wait until the command FSM is active. Assert rst=1 before a rising edge of clk and keep it asserted through that edge.
elements.expected_response: At the first rising edge of clk while rst=1, the synchronous reset side of the observed behavior holds: the FSM returns to idle, scl_oen and sda_oen are high, and cmd_ack, al, and busy are low.
elements.check_method: At the reset rising edge, sample registered outputs after nonblocking assignments settle and compare scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, cmd_ack=0, al=0, and busy=0 against the reset reference model; also confirm in_idle is asserted and command_active is deasserted.

elements.stimulus: Asynchronously initialize the DUT, deassert nReset, set ena=1 and a valid clk_cnt, issue a WRITE command with din=0, and wait until the command FSM is in its active WRITE sequence. Keep rst=0 for the next rising edge of clk and do not issue a reset.
elements.expected_response: At that rising edge, the contrasting non-reset side of the observed behavior holds: synchronous reset is not applied, so the active command's ordinary output behavior continues rather than forcing the reset vector; in particular, the WRITE phase retains its commanded SDA ownership and the active transaction is not synchronously returned to idle.
elements.check_method: Use the command-sequence probe and bus model at the sampled rising edge to confirm rst=0, command_active=1, and the ordinary WRITE output-enable state (sda_oen=0 when the WRITE phase drives din=0), with no reset-induced simultaneous vector scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, cmd_ack=0, al=0, busy=0. Compare against the non-reset reference model.

elements.stimulus: Provide the complete module specification document to the verification artifact checker.
elements.expected_response: The specification identifies a section named exactly "Processing Flow" for the i2c_master_bit_ctrl module.
elements.check_method: Parse the specification text and assert that the required section heading or label "Processing Flow" is present in the module's documented processing-flow section.

elements.stimulus: While clk is running, assert nReset low asynchronously between clock edges and hold it low for at least one clock period; drive cmd to START, ena high, clk_cnt to 0, and keep scl_i and sda_i released high.
elements.expected_response: During the asserted-reset window, cmd_ack remains low, busy and al remain low, scl_oen and sda_oen are high, and the controller is initialized in idle; this is the reset-initialization side of the observation.
elements.check_method: Sample outputs immediately after nReset assertion and after subsequent posedges; compare against reset-value assertions and confirm in_idle is true and no cmd_ack pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: Release nReset, then assert rst high synchronously for a rising edge while clk is running; hold rst high through that edge with cmd set to START and ena high, then deassert rst.
elements.expected_response: At the rising edge with rst asserted, cmd_ack is low, busy and al are low, scl_oen and sda_oen are high, and the controller returns to initialized idle; this is the synchronous reset-initialization side of the observation.
elements.check_method: Sample registered outputs after the reset edge and verify reset values, in_idle, and absence of cmd_ack; also verify nReset low asynchronously has priority if asserted simultaneously.

elements.stimulus: After completing reset and releasing both reset inputs, keep ena high, drive a released-high bus, issue a valid START command while idle, and wait through the variable prescaler and START sequence until command completion.
elements.expected_response: After reset release, the outputs are governed by normal command processing rather than being newly forced to reset-initialization values: the START sequence changes the output-enable state as required and produces one cmd_ack pulse at completion; this is the contrasting post-reset side of the observation.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to allow variable completion latency, verify the FSM leaves idle and later returns to idle, and assert that cmd_ack is a one-clock pulse associated with START completion rather than permanently low.

elements.stimulus: First operate the controller sufficiently to make at least one status or output-enable non-idle, then assert nReset low between clk rising edges and hold it low for at least one clock period.
elements.expected_response: At asynchronous nReset assertion, the module returns to the reset-held idle state: cmd_ack, busy, and al are low, while scl_oen and sda_oen are high, releasing both bus lines. This is the holding side of the requirement's shows statements.
elements.check_method: Use an asynchronous assertion monitor to sample outputs immediately after nReset falls, then sample after the next clk edge; compare cmd_ack==0, busy==0, al==0, scl_oen==1, and sda_oen==1 against the reset reference model.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, first issue a command or otherwise drive the controller into non-idle activity, then drive rst high so that it is sampled on a rising edge of clk and hold rst high for at least one additional rising edge.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge that samples rst high, the module returns to the synchronous-reset idle state: cmd_ack, busy, and al become low, and scl_oen and sda_oen become high, releasing SCL and SDA. These are the holding-side values of the requirement's shows statements.
elements.check_method: At the rst sampling edge and the following settled clock state, compare the registered outputs with the reset reference model: cmd_ack==0, busy==0, al==0, scl_oen==1, and sda_oen==1. Confirm the transition occurs synchronously rather than at rst assertion between edges.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset high and rst low, set ena high and clk_cnt to 0, hold the external SCL and SDA bus high, and issue a START command while the controller is idle; continue clocking until the START sequence reaches its SDA-low phase.
elements.expected_response: When reset is not asserted, ordinary command behavior is allowed to differ from the reset-held values: the START sequence leaves idle, sda_oen becomes low to drive SDA low, and busy becomes high after the filtered START condition is detected. This is the contrasting, non-reset side of the requirement's shows statements; cmd_ack and al remain governed by normal command behavior rather than being forced to reset values.
elements.check_method: Use the command/FSM reference model to identify START acceptance and the filtered START event. At the corresponding settled clock edges, check that the observed sda_oen or busy differs from its reset-held value (sda_oen==0 during START or busy==1 after START detection), while reset inputs remain deasserted.

elements.stimulus: Release the DUT from reset, issue a WRITE command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, and before the command completes assert nReset=0 between two rising edges of clk. Keep nReset low for at least one clock, with rst=0.
elements.expected_response: Immediately when nReset is asserted, and throughout the assertion, the FSM returns to idle; cmd_ack, al, and busy are low; scl_oen and sda_oen are high, releasing both lines; arbitration checking is disabled; timing and filter counters are reset or reloaded; and the filtered SCL/SDA values are initialized high. This is the reset side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use asynchronous event checks for cmd_ack, al, busy, scl_oen, and sda_oen without waiting for clk. After the next settled clock, compare in_idle=1, sda_check_active=0, filtered_scl_high=1, filtered_sda_high=1, cnt_nonzero=0 or the specified reload state, and filter_sample_due=0 against a reset reference model.

elements.stimulus: Start from an active WRITE or READ operation with ena=1 and at least one status/output-enable value different from its idle reset value. Assert rst=1 coincident with a rising edge of clk while nReset remains high, then hold rst high for one additional rising edge before deasserting it.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge where rst is high, the FSM synchronously returns to idle; cmd_ack, al, and busy are cleared; scl_oen and sda_oen become high on the reset update, releasing SCL and SDA; arbitration checking is disabled; counters are reset or reloaded; and filtered SCL/SDA are initialized to high. No command-completion pulse is generated by the aborted operation. This is the reset side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample registered outputs after nonblocking assignments at each rising edge. Compare cmd_ack=0, al=0, busy=0, scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, in_idle=1, sda_check_active=0, filtered_scl_high=1, filtered_sda_high=1, and reset/reload counter probes with the synchronous-reset reference model; verify no delayed ack after rst is released.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset=1 and rst=0. With ena=1, issue a WRITE command with din=0 and clk_cnt=1 on an idle-high bus, and observe a stable active WRITE phase before allowing completion.
elements.expected_response: Outside reset, the ordinary active-command behavior is observed instead of the reset values: command_active and in_write_sequence are asserted, sda_oen is low while transmitting din=0, and the FSM is not idle; cmd_ack remains low until the terminal phase. This is the contrasting, non-reset side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: At settled rising-edge samples, require command_active=1 and in_write_sequence=1, sda_oen=0, and in_idle=0 during the selected WRITE phase; require cmd_ack=0 before completion. Compare the phase and output-enable relationship against the command reference model, demonstrating that the ports are not inherently held at their reset values when no reset is asserted.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt=0, and allow reset initialization to complete. Drive the external bus high with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 for enough enabled clocks for synchronization and filtering, then drive sda_i=0 while keeping scl_i=1 and hold both levels long enough to produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition.
elements.expected_response: busy becomes 1 after the filtered SDA transition is processed. This is the holding side of the observed-via behavior: busy becoming 1 demonstrates that the external SCL and SDA inputs were continuously synchronized, filtered, and processed into a START event.
elements.check_method: Sample busy after each posedge clk after registered updates settle; correlate the assertion with the reference model's two-stage synchronization, filter sampling, majority result, and filtered SDA falling edge while filtered SCL is high. Require busy to transition from 0 to 1 without requiring a raw-input edge timing match.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt=0, and allow reset initialization to complete. Keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 continuously for enough enabled clocks to establish filtered idle-high values; do not apply any SDA high-to-low transition while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: busy remains 0 throughout the observation interval. This is the contrasting side of the observed-via behavior: busy does not become 1 when no qualifying filtered SDA transition occurs, so no false evidence of a continuously sampled START event is produced.
elements.check_method: Monitor busy on every settled posedge clk and compare against a reference filter and START detector; require no busy assertion while filtered SDA remains high and filtered SCL remains high.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt=0, and allow reset initialization to complete with dout=0. Drive sda_i=1 and scl_i=0 long enough for the low level to synchronize and filter, then drive scl_i=1 while keeping sda_i=1 until a filtered SCL rising edge occurs.
elements.expected_response: dout updates to 1 when the filtered SCL rising edge is processed. This is the holding side of the observed-via behavior: dout updating to the current filtered SDA value demonstrates continued sampling and processing of the external SCL and SDA inputs.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to predict the synchronized and majority-filtered SCL rising edge and filtered SDA value; sample dout after each posedge clk and require it to become 1 on the processing cycle, with the specified registered-output latency.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt=0, and allow reset initialization to complete with dout=0. Drive sda_i=1 and scl_i=0 continuously for enough enabled clocks to establish filtered SCL low, then keep scl_i=0 and sda_i=1 for the remainder of the observation interval so no filtered SCL rising edge occurs.
elements.expected_response: dout retains its previous value of 0 throughout the interval. This is the contrasting side of the observed-via behavior: dout does not update when no filtered SCL rising edge occurs.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered SCL and dout on every settled posedge clk using the reference synchronization/filter model; require no filtered SCL rising edge and require dout to remain equal to its reset value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 for several rising edges of clk. Change sda_i to 0 while keeping scl_i=1, then hold both levels stable for sufficient rising edges to cover two-stage synchronization and filter settling.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy rises after the expected synchronization and filtering latency, evidencing that raw scl_i and sda_i were captured on successive clk rising edges and propagated to START detection.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk, sample the synchronized/filter reference model and compare the observed busy transition against the modeled two-stage capture and filter latency; require exactly one transition from busy=0 to busy=1 after the modeled START detection.

elements.stimulus: After reset with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, pulse sda_i low for fewer clocks than required for the two-stage synchronizer and filter to settle, then return sda_i high while keeping scl_i=1.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: busy remains low; the START-induced busy transition is absent because the raw excursion does not propagate as a valid synchronized and filtered SDA transition.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the two-stage capture and filter histories, then assert that busy never rises during or after the short pulse and that no filtered START event is observed.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous nReset low, release it, and run with rst=0, ena=1, and clk_cnt=0. Hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 until reset state is established, then drive sda_i=0 and hold both scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 for enough rising edges of clk to pass the two-stage capture and three-sample filtering path.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: busy remains low until the synchronized and filtered SDA high-to-low transition is detected while filtered SCL is high, then busy rises on the registered observation cycle. The transition must not be acted on directly at the raw-input edge.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk after NBA settling, compare busy and the START-condition/filter probes against a reference model containing two capture stages and the three-sample majority filter; verify busy changes only after the modeled synchronized filtered START.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous nReset low, release it, and run with rst=0, ena=1, and clk_cnt=0. Hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 so busy=0, then inject a short sda_i low pulse lasting no more than one clk period before returning sda_i high, without allowing the captured and filtered SDA history to obtain a low majority.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of shows: the raw or metastability-prone SDA perturbation does not produce a synchronized filtered START, so busy remains unchanged at 0; no busy assertion is permitted from the raw glitch alone.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk after NBA settling, compare busy and filtered START-condition probes with the two-stage-capture/majority-filter reference model; verify the pulse does not create a filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high and busy never rises.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous nReset low and release it, keep ena high, set clk_cnt to 4, hold scl_i high and sda_i high until the synchronized and filtered histories are initialized. While the bus is idle, drive sda_i low for only one filter sampling interval, shorter than the three-sample majority window, then restore sda_i high; do not issue a command.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0102: busy remains low because the short synchronized SDA disturbance is suppressed by the digital input filter and no filtered START condition is produced.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after synchronization and filtering settle, compare busy against a reference model containing the two-stage synchronizers, filter sample interval, three-sample SDA history, and majority decision; assert that busy never rises during or after the short excursion.

elements.stimulus: Reset and initialize as in TP-0000, keep ena high and clk_cnt at 4, hold scl_i high and sda_i high, then drive sda_i low continuously for at least three filter sampling intervals so the synchronized filter history contains a majority of low samples; keep the low level long enough for filtered START processing.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding contrast of REQ-0102: busy rises after the filtered SDA high-to-low transition, demonstrating that a sustained synchronized input change passes through the digital input filter and is observable as a filtered START condition.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to predict the first filtered SDA falling edge while filtered SCL is high, then compare busy after the corresponding registered update and require busy=1; distinguish this from TP-0000 by confirming the low level persists for at least three filter samples.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high, set clk_cnt to 16'd8, hold the bus released with scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=START on an enabled command tick, then drive a stable SDA high-to-low transition while SCL remains high and keep the resulting START-shaped bus condition stable.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of REQ-0103: filter sampling opportunities occur every clk_cnt>>2 = 2 enabled clocks, and busy asserts only after the synchronized transition has passed the corresponding filtered-sample opportunities needed to produce filtered SDA high-to-low while filtered SCL is high. busy must not assert at a latency consistent with a different sampling interval or before the required filtered samples.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the two-stage synchronizers, filter counter, three-sample histories, majority filter, and START detector. Count enabled clocks from the synchronized SDA transition to busy assertion; compare all filter_sample_due events and the registered busy observation against the model, allowing the specified synchronization and registered-output latency.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt to 16'd0, hold the bus released with scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=START on an enabled command tick, then drive a stable SDA high-to-low transition while SCL remains high and keep the START-shaped bus condition stable.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting zero-derived case of REQ-0103: clk_cnt>>2 is zero, so the filter sampling interval is treated as sampling on every enabled clock. busy asserts after the corresponding synchronized samples and majority-filtered START detection, with no multi-clock filter-counter spacing. Its latency must differ from the clk_cnt=8 case as predicted by the reference model; behavior consistent with a nonzero interval or with no filter sampling is incorrect.
elements.check_method: Run the same cycle-accurate synchronizer/filter/START reference model with clk_cnt=0, verify filter_sample_due on every enabled clock, and compare the predicted filtered transition and registered busy assertion cycle. Cross-check the measured latency against TP-0000's clk_cnt=8 result to confirm the prescale-dependent difference.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=8, and scl_i high. Initialize the filtered SDA history high by holding sda_i high, then drive sda_i low and keep it low through the synchronizer and two enabled filter-counter expiries so that the newly shifted synchronized low SDA sample completes a high-to-low majority transition while filtered SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: At the enabled filter-counter expiry that shifts the sample completing the high-to-low majority transition, busy rises from 0 to 1 on the corresponding registered update. This is the 'busy rises from 0 to 1 at the resulting filtered START detection' side of REQ-0104@1.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to predict filter-counter expiry, two-stage synchronization, and three-sample history updates. At the predicted expiry, sample busy after the posedge and require a 0-to-1 transition; require no busy transition at earlier expiries that do not yet produce the majority change.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=8, and scl_i high. Keep sda_i high, or apply a low SDA interval shorter than required for the synchronized sample to complete a high-to-low majority transition, and allow at least one enabled filter-counter expiry to shift the resulting synchronized sample into fSCL and fSDA.
elements.expected_response: The enabled filter-counter expiry does not produce a filtered SDA high-to-low majority transition, so busy remains 0 and does not rise. This is the 'busy does not rise when the shifted sample does not produce a filtered SDA high-to-low majority transition' side of REQ-0104@1.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the filter-counter expiry and resulting synchronized history update. Sample busy after the expiry and require it to remain low, with no 0-to-1 transition during the observation window.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset with ena=1, set clk_cnt=0, and leave SCL and SDA externally released high so the initialized three-sample histories contain high values. Then drive SDA low while keeping SCL high for enough enabled clocks to produce at least two synchronized low SDA samples, and maintain the low level until the filter update that changes the SDA history from fewer than two low samples to at least two low samples.
elements.expected_response: The majority-filtered SDA becomes low while the majority-filtered SCL remains high; this is the filtered START case, so busy rises after the registered filtered-transition processing. This is the majority-holds case for REQ-0105.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the two-stage synchronizers, filter sample updates, three-sample histories, and two-out-of-three majority values. At each settled posedge, compare the modeled filtered START event and expected busy assertion with busy, allowing the specified registered output latency.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset with ena=1, set clk_cnt to a nonzero value, and keep SCL externally high. Generate an SDA low pulse timed through the synchronizer and filter model to contribute no more than one low sample in the three-sample SDA history, then return SDA high before a second low sample is shifted. Repeat with SCL low long enough that fewer than two SCL history samples are high while SDA transitions low, if needed to exercise both sub-majority conditions.
elements.expected_response: busy does not rise: an SDA history with fewer than two low samples does not make filtered SDA low, and an SCL history with fewer than two high samples cannot qualify the transition as a filtered START. This is the sub-majority-does-not-hold case for REQ-0105.
elements.check_method: Predict synchronized samples, filter update points, three-sample histories, and majority outputs with a reference model. Assert that no modeled filtered START event occurs and compare busy after every filter update and registered-output settling point; record separate coverage for SDA sub-majority and SCL sub-majority.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a READ command with ena high. Keep filtered SCL low, drive SDA to a stable value of 0, then hold the external SCL and SDA lines long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to produce a filtered SCL rising edge with filtered SDA low. Repeat with stable SDA high on a subsequent READ bit.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on each filtered SCL rising edge during the active READ sequence, dout updates to the stable filtered SDA value: 0 for the first bit and 1 for the second bit.
elements.check_method: At every filtered_scl_rising probe event while in_read_sequence is asserted, compare the registered dout after the posedge with filtered_sda_low/high and verify the one-clock registered update corresponds to the filtered SDA value rather than the raw SDA input.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a READ command with ena high and establish a known dout value from a valid filtered SCL rising edge. While the bus is otherwise stable, inject SDA and SCL pulses shorter than the synchronization/filter interval, ensuring the pulses do not create a filtered SCL rising edge or change the majority-filtered SDA value; then return the raw lines to their prior levels.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: dout does not update in response to the raw SDA or SCL glitches, because they do not produce the corresponding filtered SCL edge or filtered SDA value. dout remains at its previously captured value.
elements.check_method: Monitor raw input transitions, filter_sample_due, filtered_scl_rising, filtered_sda_high/low, and dout. Assert that each injected glitch produces no filtered SCL rising edge or filtered SDA transition and that dout remains unchanged on all intervening posedges.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the bus released and filtered SCL high, hold SDA high long enough for the synchronizer and majority filter to settle, then drive SDA low stably through a complete filter update; afterward drive SDA high stably through a complete filter update.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the filtered SDA changes high-to-low while filtered SCL is high, busy asserts high; when the filtered SDA subsequently changes low-to-high while filtered SCL remains high, busy clears low. The transitions occur according to the delayed filtered-signal comparison, not from the raw SDA transition alone.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronizer, filter histories, filtered SDA, delayed SDA, and filtered SCL. At each modeled filtered SDA transition while filtered SCL is high, compare busy after the registering clock edge with the expected START/STOP status and verify no transition is credited before the modeled filtered transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset with filtered SCL high and filtered SDA stably high, inject an SDA low pulse shorter than the filter interval, then return SDA high and keep it stable; do not allow the pulse to change the majority-filtered SDA value.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because the delayed filtered SDA does not record a corresponding filtered high-to-low transition, busy must remain unchanged and must not assert. Likewise, returning the raw SDA high must not create a busy clear transition absent a filtered low-to-high transition.
elements.check_method: Confirm with the reference filter model and filtered-signal probes that filtered SDA and its delayed version remain high throughout the glitch, then compare busy before, during, and after the pulse; require no busy edge or spurious START/STOP indication.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, leave the controller idle, set clk_cnt to 0, and hold the externally resolved filtered-equivalent bus values at SCL=1 and SDA=1 for multiple enabled clocks. Do not issue a command and do not create an SDA high-to-low transition while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: The non-holding side of the observation applies: busy remains 0. No bus event is detected for stable filtered SCL/SDA values, and no unrelated SDA transition pattern causes busy to rise.
elements.check_method: Sample busy after each posedge clk and compare against a reference model containing current and one-cycle-delayed filtered SCL/SDA values; assert that busy never rises during the stable interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, leave the controller idle, set clk_cnt to 0, and hold filtered-equivalent SCL high with filtered-equivalent SDA high. Then drive SDA externally low and hold it low long enough for synchronization and the three-sample majority filter to produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL remains high; do not issue a command.
elements.expected_response: The holding side of the observation applies: when the filtered SDA high-to-low transition occurs while filtered SCL is high, busy rises to 1 on the registered response cycle, demonstrating detection of the START bus event from the current-versus-delayed filtered-value comparison.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronizers, filter histories, current filtered values, and delayed filtered values to identify the filtered START pattern. Compare busy after each posedge clk and require a 0-to-1 transition on the cycle after the modeled filtered START detection.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and the bus filtered idle high, drive scl_i high and drive sda_i low long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of shows: a START condition is detected and busy rises on the registered update that processes the filtered transition, remaining asserted until a STOP condition or reset.
elements.check_method: Compare the reference model's filtered SDA/SCL histories and START event against busy sampled after each posedge; require busy to rise exactly at the modeled registered detection point and remain high thereafter absent STOP or reset.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy low, apply an SDA transition that is not a filtered high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high: first toggle sda_i low and back high for less than the filter interval while scl_i is high, then drive a stable SDA high-to-low transition while scl_i is low.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding case of shows: busy does not rise in response to either non-qualifying SDA activity, because no filtered SDA high-to-low transition occurs while filtered SCL is high.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to confirm that no qualifying START event is generated, then sample busy after every posedge and require it to remain low throughout the stimulus, excluding reset behavior.

elements.stimulus: With the bus initially filtered high, drive filtered SDA low while filtered SCL is high long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to detect a START and set busy=1. Then keep filtered SCL high and release SDA so filtered SDA makes a stable low-to-high transition, holding the new levels long enough for the filtered STOP condition to be processed.
elements.expected_response: After the registered processing of the filtered low-to-high SDA transition while filtered SCL is high, the controller detects the STOP condition and busy clears to 0. This is the clearing side of REQ-0110's observed_via shows clause.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronizer, filter history, and filtered-edge timing; sample busy after each posedge settles and assert that busy is 1 after the START detection and becomes 0 exactly after the filtered STOP detection.

elements.stimulus: With the bus initially filtered high, drive filtered SDA low while filtered SCL is high long enough to detect a START and set busy=1. Keep filtered SCL high and filtered SDA low; optionally apply a raw SDA high glitch shorter than the required synchronization and majority-filter interval, so filtered SDA does not make a low-to-high transition.
elements.expected_response: Because no filtered SDA low-to-high transition occurs while filtered SCL is high, no STOP condition is detected and busy remains 1. This is the non-clearing side of REQ-0110's observed_via shows clause.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to confirm filtered SDA remains low and no filtered STOP event is produced; compare registered busy after every posedge and assert it remains high after the initial START detection.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, then release it; keep rst low and ena high. Drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough for synchronization and filtering to establish filtered SCL and SDA high. While scl_i remains 1, drive sda_i=0 and hold it stable until start_condition is observed, then continue for the registered busy update.
elements.expected_response: This is the START side of the observed behavior: after the filtered START condition is detected, busy becomes 1 on the corresponding registered status update and remains 1 while no STOP condition is detected.
elements.check_method: Use the start_condition probe as the detection event and compare busy in the settled post-posedge sample against a reference model that accounts for synchronizer/filter latency; require busy==1 on the update following detection.

elements.stimulus: Reset and establish a filtered bus-high idle, then create a filtered START by holding scl_i=1 and driving sda_i from 1 to 0 until start_condition is observed. After busy becomes 1, keep scl_i=1 and drive sda_i from 0 to 1, holding it stable until stop_condition is observed, then continue for the registered busy update.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting STOP side of the observed behavior: after the filtered STOP condition is detected, busy becomes 0 on the corresponding registered status update, rather than remaining 1.
elements.check_method: Use start_condition to confirm the precondition busy==1, use stop_condition as the STOP detection event, and compare the settled post-posedge busy output with the reference model; require busy==0 on the update following detection.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a WRITE command with din=1 while the external bus keeps SDA high and SCL high. Do not introduce any externally caused filtered SCL falling edge during the released high phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting ordinary-behavior case: scl_oen follows the locally timed WRITE sequence, transitions from released high to driven low at the normal local timing boundary, and cmd_ack is produced after the normal WRITE low phase without synchronization-induced retiming or clock-stretch delay.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for clk_en, filtering, and WRITE phase timing. At every posedge compare scl_oen and cmd_ack with the model, and verify no slave-wait or synchronization event occurs during the released high phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and externally drive SCL low after the DUT releases it for the WRITE high phase. Hold SCL low long enough for filtered SCL to remain low, then release SCL high and allow the filter to detect the high level.
elements.expected_response: This is the clock-stretching side of the observation: scl_oen remains 1 while released SCL is filtered low, the WRITE phase does not advance, and cmd_ack is delayed. Once filtered SCL becomes high, scl_oen may transition to 0 according to the resumed normal timing and the command eventually completes with one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered SCL, slave_wait_active, scl_oen, and cmd_ack on settled posedge samples. Compare against a reference model that freezes the timing counter and FSM during the filtered-low interval, then verify the delayed transition and eventual acknowledgment.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and during the released high phase externally force SCL low so that a filtered SCL falling edge is detected while scl_oen remains 1. Keep SCL low for the synchronized low period, then release it high.
elements.expected_response: This is the multi-master synchronization side of the observation: the local timing is resynchronized to the shared SCL low period, so the next scl_oen boundary and eventual cmd_ack occur only after the synchronized low-period timing; no command completion occurs before that synchronization-dependent delay.
elements.check_method: Correlate scl_sync_event and filtered SCL falling-edge observations with the timing reference model. Verify the timing counter reload/resynchronization, compare the subsequent scl_oen transition and cmd_ack cycle against the synchronized model, and ensure the WRITE command completes exactly once.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command while the bus is initially high, and allow the command to reach the phase where scl_oen=1 releases SCL. Then drive scl_i=0 and hold it long enough for the filtered SCL input to become low; keep the external SCL low until the controller has been waiting, then drive scl_i=1 and hold it high until filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.expected_response: While scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL remains low, the slave_wait_active probe asserts, the READ FSM does not advance, and cmd_ack does not pulse; this is the holding side of the requirement's observed behavior. After filtered SCL becomes high, waiting ends and cmd_ack eventually pulses once at normal command completion.
elements.check_method: Use the clocking block to sample after each posedge; assert that scl_oen=1, slave_wait_active=1, and no cmd_ack pulse occur throughout the filtered-low interval, then verify that a single cmd_ack pulse occurs only after filtered_scl_high becomes true. Compare against a reference model of filtering, slave-wait timing, and command progression.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command while scl_i remains high and the external bus does not stretch SCL. Allow the command to reach the phase where scl_oen=1 releases SCL, and keep scl_i high so the filtered SCL input remains high.
elements.expected_response: When scl_oen=1 releases SCL and filtered SCL is high, slave_wait_active does not assert, the command advances normally, and cmd_ack pulses once at the command's terminal completion phase without postponement; this is the contrasting non-holding side of the requirement's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample registered outputs and probes after each posedge; verify scl_oen=1 is followed by filtered_scl_high=1 with slave_wait_active=0, and measure that the single cmd_ack pulse occurs at the reference-model completion point rather than being delayed by clock stretching.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 then release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, initialize the bus high, set clk_cnt=1 and din=0, issue the supported WRITE command cmd=0100 while idle, and after the WRITE releases SCL drive scl_i=0 continuously for at least 20 enabled clocks so filtered SCL remains low.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in REQ-0114's shows clause: once the accepted WRITE releases SCL (scl_oen=1), the controller indicates slave_wait, does not advance the command, and cmd_ack remains 0 with no completion pulse for the entire interval that filtered SCL remains low.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after command acceptance, assert that while scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL is low, slave_wait_active remains asserted, cmd_ack is 0, and the WRITE does not reach its terminal acknowledgement phase; use a waveform assertion to detect any cmd_ack pulse during the hold interval.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 then release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, initialize the bus high, set clk_cnt=1 and din=0, issue the supported WRITE command cmd=0100 while idle, and keep scl_i=1 so that released SCL reaches filtered high throughout the command.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding case in REQ-0114's shows clause: after SCL is released and filtered SCL is high, slave_wait is not active, the WRITE progresses through its remaining phases, and cmd_ack pulses exactly once at sequence completion.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen, filtered SCL, slave_wait_active, and cmd_ack on settled posedge samples; assert that the command advances after the released SCL becomes filtered high, no slave-wait interval persists, and exactly one one-clock cmd_ack pulse occurs before returning idle.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=0, and issue cmd=WRITE (0100) while the bus is idle. Drive the external SCL line low after the WRITE sequence releases SCL, and hold scl_i=0 long enough for filtered SCL to become low and remain low.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in the observed port behavior: while the released SCL remains filtered low, cmd_ack remains low, no command-completion pulse occurs, the WRITE FSM remains in its active high-phase wait, and the timing counter remains paused with no clk_en_tick or FSM phase advancement.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after the high-phase wait begins, compare cmd_ack against 0 and verify that command_active/in_write_sequence remain asserted, scl_oen remains released, and no clk_en_tick or state-transition indication occurs. Continue for multiple enabled-clock periods to distinguish a pause from normal latency.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=0, and WRITE command sequence, but after the WRITE sequence releases SCL, allow the external SCL line to be high and hold scl_i=1 until filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting ordinary case in the observed port behavior: once filtered SCL is high, the held high phase completes, the FSM advances through the remaining WRITE phase, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock cycle; command completion is not indefinitely postponed.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate scoreboard synchronized to posedge clk. Verify filtered_scl_high becomes true, the FSM leaves the high-phase wait, and cmd_ack produces one and only one asserted cycle followed by 0, with no arbitration loss.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, issue a WRITE command with din=0, and keep the bus released high. When the command reaches its released-SCL high phase (scl_oen=1), drive scl_i low externally early enough that the synchronized and filtered SCL falling edge occurs before the next locally timed phase boundary; then keep scl_i low until the controller begins its low phase.
elements.expected_response: The externally caused filtered SCL falling edge is recognized while SCL is released, corresponding to scl_sync assertion and timing-counter reload. The expected REQ-0116 holding case is observed at scl_oen: scl_oen remains 1, and the next SCL phase transition is postponed until the synchronized shared-bus low-period timing has elapsed rather than occurring on the original local schedule.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronizer/filter latency, filtered SCL falling-edge detection, counter reload, and subsequent low-period timing. Confirm the scl_sync_event probe at the filtered falling edge, compare scl_oen against the model, and assert that the release-to-low transition is delayed by the synchronization/reload interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, issue the same WRITE command with din=0, and keep scl_i externally high throughout the released-SCL high phase (scl_oen=1), with no externally caused filtered SCL falling edge before the next locally timed phase boundary.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting no-edge case is observed at scl_oen: scl_oen remains 1 only until the normal local timing schedule expires, then advances to the next command phase without the postponement caused by shared-bus synchronization. No scl_sync_event occurs.
elements.check_method: Run the same cycle-accurate reference model without an external SCL falling event. Compare the observed scl_oen transition cycle with the normal local counter schedule and verify that it occurs earlier than in TP-0000 by the synchronization/reload delay, with no scl_sync_event probe assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=4, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, and issue a WRITE command with din=1 on an enabled timing tick. Continue clocking through the WRITE stable-high phase and the subsequent SCL-low phase while recording scl_oen and clk_en_tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen changes between WRITE bit-timing phases only on counter-generated clk_en ticks. The stable-high phase and following SCL-low phase are separated by the configured counter-paced intervals, and the command eventually produces its normal completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of cnt reload, decrement, expiry, and clk_en generation. Compare every observed scl_oen transition and its cycle distance from the preceding transition against the model, and verify transitions coincide with clk_en_tick.
