elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=4, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, and issue a WRITE command with din=1. Once the WRITE command has entered a phase that requires the next scl_oen transition, sample scl_oen on each of the next three enabled clocks before the modeled cnt expiry, then continue until expiry.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: before cnt expires, scl_oen must remain unchanged; it must not advance through WRITE phases on an unpaced clock or at an incorrect cadence. The phase transition is permitted only at the modeled clk_en tick after the configured interval. Any earlier scl_oen change is the otherwise side of the observation and fails.
elements.check_method: Predict the first legal transition cycle from the counter reference model and assert scl_oen stability on all preceding enabled clocks. Compare the observed transition cycle with cnt_expired and clk_en_tick, flagging an early or late transition as a counter-timing failure.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive clk_cnt=3, provide a released-high bus, and issue one supported START command on an enabled timing tick. Keep rst and nReset inactive, and prevent arbitration loss, clock stretching, and external SCL synchronization until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: cmd_ack is asserted exactly once only after the START command phases have advanced through timing intervals governed by a counter loaded from clk_cnt=3 and decremented on successive clk cycles; it is not asserted immediately on every clock.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for cnt reload, decrement, expiration, and command-phase advancement. Compare the observed one-cycle cmd_ack position against the model's predicted completion cycle and verify no earlier ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: Run the same otherwise-identical supported START command twice with ena=1 and a released-high bus: first with clk_cnt=0, then with clk_cnt=8. Keep reset inactive and exclude clock stretching, arbitration loss, and external SCL synchronization.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of shows: cmd_ack completion timing must change with clk_cnt. A design exhibiting timing independent of clk_cnt, advancing every clock for both runs, or failing to complete is a failure of the requirement; the expected DUT behavior is the two completion times predicted by the corresponding counter-loaded-and-decremented reference models.
elements.check_method: Record the posedge at which the command is accepted and the posedge carrying the one-cycle cmd_ack for each run. Compare each latency with its cycle-accurate reference-model prediction and require the clk_cnt=8 latency to differ from the clk_cnt=0 latency in the prescribed direction.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, set clk_cnt=3, present a supported START command while idle, then keep the bus externally released high and run posedges through the current START timing phase until the timing counter expires.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: On the expiration cycle, the clk_en_tick probe asserts and the command FSM advances to the next START timing phase; after the registered update, scl_oen changes to the output-enable level prescribed by that next phase. The phase transition occurs only in association with the expiration-generated clk_en tick.
elements.check_method: Use a reference divider model to predict counter decrement, expiration, and clk_en_tick. At each posedge sample probes and scl_oen after nonblocking assignments settle, and compare the observed clk_en_tick-to-scl_oen transition and START phase sequence against the model.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, set clk_cnt=3, present a supported START command while idle, then observe the same current START timing phase on one or more posedges while the timing counter is still nonzero and before its expiration.
elements.expected_response: CONTRASTING CASE: Before the timing counter expires, cnt_nonzero remains asserted, clk_en_tick is not asserted, the FSM does not advance its timing phase, and scl_oen holds its current registered level with no command-phase transition.
elements.check_method: Use the reference divider model to identify cycles before expiration. Compare cnt_nonzero, clk_en_tick, the in_start_sequence probe, and consecutive scl_oen samples; require no scl_oen change or phase transition on all pre-expiration cycles.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, set clk_cnt=0, present a supported START command while idle, and run the command through multiple timing phases with the bus externally released high.
elements.expected_response: With the zero reload value, the counter reaches its expiration condition without becoming stuck; clk_en_tick is asserted on every enabled timing opportunity and the command FSM advances through successive START phases, producing the corresponding registered scl_oen transitions rather than remaining in one phase indefinitely.
elements.check_method: Model the specified zero-prescaler behavior and compare clk_en_tick and scl_oen at every posedge. Require no extended interval without clk_en_tick while ena is high and require the observed START phase transitions to match the reference sequence.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, issue a START command, then continue clocking the active START sequence for cycles before the timing counter expires; do not assert reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: This is the no-advance side of the requirement: while the active command phase is waiting and clk_en is not asserted, including cycles where the timing counter is nonzero, scl_oen holds the output-enable value for the current START phase and does not change to the value for the next phase.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use the divider/FSM reference model and compare scl_oen with the prior-cycle value whenever the model predicts cnt_nonzero=1 and clk_en_tick=0; require scl_oen to remain unchanged and require the in_start_sequence or command_active probe to remain active.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, issue a START command, and continue clocking until the active START sequence reaches a phase boundary with the timing counter expired; allow the resulting clk_en tick and continue one additional posedge without reset, stretching, or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: This is the advance side of the requirement: scl_oen changes to the output-enable value prescribed for the next START bit-timing phase only after the posedge that asserts clk_en_tick; no corresponding phase change is visible on earlier non-tick cycles.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate divider and FSM reference model to identify cnt_expired=1 and clk_en_tick=1, then compare the registered scl_oen after that posedge against the next-phase value. Assert that scl_oen was held on all preceding cycles with clk_en_tick=0 and that the change occurs at the first permitted registered update.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to a nonzero value and keep the bus released high. With ena high, issue a supported WRITE command and wait until it is accepted and command_active is asserted. Before the command reaches its terminal phase, drive ena low and hold it low for multiple clock cycles, then reassert ena high.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding-case side of the observed behavior: while ena remains low, cmd_ack stays low and the WRITE FSM does not progress through normal bit-timing phases. The timing counter is reloaded rather than advancing toward a timing tick. After ena is reasserted, the command may resume and eventually produce its normal one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: At every posedge while ena is low, compare cmd_ack against 0 and verify no command-phase or output-enable transition attributable to normal FSM timing occurs. After re-enabling ena, verify the command eventually completes with exactly one cmd_ack pulse using a reference model that accounts for the counter reload.

elements.stimulus: Use the same clk_cnt, released-high bus, and supported WRITE command. Keep ena high continuously, issue the command, and wait for it to be accepted and command_active to assert without inserting an ena-low interval.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding-case side of the observed behavior: with ena high, normal bit-level FSM timing progresses, the command reaches its terminal phase, and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock cycle.
elements.check_method: Monitor command_active, output-enable phase transitions, and cmd_ack on settled posedge samples. Compare the observed sequence and variable completion latency against a divider/FSM reference model, and require one and only one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the bus released/high. Issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1 while the controller is idle, and keep filtered SDA high throughout the WRITE stable high phase while SDA is released.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE operation's released-SDA stable high phase, arbitration checking is active and the controller observes no arbitration loss: al remains low. The WRITE operation proceeds to its normal completion and produces cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: At each enabled timing phase, correlate in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and sda_check_active with filtered_sda_high; compare al and cmd_ack against a reference model and verify al is low through command completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the bus released/high. Issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1 while the controller is idle. When the WRITE operation reaches its stable high phase with SDA released, externally drive SDA low and hold it long enough for the filtered SDA to become low.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE operation's released-SDA stable high phase, arbitration checking detects the filtered SDA low condition and al asserts. This is the contrasting side of the observed behavior: al asserts when filtered SDA is low, indicating arbitration loss. The active WRITE aborts without cmd_ack and both output enables are released.
elements.check_method: Use the probes in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and sda_check_active to identify the checking window; verify the external low produces filtered_sda_low, then compare al assertion, absence of cmd_ack, and released scl_oen/sda_oen with the arbitration-loss reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue an enabled WRITE command with din=1. Model the bus as released high, then wait until the WRITE data phase releases SDA and SCL (sda_oen=1 and scl_oen=1). During this stable high WRITE window, externally hold SDA low long enough for filtered SDA to become low, then allow the command to terminate or abort.
elements.expected_response: The stable high WRITE phase is reached with SDA released, and the expected-high SDA arbitration check is active. Because filtered SDA is low while din=1, al asserts, the active WRITE command aborts without cmd_ack, and both output enables are released. This is the asserting side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, use the WRITE-phase probe and output enables to identify the stable high window; compare filtered SDA and al against a reference model. Require al to transition high after filtered SDA is observed low, require no cmd_ack for the aborted command, and require al to remain high until reset.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue an enabled WRITE command with din=1. Model the bus as released high and keep SDA externally released high after the WRITE data phase releases SDA and SCL (sda_oen=1 and scl_oen=1), through the stable high WRITE window and until normal completion.
elements.expected_response: The stable high WRITE phase is reached with SDA released and filtered SDA remaining high. al remains low and the WRITE command completes normally with exactly one cmd_ack. This is the non-asserting side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, use the WRITE-phase probe and output enables to identify the stable high window; compare filtered SDA, al, and cmd_ack against a reference model. Require al to remain low throughout the high phase and require exactly one completion pulse after the normal WRITE sequence.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=1, and issue cmd=WRITE while the FSM is idle. Allow the command to be accepted on a clk_en tick and advance without reset, disable, clock stretching, or prior arbitration loss. During the WRITE stable high phase, keep the DUT's SDA released and externally drive sda_i low long enough for the synchronized three-sample filter to produce filtered SDA low.
elements.expected_response: While SDA arbitration checking is active in the released high-data phase, the expected-high versus filtered-low mismatch causes al to assert; the command is aborted without cmd_ack and both output enables are released.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, qualify the check with in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and sda_check_active, and compare al against a reference model of synchronization and majority filtering. Confirm al becomes 1 after the mismatch is processed, no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted command, and sda_oen and scl_oen are released.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=1, and issue cmd=WRITE while the FSM is idle. Allow the command to be accepted on a clk_en tick and advance without reset, disable, clock stretching, or prior arbitration loss. During the WRITE stable high phase, keep the DUT's SDA released and externally allow sda_i to remain high long enough for the synchronized three-sample filter to produce filtered SDA high.
elements.expected_response: Because the expected-high and filtered-low mismatch is absent, al remains low for this scoped SDA arbitration condition; the WRITE proceeds through its normal low phase and eventually produces its normal one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, qualify the check with in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and sda_check_active, and compare al and cmd_ack against the normal-write reference model. Confirm al stays 0 throughout the operation and cmd_ack occurs once after normal completion.

elements.stimulus: Reset with al low, then drive ena=1 and issue a valid WRITE command while the bus is released high. After the command is accepted and is executing, externally create a filtered STOP condition by causing filtered SDA to transition from low to high while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: At the clock processing the unexpected STOP during the active WRITE command, al asserts. This is the arbitration-lost side of the observed behavior; the command is aborted and no command-complete pulse is generated for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered STOP-condition probe and command_active/in_write_sequence probes to qualify the event, then compare al on the settled post-posedge output against a reference model. Check that al transitions low-to-high on the event and that cmd_ack does not assert for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: Reset with al low, keep the bus released high, drive ena=1, and issue a valid STOP command while idle. Allow the STOP sequence to execute through its generated STOP condition, with filtered SDA transitioning from low to high while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: When the STOP condition occurs during the active STOP command, al remains deasserted. This is the contrasting non-arbitration-loss side of the observed behavior, and the STOP command completes with a one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered STOP-condition and in_stop_sequence probes to qualify the event, then sample al and cmd_ack after each posedge. Compare against a reference model requiring al to remain low and cmd_ack to pulse once at STOP completion.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset high and rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and during the write stable high phase with SCL released, externally hold SDA low so the filtered SDA is low while the master expects it high.
elements.expected_response: At the clock edge where arbitration loss is detected and al rises, the FSM returns to idle and both scl_oen and sda_oen are high, releasing SCL and SDA. This is the holding side of the observed_via difference: the ports show released-high values rather than their non-loss driven-low values.
elements.check_method: At the settled sampling point after the arbitration-loss posedge, assert al=1 and in_idle=1, and compare scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1 against the reference model; also verify no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset high and rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a WRITE command with din=0, keep the external SDA released/high or low as appropriate without causing arbitration loss, and observe the normal active-command low phase in which the controller drives both SCL and SDA low.
elements.expected_response: While the normal non-arbitration-loss low phase is active, al remains low, the FSM remains active rather than returning to idle, and scl_oen and sda_oen remain low, driving SCL and SDA low. This is the contrasting otherwise side of the observed_via difference.
elements.check_method: Use the write-sequence and command-active probes to identify the normal low phase, then sample al, in_idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen after each posedge and compare against the reference model; require al=0, in_idle=0, scl_oen=0, and sda_oen=0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=1000 (READ) on an enabled clk_en tick with a released bus. Allow the FSM to enter the READ window with scl_oen=1. Establish filtered SDA low, then apply a raw SDA-high pulse shorter than the filter sampling interval without changing the filtered SDA value. Drive SCL high so that a filtered SCL rising edge occurs while the READ window is active.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered SCL rising edge, dout captures 0, the filtered SDA value. This is the holding side of the observed_via shows condition: dout captures the filtered SDA value at the sampling edge, despite the opposing raw SDA pulse.
elements.check_method: At the posedge that asserts filtered_scl_rising, sample dout after nonblocking updates settle and compare it with the reference model's three-sample majority filtered SDA value; confirm dout=0 and that the raw SDA pulse did not determine the result.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=1000 (READ) on an enabled clk_en tick with a released bus. Allow the FSM to enter the READ window with scl_oen=1. Establish filtered SDA high, then apply a raw SDA-low pulse shorter than the filter sampling interval without changing the filtered SDA value. Drive SCL high so that a filtered SCL rising edge occurs while the READ window is active.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered SCL rising edge, dout captures 1, the filtered SDA value. This is the holding side of the observed_via shows condition for the opposite data value: dout captures the filtered SDA value at the sampling edge, rather than the opposing raw SDA pulse.
elements.check_method: At the posedge that asserts filtered_scl_rising, sample dout after nonblocking updates settle and compare it with the reference model's three-sample majority filtered SDA value; confirm dout=1 and that the raw SDA pulse did not determine the result.

elements.stimulus: With ena high, first drive the external SCL line low long enough for the filtered SCL value to become low. Issue the READ command, keep external SDA high, and then release external SCL high long enough for filtering to produce a filtered SCL low-to-high transition while the READ sequence is active.
elements.expected_response: At the clocked row where filtered_scl_rising is asserted, dout updates to 1, the filtered SDA value. This is the holding case of observed_via.shows: dout updates to the filtered SDA value captured at the filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronizers, filter histories, and filtered-edge detection; on the posedge where filtered_scl_rising is observed, compare registered dout after NBA settling with the modeled filtered SDA value and require dout == 1.

elements.stimulus: Complete one READ with external SDA high and external SCL high to establish dout = 1. Then issue a second READ with ena high, keep external SCL driven low so filtering keeps filtered SCL low throughout the active READ interval, and do not permit any filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: For every clocked row of the second READ interval where filtered_scl_rising is not asserted, dout remains at its previously captured value of 1 and does not capture a new filtered SDA value. This is the non-holding case of observed_via.shows: dout does not capture a new filtered SDA value at rows without a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify all rows without a filtered SCL rising edge and compare dout after each posedge; require dout to remain unchanged at 1 for the entire no-edge interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=READ with ena=1 and a released-high SDA/SCL bus. Drive the external bus so synchronization and filtering produce filtered SDA=0, then produce a filtered SCL rising edge while the READ FSM is in its bit-sampling phase; do not assert reset, al, or cmd_ack before the edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at the registered update for that filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 0, the sampled filtered SDA bit supplied to the byte-level controller.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered_scl_rising and the READ-phase probe, sample dout after the corresponding posedge, and compare dout against the reference model's filtered SDA value captured on that edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=READ with ena=1 and a released-high SDA/SCL bus. Drive the external bus so synchronization and filtering produce filtered SDA=1, then produce a filtered SCL rising edge while the READ FSM is in its bit-sampling phase; do not assert reset, al, or cmd_ack before the edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at the registered update for that filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 1, the sampled filtered SDA bit supplied to the byte-level controller.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered_scl_rising and the READ-phase probe, sample dout after the corresponding posedge, and compare dout against the reference model's filtered SDA value captured on that edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=READ with ena=1 and enter the READ bit-sampling phase. Establish a previously sampled dout value, then change the external SDA input sufficiently for filtered SDA to change while keeping filtered SCL continuously high and preventing any filtered SCL rising edge; keep the READ operation active and do not assert reset, al, or cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case: dout does not update to the changed filtered SDA value because no filtered SCL rising edge sampled it; dout retains its prior registered value until a valid filtered SCL rising edge occurs.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered_scl_rising probe and reference model to confirm that no sampling edge occurred during the SDA change, then compare dout cycle by cycle with its pre-change value before READ completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the FSM idle, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, present cmd=WRITE with din=0, and hold the command while preventing the first clk_en tick from occurring for several enabled clk cycles.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0130: scl_oen remains at the idle released value 1, the FSM remains idle, and no WRITE sequence phase is entered before clk_en permits advancement.
elements.check_method: At every posedge before the reference divider predicts the first clk_en tick, compare scl_oen against 1 and assert in_idle=1 and in_write_sequence=0; flag any early scl_oen transition or command-sequence entry.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, present cmd=WRITE with din=0 while idle, then continue supplying enabled clocks through the first clk_en tick and subsequent WRITE timing phases with SCL released externally high.
elements.expected_response: Advancement case of REQ-0130: on the clk_en-permitted acceptance, the FSM leaves idle and enters the WRITE sequence; scl_oen follows the selected WRITE sequence, including the subsequent driven-low SCL phase rather than remaining in the idle state.
elements.check_method: Use a divider reference model to identify the first clk_en tick, then check that in_write_sequence becomes asserted only at or after that tick and that scl_oen changes from its idle value to the reference-model WRITE phase value on the corresponding registered update; reject any failure to advance after the permitted tick.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus released-high, set ena=1 and cmd=4'b0001 (START), and hold these inputs through an enabled clk_en acceptance tick while the command FSM is idle.
elements.expected_response: Positive side of shows: scl_oen follows the START-selected sequence, remaining released initially, then driving SCL low during the START command, and the command eventually completes with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle and in_start_sequence probes to identify acceptance and phases; compare sampled scl_oen and cmd_ack on posedges against a command-FSM reference model, allowing clk_en-dependent latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, establish an active transaction context with the bus released-high, set ena=1 and cmd=4'b0010 (STOP), and hold the command through an enabled clk_en acceptance tick while the command FSM is idle.
elements.expected_response: Positive side of shows: scl_oen follows the STOP-selected sequence, including SCL release/high behavior before command completion, and cmd_ack is produced when the STOP sequence completes.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle and in_stop_sequence probes; compare the registered scl_oen phase sequence and one-clock cmd_ack pulse with the STOP reference model at each posedge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the external bus released-high, set ena=1 and cmd=4'b1000 (READ), and hold the command through an enabled clk_en acceptance tick while the command FSM is idle; provide a stable external SDA value for the read window.
elements.expected_response: Positive side of shows: scl_oen follows the READ-selected sequence, releasing SCL for the read high phase and subsequently pulling SCL low before cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle and in_read_sequence probes; compare scl_oen transitions, phase ordering, and completion pulse timing against the READ reference model, with variable clk_en/filter latency permitted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the external bus released-high, set ena=1, drive din to a defined value, and set cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE); hold the command through an enabled clk_en acceptance tick while the command FSM is idle.
elements.expected_response: Positive side of shows: scl_oen follows the WRITE-selected sequence, releasing SCL for the write high phase and subsequently pulling SCL low before cmd_ack, without selecting a different command sequence.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle and in_write_sequence probes; compare registered scl_oen phase ordering and the one-clock cmd_ack pulse with the WRITE reference model at posedges.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) while the command FSM is idle for multiple enabled clk_en ticks; keep the bus released-high.
elements.expected_response: Negative side of shows: scl_oen stays in the released idle state, no START, STOP, READ, or WRITE timing sequence occurs, and no command-completion pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle probe to confirm the FSM remains idle; assert that scl_oen remains released and that cmd_ack stays low over the observation interval, with no active-command probe assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and drive an unsupported cmd value such as 4'b0011 while the command FSM is idle for multiple enabled clk_en ticks; keep the bus released-high.
elements.expected_response: Negative side of shows: the unsupported value is treated as no operation; scl_oen stays in the released idle state, no command timing sequence occurs, and no cmd_ack is generated.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle probe and command-active probe; compare scl_oen and cmd_ack against the no-operation reference behavior on every enabled clock.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, release reset with both bus lines externally high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then present cmd=START while the FSM is idle and hold it until command completion.
elements.expected_response: The recognized-command side of the requirement is observed: after the enabled evaluation tick, the FSM leaves idle and sda_oen and scl_oen execute the START-specific sequence, including SDA release followed by SDA low while SCL is high and then SCL low, before returning to idle and producing the normal completion indication.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle and in_start_sequence probes and compare the registered sda_oen/scl_oen waveform against a reference FSM model, checking that a START sequence occurs before cmd_ack and that no sequence occurs while still idle.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, release reset with both bus lines externally high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then present cmd=STOP while the FSM is idle and hold it until command completion.
elements.expected_response: The recognized-command side of the requirement is observed: after the enabled evaluation tick, the FSM leaves idle and sda_oen and scl_oen execute the STOP-specific sequence, including SDA low, SCL release, and SDA release while SCL is high, before returning to idle and producing the normal completion indication.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle and in_stop_sequence probes and compare registered sda_oen/scl_oen transitions with a STOP reference sequence through cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, release reset with SCL externally toggled to provide a filtered rising edge, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then present cmd=READ while the FSM is idle and hold it until command completion.
elements.expected_response: The recognized-command side of the requirement is observed: after the enabled evaluation tick, the FSM leaves idle and sda_oen and scl_oen execute the READ-specific sequence, with SDA released and SCL released for the read window, followed by the low phase and command completion.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle and in_read_sequence probes, drive a legal filtered SCL read waveform, and compare registered output-enable phases and cmd_ack timing with a READ reference model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, release reset with the bus externally high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, drive din=0 and present cmd=WRITE while the FSM is idle; hold the command until completion.
elements.expected_response: The recognized-command side of the requirement is observed: after the enabled evaluation tick, the FSM leaves idle and sda_oen and scl_oen execute the WRITE-specific sequence, including the data-driven SDA phase and released/high then low SCL phases, before command completion.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle and in_write_sequence probes and compare registered sda_oen/scl_oen transitions against a WRITE reference model, including the din=0 data phase.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, release reset with both bus lines externally high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then present cmd=NOP (0000) while the FSM is idle for multiple enabled timing ticks; repeat with an unsupported value such as cmd=0011.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting non-recognized side of the requirement is observed: for both NOP and unsupported cmd=0011, the FSM remains idle; scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the idle released state, no command-specific SCL or SDA sequence begins, and no command-complete pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: Use the in_idle probe and monitor sda_oen, scl_oen, and cmd_ack over multiple clk_en ticks; compare against an idle reference model and assert that neither command-specific sequence probe becomes active.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 to model a released-high bus. With ena=1 and the FSM idle, issue cmd=4'b0001 (START) on a clock edge and keep ena high until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0133: after command acceptance, scl_oen and sda_oen are initially released high as needed; sda_oen then changes to 0 while scl_oen remains 1, generating SDA low while SCL remains released high; subsequently scl_oen changes to 0. The SDA-low/high-SCL ordering is observable before SCL is pulled low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, monitor scl_oen and sda_oen with a temporal assertion requiring the sequence (scl_oen=1,sda_oen=1) followed by (scl_oen=1,sda_oen=0) before (scl_oen=0). Fail if SDA is driven low before SCL is released or if SCL is not released during the SDA-low phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the FSM idle and both bus inputs high, set ena=1 and issue cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) for one enabled command-acceptance tick; do not issue a START command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case of REQ-0133: because the START activation is absent, the START-generation port behavior must not occur; scl_oen and sda_oen remain released high, with no transition to the SDA-low-while-SCL-released combination and no subsequent START SCL-low phase.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen and sda_oen after every posedge through the observation window and assert that the pair remains (1,1); additionally assert that no (scl_oen=1,sda_oen=0) interval occurs. Check that no command sequence or command acknowledgement is produced.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it; keep rst low, ena high, clk_cnt at 16'h0000, scl_i and sda_i released high, and issue cmd=4'b0001 for an enabled START command. Hold the bus high until the START phase is observed with sda_oen low and scl_oen high, then continue clocking without changing the command inputs.
elements.expected_response: After the START condition, scl_oen becomes 0 to drive SCL low, the FSM probe in_idle becomes 1, and cmd_ack becomes 1 for exactly one clock cycle before returning to 0. This is the holding side of the observed behavior: scl_oen is driven low and cmd_ack produces the one-clock completion pulse.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, monitor scl_oen, cmd_ack, and in_idle. Assert that the post-START completion phase has scl_oen=0 and in_idle=1, and use a cycle counter or assertion to require cmd_ack=1 on exactly one consecutive sampled cycle with cmd_ack=0 on the preceding and following cycles.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it; keep rst low, ena high, clk_cnt at 16'h0000, scl_i and sda_i released high, and issue cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) while the FSM is idle. Do not issue a START command or create a START condition on the bus, and clock several enabled cycles.
elements.expected_response: The non-holding side of the observed behavior occurs: because no START condition has been generated, scl_oen does not become 0 for post-START completion and remains released at 1, the FSM remains idle, and cmd_ack stays low with no one-clock completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen, cmd_ack, and in_idle after each settled posedge for several cycles. Assert scl_oen remains 1, in_idle remains 1, and cmd_ack never asserts; flag any low scl_oen or any cmd_ack pulse as a failure of the contrasting case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus released-high, set ena=1 and cmd=STOP (0010), and drive clocks until the STOP command is accepted and either cmd_ack asserts or the STOP sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: During the STOP sequence, sda_oen is driven low before scl_oen is released high; at the transition to the SCL-release phase, sda_oen must already be low and scl_oen may then become high. This is the holding side of the observed shows condition.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after command acceptance, record sda_oen and scl_oen and use a temporal assertion that the first observed release of scl_oen to 1 is preceded by an observed sda_oen=0 in the same STOP transaction; fail if scl_oen becomes 1 while sda_oen has never been 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus released-high, set ena=1 and cmd=START (0001) instead of STOP, and drive clocks through command acceptance and the initial START sequence.
elements.expected_response: Because the STOP-specific behavior is not active, the contrasting observed shows side is permitted: scl_oen may be released high while sda_oen has not first been driven low, so the STOP ordering must not be inferred from ordinary output behavior outside a STOP command.
elements.check_method: At command acceptance, monitor the first transition of scl_oen to 1 and verify that the trace does not require a prior sda_oen=0; separately classify the trace as non-STOP and ensure the STOP-ordering assertion is disabled for this transaction.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive a released-high bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Issue cmd=STOP (4'b0010) while idle, then allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL, and observe the interval before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: After scl_oen becomes 1 and the filtered SCL is high, but before cmd_ack, sda_oen becomes 1 and remains released, generating the STOP transition by releasing SDA high. This is the required side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, use a temporal assertion that once scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL is high during in_stop_sequence, sda_oen must be 1 until cmd_ack; also verify the SDA line rises while SCL is high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=STOP from idle. When the STOP sequence releases SCL (scl_oen=1), externally hold scl_i low so filtered SCL remains low, preventing the valid high-SCL STOP phase from being reached.
elements.expected_response: While scl_oen=1 but filtered SCL remains low, sda_oen remains 0 and SDA stays driven low; it must not release SDA high before SCL is actually high. This is the contrasting, otherwise side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: Assert that throughout the interval with scl_oen=1, filtered SCL low, and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 0. Then release the external SCL hold and verify that after filtered SCL becomes high, sda_oen changes to 1 before cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the bus initially released high, issue cmd=STOP while the FSM is idle. Allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL, observe filtered SCL high, and then release SDA high; do not assert either reset input.
elements.expected_response: When the STOP sequence completes and the final SDA release phase is reached, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock. This is the holding side of the specified shows behavior: cmd_ack pulses high at STOP completion.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, check in_stop_sequence and in_idle probes and compare cmd_ack against a reference STOP-sequence model. Require exactly one cmd_ack high cycle immediately following completion, followed by cmd_ack low on subsequent cycles.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, issue cmd=STOP while the FSM is idle, let the sequence begin, then assert nReset=0 asynchronously before filtered SCL is high for the final SDA release phase; subsequently deassert nReset and do not issue another command.
elements.expected_response: The STOP condition does not complete, the reset returns the FSM to idle, and cmd_ack does not pulse in the STOP-completion window. This is the non-holding side of the specified shows behavior: otherwise cmd_ack does not pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor the final STOP release condition using filtered SCL/SDA and in_stop_sequence/in_idle probes. Assert that no cmd_ack high pulse occurs from reset assertion through the aborted STOP completion window, and that reset initialization is observed after nReset is asserted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) on an enabled clk_en tick with SCL initially released/high. Model the slave releasing or driving SDA as needed, and allow the READ sequence to enter its data-bit window while the controller has released SCL; keep inputs stable until before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the READ data-bit window, sda_oen is high, which releases SDA so the external slave can drive the data bit; it remains released until the READ sequence advances toward completion and produces cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while in_read_sequence is active, filtered SCL is released/high for the READ data-bit window, and before cmd_ack, sample sda_oen and require it to be 1. Correlate the checked interval with the READ phase and verify no low-drive interval occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) with din=0 on an enabled clk_en tick. Let the controller enter the WRITE data-bit phase with SCL released/high and observe the corresponding data window before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: The READ-release condition does not apply in this contrasting non-READ case: during the WRITE data-bit window, sda_oen is low, driving SDA low rather than releasing it. This is the otherwise side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: At settled posedges while in_write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase are active with din=0, sample sda_oen and require it to be 0; confirm the command is WRITE rather than READ and that the low interval is confined to the write data phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, provide a released-high SCL bus, issue cmd=1000 (READ) on an enabled timing tick, and keep the external SDA value stable while the READ window is active.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: once the READ read window begins, scl_oen remains 1 for every registered cycle of the window; it does not pull SCL low while the read window is active.
elements.check_method: Use the in_read_sequence and filtered_scl_high probes to delimit the read window, then assert on each posedge that scl_oen is 1 until the read phase ends.

elements.stimulus: Continue the same ena=1 READ transaction with clk_cnt=1 and released-high SCL until the filtered read-window completion/rising-edge processing occurs, then allow the FSM to proceed to its following low phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: after the READ window ends, scl_oen transitions from 1 to 0 on the registered output update, pulling SCL low; it must not remain released high after the FSM leaves the read window.
elements.check_method: Detect the end of the read window using in_read_sequence and filtered_scl_rising, then compare consecutive settled posedge samples of scl_oen: require 1 during the final window sample followed by 0 in the subsequent low-phase sample.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a READ command with clk_cnt=0. Drive the external bus so the filtered SDA value is 1 before and during a filtered SCL rising edge in the READ window; ensure dout was previously 0.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: when the filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout updates to 1, the current filtered SDA value, on the corresponding registered output update. Otherwise side is rejected: dout remaining 0 at that edge is a failure.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered_scl_rising probe to identify the qualifying edge and sample dout after the following posedge/nonblocking-update region; compare dout against the filtered_sda_high probe and assert dout==1.

elements.stimulus: Complete a READ capture with dout=1 from the prior bit, then arrange the external bus so filtered SDA is 0 before and during the next filtered SCL rising edge in the READ window, with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows for the complementary data value: on the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 0, the current filtered SDA value. Contrasting otherwise side is rejected: dout retaining the prior value 1 instead of changing to 0 is a failure.
elements.check_method: Trigger the check on filtered_scl_rising, sample dout after the registered update, compare it with filtered_sda_low, and assert dout==0 for this edge.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, then drive ena=1 and issue cmd=READ while the bus is released high. Provide a stable external SDA value, allow the READ window to reach a filtered SCL rising edge, then allow the following low phase to complete using a nonzero clk_cnt. Observe the clock edge at which the READ bit cycle completes.
elements.expected_response: At the READ bit-cycle completion edge, the FSM is in idle and cmd_ack asserts as a one-clock command-complete pulse. This is the holding side of the observed behavior: cmd_ack asserts when the READ bit cycle completes.
elements.check_method: Use the in_read_sequence and in_idle probes to identify the terminal transition, sample cmd_ack after the posedge and settled nonblocking updates, and compare it against a reference model of the filtered SCL rising edge, low phase, and command-terminal timing. Verify cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock and then returns low.

elements.stimulus: Start a READ command with ena=1 and a released bus, enter the READ window, then assert nReset=0 before the filtered SCL rising-edge sample and terminal low phase complete. Release nReset without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: The READ bit cycle does not complete, so cmd_ack must not assert for that aborted READ. This is the contrasting side of the observed behavior: otherwise, cmd_ack is not asserted at the READ bit-cycle completion edge.
elements.check_method: Monitor the READ and idle probes and sample cmd_ack immediately after asynchronous reset assertion and on subsequent clock edges. Confirm reset returns the FSM to idle and that no command-complete pulse is produced for the interrupted READ.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=0, and issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) on a clock edge while the bus is released high. Keep din=0 through the WRITE bit's SDA setup and drive phase, and allow the command to proceed until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE bit's SDA setup and drive phase, before the corresponding SCL-high phase, sda_oen is 0. This is the din=0 side of the requirement: SDA is driven low using active-low open-drain semantics.
elements.check_method: At every enabled WRITE setup/drive phase, sample sda_oen after the posedge update and compare it against the reference mapping sda_oen == 0 for din=0; also confirm the phase is before SCL is released high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=1, and issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) on a clock edge while the bus is released high. Keep din=1 through the WRITE bit's SDA setup and drive phase, externally release SDA high, and allow the command to proceed until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE bit's SDA setup and drive phase, before the corresponding SCL-high phase, sda_oen is 1. This is the din=1 contrasting side of the requirement: SDA is released high rather than driven low.
elements.check_method: At every enabled WRITE setup/drive phase, sample sda_oen after the posedge update and compare it against the reference mapping sda_oen == 1 for din=1; also confirm the phase is before SCL is released high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, and keep the bus externally released high. While the command FSM is idle, issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=0 for the enabled command-acceptance tick, then drive cmd=0000 and keep din=0 until the WRITE completes.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit output phase, the holding side of the observed behavior applies: sda_oen is 0, so SDA is driven low for din=0. The WRITE may then complete with cmd_ack asserted once, provided no reset or arbitration loss is injected.
elements.check_method: At every cycle with in_write_sequence asserted and during the data-bit output phase, compare sda_oen against din using an assertion requiring sda_oen==0 when din==0; also verify the resolved SDA line is low and record the expected WRITE completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, and keep the bus externally released high. While the command FSM is idle, issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=1 for the enabled command-acceptance tick, then drive cmd=0000 and keep din=1 until the WRITE completes.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit output phase, the contrasting side of the observed behavior applies: sda_oen is 1, so SDA is released high for din=1. With the external bus high, the WRITE must complete without arbitration loss and produce one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: At every cycle with in_write_sequence asserted and during the data-bit output phase, compare sda_oen against din using an assertion requiring sda_oen==1 when din==1; also verify the resolved SDA line remains high, al stays low, and exactly one completion pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, present cmd=WRITE (0100) until it is accepted on an enabled timing tick, drive din=1, and model an idle bus with external SDA and SCL released high. Do not stretch SCL or interfere with SDA during the WRITE operation.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed behavior: during the WRITE stable-high phase, scl_oen is high, releasing SCL while SDA arbitration checking is active; on the subsequent phase transition scl_oen becomes low to pull SCL low; the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack becomes high for exactly one clock at the end of the sequence.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen and cmd_ack after settled posedges. Using the WRITE-sequence and write_stable_high_phase probes, assert temporal ordering of scl_oen=1 during the stable high phase followed by scl_oen=0, then verify exactly one cmd_ack pulse and idle entry with no al assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, present cmd=WRITE (0100) until acceptance on an enabled timing tick, drive din=1, and keep SCL externally released high. When the controller enters the WRITE stable-high phase with scl_oen high, externally force SDA low to cause arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case of the observed behavior: the required WRITE completion sequence is aborted, so scl_oen does not show the required release-then-pull-low progression and cmd_ack does not pulse. The controller instead releases the bus and terminates the active command without acknowledgement.
elements.check_method: At the write_stable_high_phase probe, inject filtered SDA low and monitor scl_oen and cmd_ack after each settled posedge. Assert that no post-release scl_oen low phase completing the WRITE occurs and that cmd_ack remains low for the aborted command; confirm the arbitration-loss abort and bus release.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Issue cmd=START from idle and run until the START sequence reaches its SDA-low, SCL-high phase.
elements.expected_response: During the active START phase, scl_o=0 and sda_o=0. SCL is released with scl_oen=1, while SDA is actively pulled low with sda_oen=0; this is the active pull-down side of the open-drain behavior.
elements.check_method: At every posedge while in_start_sequence is asserted, compare scl_o and sda_o to 0 and check the expected enable polarity against the phase probe and bus line state.

elements.stimulus: Continue the accepted START command from its initial phase with ena=1 and scl_i=sda_i=1 until the sequence reaches a phase in which both I2C lines are released, then complete the command.
elements.expected_response: While the START sequence requires released lines, scl_o=0 and sda_o=0 remain constant, while scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1. This is the released side of the open-drain behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample outputs after each posedge during in_start_sequence and compare the constant drive outputs and both output-enable values with the reference phase model.

elements.stimulus: Establish a busy transaction, then issue cmd=STOP with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and a high external bus. Run until the STOP sequence reaches its SDA-low phase while SCL is low or being held low.
elements.expected_response: During the active STOP pull-down phase, scl_o=0 and sda_o=0. Any actively driven-low line has its corresponding enable at 0; for example, SDA has sda_oen=0, demonstrating the active pull-down side.
elements.check_method: Use in_stop_sequence and the expected STOP phase to check after every posedge that constant-low drive outputs are maintained and the active line's enable is 0.

elements.stimulus: Continue the STOP command with ena=1 and external scl_i=sda_i=1 until SCL is released and then until SDA is released in the STOP high phase; allow cmd_ack to complete.
elements.expected_response: Whenever SCL or SDA is released during STOP, its output enable is 1, while scl_o=0 and sda_o=0 remain constant. The released line must not be actively pulled low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge in_stop_sequence, compare scl_oen and sda_oen with the STOP reference model at every release transition and verify both drive outputs stay 0.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=WRITE with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=0, and external scl_i=sda_i=1. Run through the WRITE bit's low phase and complete the command.
elements.expected_response: When WRITE drives SDA low for din=0, sda_oen=0 and the SCL phase enable reflects whether SCL is driven or released. Throughout the command, scl_o=0 and sda_o=0; 0 is used for every actively pulled-low line.
elements.check_method: During in_write_sequence, use write_stable_high_phase and the phase model to check enable polarity on every posedge, including the din=0 driven-low phase, and continuously check both drive outputs are 0.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=WRITE with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=1, and external scl_i=sda_i=1. Run until the WRITE sequence reaches its released SCL high phase, then complete the command.
elements.expected_response: During the released high phase, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 for din=1; neither line is actively pulled low. The constant drive outputs remain scl_o=0 and sda_o=0. This is the release side contrasting with the active-low case.
elements.check_method: While in_write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase are asserted, sample after each posedge and compare both enables and both constant drive outputs with the reference model.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=READ with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, external scl_i=sda_i=1, and return a valid SDA value from the external device during the read window. Run through the SCL-low phase and completion.
elements.expected_response: During the READ window SDA is released with sda_oen=1 and SCL is released with scl_oen=1; both lines are therefore not actively pulled low. scl_o=0 and sda_o=0 remain constant.
elements.check_method: While in_read_sequence is asserted, check after each posedge that the read-window enables are 1 and that both drive outputs are 0; separately verify dout capture at filtered_scl_rising.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=READ with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then advance through the READ sequence to its SCL-low phase after the filtered SCL rising edge; keep the external bus otherwise high and complete the command.
elements.expected_response: In the READ SCL-low phase, scl_oen=0, showing active pull-down, while SDA remains released with sda_oen=1. The drive outputs scl_o and sda_o remain 0 throughout. This contrasts the active SCL state with the released READ-window state.
elements.check_method: Use in_read_sequence and filtered_scl_rising to identify the phase transition, then compare scl_oen=0, sda_oen=1, scl_o=0, and sda_o=0 after each relevant posedge.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low between clock edges, release it, then apply synchronous rst high for one rising edge and deassert it. Keep ena high with cmd=NOP and observe the outputs through several idle clocks.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the observed behavior: scl_o and sda_o remain continuously 0 during asynchronous reset, synchronous reset, and idle operation. After reset, scl_oen and sda_oen are 1, selecting released SCL and SDA lines.
elements.check_method: At asynchronous-reset observation and after each subsequent posedge, compare scl_o and sda_o against constant 0 and compare reset/idle scl_oen and sda_oen against 1 using a cycle-by-cycle scoreboard.

elements.stimulus: With nReset released, rst deasserted, ena high, clk_cnt=0, and an externally released-high bus, issue START. After its acknowledgement, issue WRITE with din=0, allowing the normal SCL/SDA phases to complete, then issue STOP.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting ownership side of the observed behavior: scl_o and sda_o remain 0 in every phase, while scl_oen or sda_oen is 0 whenever the corresponding line is actively pulled low and is 1 whenever that line is released. The START, WRITE, and STOP sequences must therefore show both enable values with the active-low polarity, including SDA low during START/STOP phases, SCL low phases, and released-high phases.
elements.check_method: Use the command-phase probes and sampled bus ownership to build a reference trace. On every settled clock, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0; whenever a phase requires a driven-low or released line, compare scl_oen and sda_oen to the corresponding expected 0 or 1 value, accounting for the registered one-clock output latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, keep both external bus lines released high, issue cmd=START, and wait until the START sequence reaches its SDA-low phase with sda_oen=0 while scl_oen remains 1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for SDA: while sda_oen is low, the corresponding SDA line output sda_o is 0; sda_o remains the contractually constant low value.
elements.check_method: At the settled posedge where the SDA-low phase is entered, assert sda_oen==0 and sda_o==0, and record the SDA observation as the low-enable side of REQ-0147.

elements.stimulus: Using the same enabled START transaction, observe the initial START phase before SDA is pulled low, when sda_oen=1 and the external SDA line is released high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for SDA: when sda_oen is high, SDA is released, but the observed sda_o output remains 0 because sda_o is contractually constant low; this is the non-holding side of the observed-via behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample after the posedge producing the initial released-SDA phase and assert sda_oen==1 and sda_o==0; compare this observation with TP-0000's sda_o==0 at sda_oen==0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, keep both external bus lines released high, issue cmd=START, and wait until the START sequence reaches its SCL-low phase with scl_oen=0.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for SCL: while scl_oen is low, the corresponding SCL line output scl_o is 0; scl_o remains the contractually constant low value.
elements.check_method: At the settled posedge where the SCL-low phase is entered, assert scl_oen==0 and scl_o==0, and record the SCL observation as the low-enable side of REQ-0147.

elements.stimulus: Using the same enabled START transaction, observe the initial START phase before SCL is pulled low, when scl_oen=1 and the external SCL line is released high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for SCL: when scl_oen is high, SCL is released, but the observed scl_o output remains 0 because scl_o is contractually constant low; this is the non-holding side of the observed-via behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample after the posedge producing the initial released-SCL phase and assert scl_oen==1 and scl_o==0; compare this observation with TP-0002's scl_o==0 at scl_oen==0.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena high, and both external bus lines otherwise released high, issue a START command and sample the START phase in which scl_oen is high. Keep the external SCL participant released.
elements.expected_response: The SCL line is high because scl_oen is 1 and the external pull-up is unopposed. This is the holding case in observed_via.shows: scl_oen is 1, so SCL is released and the external pull-up brings SCL high.
elements.check_method: At the settled clock edge for the START release phase, compare scl_oen == 1 and the modeled wired-AND SCL line == 1; assert that no external device drives SCL low.

elements.stimulus: Continue the same START command until its following phase in which the controller drives SCL low, with no external participant driving SCL.
elements.expected_response: The SCL line is low because scl_oen is 0 and the controller actively drives it low rather than releasing it. This is the contrasting otherwise case in observed_via.shows.
elements.check_method: At the settled clock edge for the driven-low phase, compare scl_oen == 0 and the modeled wired-AND SCL line == 0.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena high, and both external bus lines otherwise released high, issue a START command and sample the initial START phase in which sda_oen is high. Keep the external SDA participant released.
elements.expected_response: The SDA line is high because sda_oen is 1 and the external pull-up is unopposed. This is the holding case in observed_via.shows: sda_oen is 1, so SDA is released and the external pull-up brings SDA high.
elements.check_method: At the settled clock edge for the initial START release phase, compare sda_oen == 1 and the modeled wired-AND SDA line == 1; assert that no external device drives SDA low.

elements.stimulus: Continue the same START command until its phase in which the controller pulls SDA low while SCL is high, with no external participant driving SDA.
elements.expected_response: The SDA line is low because sda_oen is 0 and the controller actively drives it low rather than releasing it. This is the contrasting otherwise case in observed_via.shows.
elements.check_method: At the settled clock edge for the driven-low phase, compare sda_oen == 0 and the modeled wired-AND SDA line == 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive cmd=START while the FSM is idle; provide a released-high bus and allow the START sequence to run to its terminal phase using clk_cnt=1.
elements.expected_response: At completion of the START sequence, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle, with cmd_ack low during the preceding active phases and on the following cycle. This is the holding side of the observed shows behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked assertion keyed to START-sequence completion: cmd_ack must be high on exactly one sampled posedge and low on the immediately preceding and following sampled posedges; count no additional pulses before the next command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive cmd=START while idle; provide a released-high bus and sample every clk from command acceptance through completion and for at least one cycle afterward.
elements.expected_response: cmd_ack remains low throughout all nonterminal START phases and returns low immediately after its single completion pulse; it is absent whenever the sequence is not completing. This is the otherwise side of the observed shows behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare cmd_ack against a reference START phase model on every posedge: require zero during all modeled nonterminal phases, one only at the terminal completion indication, and zero on the next cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive cmd=STOP while idle; provide a bus that permits the STOP waveform, including SCL becoming high after release, and allow the STOP sequence to reach its terminal phase using clk_cnt=1.
elements.expected_response: At completion of the STOP sequence, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle, with cmd_ack low before completion and on the next cycle. This is the holding side of the observed shows behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference STOP phase completion event and assert that cmd_ack is high on exactly that one posedge only, with low values on the adjacent sampled cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive cmd=STOP while idle; provide a bus that permits STOP completion and monitor cmd_ack throughout the active STOP phases and after completion.
elements.expected_response: cmd_ack is absent during every nonterminal STOP phase and after the one-cycle completion indication; no early, extended, or repeated pulse occurs. This is the otherwise side of the observed shows behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare each sampled cmd_ack value with the reference STOP phase model, requiring low before the terminal phase, one high cycle at completion, and low thereafter.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive cmd=READ while idle; release SDA, provide a normal released-high SCL waveform with returned SDA data, and allow the READ sequence to complete using clk_cnt=1.
elements.expected_response: At the end of the READ sequence, after the read low phase, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle and is low on the preceding and following cycles. This is the holding side of the observed shows behavior.
elements.check_method: Detect the reference READ terminal phase and assert a single-cycle cmd_ack pulse aligned with it; verify adjacent-cycle low values and no second pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive cmd=READ while idle; provide normal SCL/SDA activity and monitor cmd_ack from acceptance through the read capture, low phase, completion, and one cycle afterward.
elements.expected_response: cmd_ack remains low during all nonterminal READ phases, including before the read low phase completion, and is low again after the single completion pulse. This is the otherwise side of the observed shows behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference READ sequence timeline to check cmd_ack on every posedge: low for nonterminal phases, high for exactly one terminal cycle, then low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive din=0 and cmd=WRITE while idle, and provide a normal bus that releases SCL high without arbitration loss; allow the WRITE sequence to complete using clk_cnt=1.
elements.expected_response: At the end of the WRITE sequence, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle, with cmd_ack low during the preceding phases and on the following cycle. This is the holding side of the observed shows behavior.
elements.check_method: Key an assertion to the reference WRITE terminal phase and require exactly one high cmd_ack sample there, with low samples immediately before and after.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive din=0 and cmd=WRITE while idle, provide a normal non-arbitrating bus, and monitor cmd_ack throughout the active WRITE sequence and after completion.
elements.expected_response: cmd_ack is absent during all nonterminal WRITE phases and after the one-cycle completion pulse; no early, multi-cycle, or repeated acknowledgement is produced. This is the otherwise side of the observed shows behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare cmd_ack on each posedge with the reference WRITE phase model, requiring low before terminal completion, one high cycle at completion, and low on all subsequent cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, drive a released-high bus, issue cmd=START on an enabled timing tick, and maintain the bus inputs so the START sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: At the START sequence completion boundary, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle, then returns low; this pulse is the completion indication that permits the next bit command to be issued.
elements.check_method: Use the in_start_sequence and in_idle probes to identify sequence entry and completion, sample cmd_ack after each posedge, assert exactly one high cycle at completion, assert low on the following cycle, and issue a subsequent valid command only after the pulse to confirm the completion boundary is usable.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a busy transaction context established, issue cmd=STOP on an enabled timing tick, provide a released-high SCL bus so the STOP sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: At the STOP sequence completion boundary, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle and is not held high on adjacent cycles; the pulse indicates that the STOP bit-level operation has completed and the next command may be issued.
elements.check_method: Track in_stop_sequence through its terminal phase, compare registered cmd_ack on consecutive posedges, require one and only one high cycle at completion, and verify cmd_ack is low before and after that cycle.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue cmd=READ on an enabled timing tick, release SDA, and provide external SCL high and low phases including a filtered SCL rising edge so the READ sequence completes normally.
elements.expected_response: After the READ sequence terminal low phase, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle, then deasserted; this pulse indicates completion and allows the next bit command to be issued.
elements.check_method: Use in_read_sequence and filtered_scl_rising probes to align the expected terminal phase, then check cmd_ack for a single registered pulse with no high cycle immediately before or after it.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, drive din=0, issue cmd=WRITE on an enabled timing tick, and provide normal released-high and driven-low SCL phases without arbitration interference until the WRITE sequence reaches completion.
elements.expected_response: At the WRITE sequence completion boundary, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle and then returns low; the pulse is the indication that the current bit-level WRITE operation has completed and the next command can be issued.
elements.check_method: Track in_write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase, identify the terminal phase from the reference timing model, and assert that cmd_ack has exactly one high registered cycle at that boundary and is low on all adjacent cycles.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, drive din=1, issue cmd=WRITE on an enabled timing tick, then hold external SDA low during the released high phase while SCL is high to force arbitration loss before the WRITE terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: The active WRITE sequence aborts on arbitration loss and returns idle with both output enables released; cmd_ack remains deasserted and no completion pulse is generated, which is the contrasting 'otherwise' side of the observed cmd_ack behavior.
elements.check_method: Use command_active, in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and al to confirm the abort occurs before normal completion; monitor cmd_ack from command acceptance through return to idle and require no high cycle, including a full-cycle low observation after the abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, din=1, and issue cmd=WRITE=4 while the external bus is released high. Allow the WRITE data setup phase to complete and keep the external SDA high while the DUT releases SCL (scl_oen=1) for the stable-high window, then allow the phase to proceed.
elements.expected_response: Holding case from the observation: during the released-SCL stable-high WRITE window, al remains low because filtered SDA is high and no arbitration loss is reported; the WRITE then proceeds to the SCL-low phase and eventually produces its normal completion.
elements.check_method: Monitor write_stable_high_phase, scl_oen, filtered_sda_high, and al after each posedge. Assert that al is low throughout the stable-high window and that no arbitration-loss abort occurs before the subsequent scl_oen=0 phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, din=1, and issue cmd=WRITE=4 while the external bus is initially released high. After the WRITE data setup phase causes the DUT to release SCL (scl_oen=1), drive the external SDA low and hold it low through the stable-high WRITE window while the DUT's SDA remains released (sda_oen=1).
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case from the observation: with filtered SDA low during the stable-high WRITE phase, al asserts, the active WRITE aborts without cmd_ack, and both scl_oen and sda_oen are released.
elements.check_method: Monitor write_stable_high_phase, scl_oen, sda_oen, filtered_sda_low, al, and cmd_ack after each posedge. Require al to transition high during the released stable-high window, require no cmd_ack for the aborted command, and verify both output enables are 1 after the abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=0100 (WRITE), din=1, and clk_cnt=0. Accept the command on an enabled timing tick, then model the open-drain bus with external SDA held low while the controller reaches the WRITE released-high stable arbitration-check phase; keep SCL responsive and do not assert either reset.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed difference: while the WRITE command remains active, scl_oen and sda_oen are released high and filtered SDA is low; at the applicable clock edge al asserts high, with no cmd_ack for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Use the write_stable_high_phase and command_active probes to identify the released-high arbitration window, verify filtered_sda_low and sda_oen=1, then compare the registered al output after the clock edge. Verify cmd_ack is not asserted for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=0100 (WRITE), din=1, and clk_cnt=0. Accept the command on an enabled timing tick, then leave the external SDA line released high while the controller reaches the WRITE released-high stable arbitration-check phase; keep SCL responsive, avoid any START/STOP or other arbitration-loss condition, and do not assert either reset.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of the observed difference: while the WRITE command remains active, scl_oen and sda_oen are released high and filtered SDA is high; al remains low throughout this arbitration window and the command proceeds without arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Use the write_stable_high_phase and command_active probes to identify the same arbitration window, verify filtered_sda_high and sda_oen=1, and sample al after each clock edge. Confirm al stays low and no unrelated arbitration-loss condition is present.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and the bus initially released, issue a READ command. During the READ sequence, drive the external SDA line high and provide a valid filtered SCL low-to-high transition.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout updates on the corresponding registered clock update to the filtered SDA value, 1.
elements.check_method: At each posedge, sample after registered outputs settle. When filtered_scl_rising is asserted, compare dout with the filtered SDA value at that edge and require dout=1.

elements.stimulus: Reset to establish a known dout, then with ena high issue a READ command while externally holding SCL low so filtered SCL remains low. Drive filtered SDA high and keep it high throughout the stalled READ interval without allowing a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout does not update to the filtered SDA value and remains at its previously registered value.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered_scl_rising and dout on every settled posedge throughout the stalled READ interval; require filtered_scl_rising to remain deasserted and require dout to remain unchanged despite filtered SDA being high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1 and ena=1 while the bus is released high. During the WRITE stable-high arbitration-check phase, externally hold SDA low so filtered SDA is low while the controller expects released SDA high.
elements.expected_response: Arbitration loss is asserted; on the registered output row handling the loss, the FSM is idle and both scl_oen and sda_oen are high. This is the holding case: SCL and SDA are released after arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Use command_active, in_write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and sda_check_active to identify the injected arbitration-loss condition. After the next registered update, sample al, in_idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen and require al=1, in_idle=1, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1; also require no cmd_ack pulse for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1 and ena=1 while SDA remains externally high throughout the released WRITE high phase, allowing the WRITE command to proceed without arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Arbitration is not lost: al remains 0 and the FSM continues the normal WRITE sequence until its command-complete acknowledgment. This is the contrasting side: because arbitration has not been lost, scl_oen and sda_oen are not required to become high as an arbitration-loss return-to-idle action; they follow the normal WRITE phase sequencing.
elements.check_method: Use in_write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase to identify the normal released-high phase, monitor al for the entire command, and verify the FSM does not transition to idle due to arbitration loss. Check that the normal WRITE sequence reaches a one-clock cmd_ack and compare scl_oen and sda_oen against phase-appropriate normal output-enable values rather than requiring both to be high.
